sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: What three facts appear on a Washington vehicle title, and where must you never store that document?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: DOL issues a Certificate of Ownership, called the title, for most vehicles, showing the registered and legal owners, the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) and any lender, and it should be kept somewhere safe but never in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Must every Washington vehicle be registered with DOL—and how can someone without a driver license register one?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Every vehicle must be registered with DOL, and you need a driver license to register one unless the law exempts you, in which case you file a Vehicle Registration Driver License Exemption form.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: How long do new Washington residents have to register their vehicles, and how fast should an out-of-state purchase be registered?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: New residents have thirty days to register their vehicles, while a vehicle bought in another state should be registered in Washington right away.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which two core ownership and identity items are required to register a vehicle in Washington?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: To register a vehicle you need its current title, or a replacement from the issuing state if it is lost, plus a Washington driver license for every registered owner.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What two steps must you take with the fresh registration slip issued each year when you renew your tabs?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: You receive a new registration each year when you renew your tabs, and you must sign it and keep it in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Does updating your driver license address automatically update your vehicle registration address—and where do you change it?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Updating the address on your driver license does not update your vehicle address, which you change separately online in License Express or at a vehicle licensing office.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Why must a Washington driver who moves complete two separate address updates with DOL?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Changing your driver license address leaves the vehicle address unchanged, so the two records must each be updated.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Where must Washington plates be mounted, in what condition, and what rule governs license-plate frames?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Plates must be displayed clean and readable on both the front and rear of a Washington-registered vehicle, and a plate frame is allowed only if it leaves the letters, numbers and tabs uncovered.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Which two immediate steps must you take when selling, trading, gifting, or disposing of a vehicle—and within how many days?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: When you sell, trade, gift or dispose of a vehicle you must file a Vehicle Report of Sale within five days and take your license plates off the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Does filing a Report of Sale transfer ownership—and how many days does the buyer have to transfer the signed title?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: A report of sale does not transfer ownership; the owner signs and dates the title for the buyer, who must bring it to a licensing office within fifteen days to avoid penalty fees.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Is a car dealership legally required to file your Report of Sale on a trade-in?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: A dealership may file the report of sale for you but is not required to, so filing it yourself protects you.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: After a private vehicle sale in Washington, how does the seller's filing deadline compare with the buyer's transfer deadline?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: After a sale the seller files the report of sale within five days, while the buyer has fifteen days to transfer ownership with the signed title.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What coverage must Washington motorists carry, and where must proof of that coverage stay?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Washington requires liability insurance and proof of it carried with you or kept in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What are Washington's three minimum dollar limits for single-person injury, multi-person injury, and property damage liability?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Required liability coverage is at least twenty-five thousand dollars for injury or death of one person, at least fifty thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more people in one collision, and at least ten thousand dollars for damage to other people's property in one collision.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: Across Washington's twenty-five, fifty, and ten-thousand-dollar liability minimums, which category carries the lowest dollar floor?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: The single-person injury minimum is twenty-five thousand dollars and the multi-person minimum is fifty thousand dollars, while property damage needs only ten thousand dollars.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: Why should you review the owner's manual and locate every control and gauge before driving a different vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Vehicles differ in size, engine, safety devices, technology and handling, so read the owner's manual for every vehicle you drive and learn its controls and gauges before driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Which three cockpit items should you adjust every time you climb into a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Each time you get in a vehicle, adjust the steering wheel, seat and mirrors for good visibility so you can reach the pedals and instruments easily.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: How far should your chest sit from the steering wheel, how should your elbows bend, and where belongs your headrest?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: Sit upright with your chest at least ten inches from the steering wheel to leave room for the airbag, hold the wheel with a gentle elbow bend, and set the headrest level with your ears to guard against whiplash.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Which crash injury does the ten-inch chest gap prevent, and which crash injury does an ear-level headrest prevent?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: The seat rule keeps your chest at least ten inches from the wheel for airbag space, while the headrest is set level with your ears for whiplash protection.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Who bears legal and safety responsibility for keeping a vehicle roadworthy and answering dashboard warning lights?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Keeping your vehicle safe to drive is your responsibility, so heed warning lights and follow the owner's manual for routine maintenance before a small problem grows.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What is Washington's minimum safe tire tread depth, and what happens when tires wear shallower?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Tire tread should never be less than two thirty-seconds of an inch, because worn tires slip and slide, especially on wet roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Where do you look up the exact recommended air pressure for your vehicle's tires?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Low tire pressure affects handling, and the correct pressure is listed on the Tire and Loading Information label on the driver's door edge or in the owner's manual.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Which four cleaning, fluid, winter-clearing, and mirror-hanging habits keep every window clear?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Keep glass clean inside and out, keep washer fluid full, clear all snow, ice and frost from every window before driving, and avoid hanging items or decals that block your view.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: Why does Washington state a single universal fraction for tire tread depth yet point you to a door label for tire pressure?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: The minimum tire tread depth is two thirty-seconds of an inch, while the correct tire pressure comes from the door-edge label or the owner's manual rather than a single fixed number.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: Do Vehicle Safety Technology and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems take over legal responsibility for driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Vehicle Safety Technology (VST) and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) support good driving habits but never replace them, and the driver stays fully responsible for the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Name three real-world situations where blind-spot or camera driver-assist systems can miss hazards or stop working?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Driver-assist systems have limits: a blind-spot alert may miss a car two lanes over that is also merging, sensors may not notice people walking, rolling or riding nearby, and dirty sensors or faded markings can stop them working.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: When is the lone time Washington's guide advises turning vehicle safety features off?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Keep safety features switched on unless weather is so severe that their alerts become a distraction.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: How do forward collision avoidance tools work alongside adaptive cruise control?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: Collision avoidance features such as automatic emergency braking, forward collision warning and lane departure warning detect obstacles and warn you, while adaptive cruise control holds a set speed but slows to keep a safe gap behind the vehicle ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Which distinct hazards do lane-keeping assist, blind-spot detection, and cross-traffic alert each watch for?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Lane keeping assistance steers or alerts when you drift from your lane, blind spot detection warns of a vehicle in the next lane, and cross traffic alert warns of traffic approaching from the side, for example when backing out of a parking space.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: What does automatic high-beam control handle, and how do pre-crash tensioners or post-collision brakes help?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Automatic high beam control adjusts headlight brightness for oncoming traffic, and collision mitigation systems such as pre-crash seat belt tensioning and post-collision braking reduce harm when a crash cannot be avoided.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: Why must you still look two lanes across before merging even when your mirror blind-spot light stays off?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: A blind-spot alert covers the next lane, not a car two lanes away that is also merging, so your own hazard awareness is still needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: Between which sunset and sunrise marks does Washington law mandate headlights—and when else does the guide recommend them?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Washington law requires headlights from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise, and the guide suggests also using them all the time, in the dark, and in rain, snow, fog or smoke.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: For which two lighting reasons do daytime running lights fail as a legal substitute for headlights?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Daytime running lights are dimmer than headlights and do not turn on your taillights, so they are not a substitute for headlights.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Even though daytime running lights glow automatically up front, what stays dark on your vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Daytime running lights switch on when the car starts, but they are dimmer than headlights and leave the taillights dark.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Where are high beams appropriate, and at what exact distances must you dim for oncoming versus followed vehicles?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: High beams may be used on open roads without streetlights, but dim them within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle and within three hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Between oncoming traffic and a vehicle you are following, which requires dimming high beams farther out—five hundred or three hundred feet?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Dim high beams at five hundred feet from an oncoming vehicle but at three hundred feet when following one, so oncoming traffic gets the longer distance.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: How should you alert a trailing driver before slowing or stopping somewhere unexpected?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: If you must slow or stop where the driver behind may not expect it, tap the brake pedal three or four times quickly to warn them.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: From at least how far behind your vehicle must your red brake lights be clearly visible?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Your red brake lights must be easy to see from a distance of one hundred feet, warning the driver behind you to slow and prepare to stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: How many feet ahead of a turn or lane change must you start signaling, even on an empty street—and what comes afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Always signal before changing direction, even with nobody around, start signaling one hundred feet before you move, and make sure the signal stops blinking after the turn.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Which two Washington rear-visibility and turn-communication rules share the exact one-hundred-foot figure?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: The one hundred-foot figure appears twice on this page, once for how far away brake lights must be visible and once for how early to signal before a turn or lane change.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Using your left arm out the window, which positions signal slow-or-stop, a left turn, and a right turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Hand signals use the left arm out the driver's window: pointing down means stop or slow, pointing straight out means a left turn, and bent upward with fingers to the sky means a right turn.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: What never changes across all three Washington driver hand signals?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: All three hand signals use the left arm out the window, and only the hand direction changes: down for stop, straight out for left, up for right.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Under which two trouble situations should you switch on your vehicle's flashing hazard lights?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Turn on the flashing hazard lights when the car malfunctions or you must make an emergency stop, so others can pass you safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Which four personal, legal, vehicle, and emotional traits define a good driver in the Washington guide?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: The guide lists four traits of a good driver: mindful of yourself and others, responsible for the rules of the road, familiar with how your vehicle works and takes up space, and patient and levelheaded.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Why should a learner practice safe habits — like over-the-shoulder blind-zone checks — with deliberate intent?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Practice with intent so that safe habits, such as looking over your shoulder to check blind zones, become automatic and free your attention for the changing road.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: How can a bad cold, a headache or tight shoulders, and mental stress each degrade your driving — and whom should you ask?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Driving demands physical and mental fitness: a bad cold can slow your thinking, a headache or tight shoulders can hurt your handling, and stress can weaken your decisions, so ask a doctor about any condition that worries you.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What self-check belongs before turning the key, and what should you do if you feel unwell yet must travel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Check in with yourself before you start the engine, and if you feel unwell but still need to travel, have someone else do the driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What screening must every applicant pass before Washington issues a driver license?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Washington law requires you to pass a vision test before you are issued a driver license.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: If your license carries a corrective-lens restriction, when must you wear them — and what lens type is barred after dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: If your license requires corrective lenses, wear them every time you drive, and do not use dark or tinted corrective lenses after dark.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: Keep the two corrective-lens rules straight — what must stay on every drive versus what stays off after sunset?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: Wearing required corrective lenses is a must on every drive, but dark or tinted corrective lenses are the ones to avoid at night.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What two crucial jobs do peripheral side vision and clear sharp sight perform while you look ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Peripheral vision lets you notice vehicles and trouble from the corner of your eye while still looking ahead, and clear sight also lets you judge how far away other vehicles, people and hazards are.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: If night driving challenges your eyes, when should you drive, and where do you look to beat oncoming headlight glare?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: If night driving is hard for you, drive at night only when needed, keep your headlights on, and escape oncoming glare by looking toward the right edge of the road and steering by it.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Which three night adjustments — to aim, speed, and gap — ensure you can stop within the pavement your headlights illuminate?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: At night, keep headlights properly aimed, slow down and leave more following distance, so that you can stop within the stretch of road your headlights light up.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Contrast how you beat blinding oncoming glare at night with how you keep stopping distance inside your beams?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: To handle oncoming glare you look to the right edge of the road, while to see farther you keep headlights aimed and slow down so you can stop inside their beam.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Which warning sounds alert drivers to trouble, how does hearing loss sneak up, and how do deaf drivers compensate?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Horns, sirens and screeching tires warn you of danger, hearing loss often creeps in slowly, and deaf or hard-of-hearing drivers can adapt by leaning more on their eyes and staying extra alert.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What does Washington law forbid regarding earbuds, headphones, or noise-canceling headsets — and what single-ear exception exists?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Driving while wearing earbuds, earphones, headphones or headsets that play sound or cancel noise is illegal, although a hands-free device in one ear is allowed if it meets WAC two hundred four-ten-forty-five.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: May a Washington instruction-permit or intermediate-license holder use a hands-free cell phone while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: A driver holding an instruction permit or an intermediate license may not use a cell phone or any mobile electronic device while driving, not even a hands-free one.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: Contrast the one-ear hands-free allowance for full-license drivers against the rule for permit and intermediate holders?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Most drivers may use a hands-free device in one ear, but a driver with an instruction permit or intermediate license may not use any mobile device at all while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: Beyond alcohol and drugs, what else counts under the guide's definition of impaired driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Impaired driving means anything, including alcohol, drugs or tiredness, that makes it hard to think clearly, react fast or control your car.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Which four financial, license, and freedom penalties hit DUI offenders — and does driving experience ever offset drinking?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Penalties for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs include costly fines, higher insurance rates, a suspended or withdrawn license and possible jail, and no amount of experience makes drinking and driving safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Which single impairing substance shows up most often in impaired-driving crashes, and how should you treat suspected impaired drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Alcohol is the impairing substance most often involved in impaired-driving crashes, so watch for drivers acting impaired and give them plenty of room.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: How does alcohol change alertness, eyesight, scanning speed, multitasking, and risk confidence behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Alcohol can make you drowsy, blur or narrow your vision, slow your reactions and scanning, make multitasking like lane keeping harder, and breed overconfidence that leads to risky moves.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Which four personal and group habits keep you and your friends out of impaired-driving crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Never drive after using an impairing substance, never ride with a driver who has used any amount, stop friends and family from driving impaired, and arrange a sober driver ahead of time.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: At what age is recreational cannabis legal in Washington — and at what age or amount is driving after cannabis legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Recreational cannabis in any form is legal for adults aged twenty-one or older, yet driving after using any cannabis is illegal at every age, and no amount of it is safe for driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Which five mental and physical driving skills degrade after using cannabis?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Cannabis can reduce attention and coordination, slow reactions, weaken car handling and distance judgment, and make you drowsier.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Why doesn't turning twenty-one let a Washington adult drive after consuming recreational cannabis?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Being twenty-one or older makes recreational cannabis legal to use, but it never makes driving after cannabis legal, because that ban applies at every age and to any amount.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Does buying a medicine legally at a pharmacy or store excuse driving impaired under Washington criminal law?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A drug being legal does not make it safe for driving, and impaired driving is a crime whether the drug was prescribed, bought over the counter or in a store, or is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How can everyday cold, allergy, or headache remedies and prescription medicines impair a driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Over-the-counter remedies for colds, allergies or headaches can make you drowsy, and prescription drugs, much like alcohol, can dull reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does Washington criminal law compare impairment from a doctor's prescription, an over-the-counter tablet, and an illegal drug?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Whether a drug is prescribed, bought over the counter or illegal changes nothing about impaired driving, which stays a criminal act in every case.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: When must you hold off driving with a medicine, and how should you read a 'heavy machinery' bottle warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.memory_hook: Test new doses, machinery means cars
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Do not drive after first starting a prescription, a new medicine or a higher dose until you know how it affects you, and treat any label warning about operating heavy machinery as a warning about driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Why shouldn't a commuter ignore a medicine warning about 'operating heavy machinery' just because they work at a desk?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: A heavy machinery warning on a medicine label covers driving a car too, not only factory or construction equipment.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: What can happen when a mild medicine mixes with a second medicine or alcohol, and whom should you check with?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: A medicine that seems harmless alone can cause severe impairment when combined with a second medicine or with alcohol, so read the warnings or ask a pharmacist first.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: What is polydrug use, how do mixed substances interact, and where does it rank among fatal-crash impairments?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Polydrug use, taking more than one kind of drug such as alcohol plus cannabis or medicines, can produce stronger effects than any one drug and is the most common impairment found in fatal crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: Connect what happens when substances combine in polydrug use to its rank in deadly crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Polydrug use is about combining substances, and the combination can hit harder than any single one, which makes it the leading impairment in fatal crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Which four triggers cause driver fatigue, and how does exhaustion compare with alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.memory_hook: Strain or sleep loss mimics alcohol
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: Fatigue comes from physical or mental strain, repetitive tasks, illness or lack of sleep, and like alcohol it impairs your vision and judgment and can put you to sleep at the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Which memory, eye, mood, and lane-keeping clues tell you to pull off the road and rest immediately?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Pull over and rest if you cannot recall the last few miles, blink often or have heavy eyelids, struggle to hold your head up, miss exits or signs, feel irritable, or drift, swerve, tailgate or hit rumble strips.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: Alongside heavy eyelids, which three vehicle-handling mistakes warn that fatigue has already set in?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Hitting rumble strips, drifting from the lane and tailgating are physical driving clues of fatigue, just like heavy eyelids, and each one means pull over and rest.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: How can two drivers manage trip fatigue — and what is the fix when driving solo and feeling drowsy?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Share the driving with another driver if you can, and if you are alone and getting tired, leave the road and take a twenty-minute nap rather than push on.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: How many hours of sleep do most people need before a road trip, and how often should you schedule rest stops?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Before a long trip, get enough sleep, since most people need seven to nine hours, and plan breaks roughly every one hundred miles or two hours.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: Separate when the twenty-minute nap applies from when the hundred-mile or two-hour break rule applies?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: The twenty-minute nap is the fix when you are already drowsy and alone, whereas stopping about every one hundred miles or two hours is the plan you make before a long trip.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: What subtle pedal habit can creep in without an anxious driver even realizing it?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Feelings change behavior behind the wheel: an anxious driver may press too hard on the accelerator without noticing.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Which breathing image and two counting exercises does the guide suggest to cool down while safely parked?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: To calm down while parked, breathe in through your nose and out as if cooling hot soup, or count slowly from one to twenty or back from one hundred by threes.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: How does Washington classify aggressive driving, what intent defines it, and which six risky behaviors accompany it?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Aggressive driving is a traffic offense, meaning a driver purposely endangers people or property, and it is linked with speeding, tailgating, unsafe lane changes, poor signaling, ignoring traffic controls and crowding walkers or cyclists.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: What core element separates aggressive driving from a simple mistake, and what offense category applies?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Aggressive driving is defined by intent, a driver purposely endangering people or property or forcing others to protect themselves, and it is classed as a traffic offense.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: Which three penalties hit illegal street racing or unauthorized street demonstrations — and who besides the driver faces them?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: Street racing and unauthorized street demonstrations carry severe penalties, including fines, jail and vehicle impound, for drivers and for anyone who instigates or helps.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: How does road rage escalate past aggressive driving into a criminal offense, and what everyday pressures feed it?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Road rage is a criminal offense: an angry reaction to a road event that turns into violence using a vehicle or another weapon, often fed by stress, tight schedules or traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: Why does Washington treat road rage as a crime rather than a traffic ticket — and can passengers commit it?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Road rage is classed as a criminal offense because the anger turns into violent behavior with a vehicle or another weapon, and it can involve a passenger as well as a driver.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Which five mental or driving warning signs reveal that you are slipping into road rage yourself?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Signs you may be in road rage include violent thoughts toward others, speeding up to beat a light, weaving, overusing the horn or high beams, and braking or slowing down to punish another driver.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: If an angry driver targets your car, what four de-escalation and destination steps protect you?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: If another driver targets you with road rage, move out of the way, skip honking or gestures, keep your eyes on the road, and drive to a busy place with open businesses, calling police if needed.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Where online can you look up Washington's current rules of the road, and how long does that duty last?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Traffic laws can change, the current rules of the road can be found by searching RCW forty-six point six one online, and staying informed is your job for as long as you drive.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which half of a Washington roadway do you travel on, and when may a driver briefly enter the left side?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Drive on the right side of the road, using the left side only briefly to pass safely and legally on a two-lane road.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: On a multilane highway, how are the right and left lanes used, and does passing lift the speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: On roads with several lanes going your way, keep right except to pass, use the left lane for passing slower traffic, and obey the speed limit even while passing.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: May you use a carpool lane for passing, and when is driving on the shoulder ever allowed?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Carpool lanes are not passing lanes, and you should not pass or drive on the shoulder unless officials or signs tell you to.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Between the general left lane, a carpool lane, and a highway shoulder, which one serves passing?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: The left lane is for passing slower traffic, but a carpool lane is never a passing lane and the shoulder is off limits unless officials or signs direct you there.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Why must you continue to the next exit instead of backing up if you overshoot a freeway ramp?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Never drive in reverse on the road even if you miss a turn or exit, because backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What does Washington law say about hitchhiking or stopping to pick up a hitchhiker along a freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Hitchhiking and picking up hitchhikers on Washington freeways are both illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Which three roadside categories make up traffic control devices, and whose job is obeying them?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Traffic control devices are the signals, signs and road markings that direct traffic, and you are responsible for spotting and obeying all of them.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Which three groups of people can direct traffic in special situations, and how do their orders rank against signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Police, construction and maintenance workers and school crossing guards may direct traffic in special situations, and their directions override the signals and must be obeyed.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: How must every approaching driver treat an intersection when the overhead traffic lights go dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: At a traffic signal that is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop: stop completely, yield to traffic on your right, and go carefully when safe.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Why is cruising nonstop through an unlit, broken traffic signal illegal in Washington?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: A dark or broken traffic signal is handled as a four-way stop with a full stop and yielding to the right, not as a signal you may drive through.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What does a solid red signal require, and when is turning right on red permitted?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: At a solid red light, stop and wait for green and a clear intersection, though after a full stop you may turn right if no sign forbids a turn on red and there is room to enter traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: Under what street layout and conditions does Washington allow a left turn at a red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: After a complete stop at a red light, you may also turn left onto a one-way street when no sign prohibits it and there is room to merge.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How does a flashing red signal compare with an illuminated red arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: A flashing red light works exactly like a stop sign, while a red arrow means you may not go in the arrow's direction.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How do your movement rules differ across a solid red ball, a flashing red ball, and a red arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: A solid red means stop and wait for green, a flashing red means stop and then go in turn like a stop sign, and a red arrow forbids only the arrow's direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: How should you respond approaching a solid yellow signal versus already being inside the intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: A solid yellow light warns that red is coming, so slow and prepare to stop, but if you are already in the intersection keep going at the posted speed, never speeding up to beat it.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Which roadside sign matches a flashing yellow traffic light in Washington, and how do you proceed?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means the same as a yield sign, so treat the intersection as uncontrolled and go only when you have the right-of-way.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How does a solid yellow signal's command differ from a flashing yellow signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: A solid yellow tells you to prepare to stop because red is next, whereas a flashing yellow tells you to yield and proceed when it is your right-of-way.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: If the signal turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, how should you manage your speed?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Being caught in the intersection on a yellow means continue at the posted speed, not accelerate past it to clear the light.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What transition does a yellow arrow warn about, and whom must you yield to?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: A yellow arrow warns that the arrow will soon turn red, so get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What conditions still constrain you even when your signal shows a solid green light?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: A solid green light means go once the intersection is clear, still yielding to pedestrians and to emergency vehicles as the law requires.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Who holds right-of-way when you want to turn left on a solid circular green light?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Turning left on a solid green, oncoming traffic has the right-of-way, so wait where you can see approaching cars and turn when there is a gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What priority and conflict protection does an illuminated green arrow provide?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A green arrow gives you the right-of-way in its direction, with no oncoming, crossing or pedestrian traffic expected while it shows.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How does turning left on a solid green circle contrast with turning left on a green arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: A solid green lets you turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic, while a green arrow gives you the right-of-way for that turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Are flashing green traffic lights used in Washington, and where nearby do they warn of pedestrians?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Washington does not use flashing green lights, though British Columbia uses them to warn that pedestrians are waiting to cross.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: How do you obey a red-and-green ramp meter when entering a Washington freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: A freeway ramp meter works like a normal signal: on red stop at the white stop line, and on green continue up the ramp.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: What message category belongs to red, orange, yellow, white, green, blue, and brown road signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Sign colors carry meaning: red for prohibited or restricted actions, orange for construction warnings, yellow for general warnings, white for regulations, green for guidance, blue for motorist services and brown for recreation and culture.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: Which three vulnerable road-user zones do fluorescent yellow-green signs highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn of school, pedestrian and bicycle activity.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How do orange, standard yellow, and fluorescent yellow-green warning signs split up hazards?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Orange warns of construction and maintenance, plain yellow warns of general road conditions, and fluorescent yellow-green warns of school, pedestrian and bicycle activity.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: What distinguishes white, green, blue, and brown signs along Washington highways?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: White marks a regulatory sign, green gives directions, blue points to motorist services and brown marks recreation or cultural areas.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Where do you halt at a stop sign, and how does a yield sign adjust your approach?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop at the line, crosswalk or corner, check all directions for vehicles and pedestrians, and yield the right-of-way, while a yield sign means slow down and let traffic with the right-of-way go first.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: What mandatory action separates every stop sign from a yield sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: A stop sign always requires a full stop, whereas a yield sign requires slowing down and letting traffic that has the right-of-way cross first.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: Why can an officer ticket you for driving too fast even when your speedometer reads below the posted limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: A posted maximum speed applies to ideal conditions, so you can be ticketed for going too fast for slippery or foggy conditions even below the limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What does a posted minimum speed limit sign require, and why does it exist?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Some roads post a minimum speed limit, and you must drive at least that fast so you do not endanger other drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How do posted maximum and minimum speed limits frame safe highway travel?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: A maximum speed limit is a ceiling for ideal conditions, while a minimum speed limit is a floor you must reach so you are not a hazard.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: Which three violations do Washington's marked automated safety cameras capture, and who receives the ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Automated traffic safety cameras record drivers who fail to stop for a steady red light or a railroad crossing signal or who speed in a school zone, their locations are clearly marked, and tickets are mailed to the vehicle owner.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: How do yellow speed warning plaques differ from overhead digital variable speed limit signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Speed warning signs recommend a slower speed for a hazard such as a curve, and digital variable speed limit signs change posted limits and can close lanes ahead of slow traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: What universal rule does a red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol communicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: A red circle with a red slash over a symbol forbids that action, such as a left turn, right turn or U-turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: What does a Do Not Enter sign look like, and what urgent action does a Wrong Way sign demand?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign is square with a white horizontal bar inside a circle, and a Wrong Way sign means you are headed against traffic and must stop and turn around at once.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: How do Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs split up preventing head-on entries?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Do Not Enter warns you before you turn into a street from the wrong direction, while Wrong Way tells you that you are already traveling against traffic and must turn around.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: Who may enter a shared center left-turn lane, and which two uses are strictly banned there?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: A shared center left-turn lane is reserved for drivers turning left from either direction and may not be used for through travel or passing.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: Whom must every driver yield to inside a Washington highway work zone, and what happens to fines when crews are present?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: In a highway work zone everyone must yield to workers, equipment and vehicles with flashing yellow lights, and fines double for offenses there when workers are present.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: Which roadside stops and amenities do blue motorist service signs point toward?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Service signs point to services such as hospitals, electric vehicle charging stations and rest areas.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What information do green destination boards provide, and what do route shield shapes and colors reveal?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Destination signs give directions and distances to places such as cities and airports, and the shape and color of a route number sign tell you whether it is an interstate, U.S., state, city or county road.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Does the driver guide illustrate every road sign in Washington, and what is your legal responsibility?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: The guide shows only some Washington signs, yet drivers are responsible for knowing every sign, including city and county ones.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: What traffic flow setup does an added-lane warning sign announce for vehicles joining on the right?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: An added lane sign marks a lane that joins from the right where no merging is required.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Besides roadside flares or warning signs, how do response vehicles mark an active emergency zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Emergency zones may use flares or signs, but roadside response vehicles mark them with flashing lights.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: What two options satisfy Washington law when you approach a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.memory_hook: Change lanes or drop ten under
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: When you see a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights you must either move into a lane farther away or slow to at least ten miles per hour under the posted limit.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What is the absolute maximum speed allowed through an emergency zone in Washington?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.memory_hook: Never exceed fifty in emergency zones
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: You must never go faster than fifty miles per hour in an emergency zone.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Beyond police cars, fire engines, and ambulances, which five working rigs count as roadside response vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Roadside response vehicles include tow trucks, garbage trucks, incident response, highway maintenance and utility vehicles as well as police, fire trucks and ambulances.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Passing a flashing roadside response vehicle, must you both change lanes and slow ten under, or choose one?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.memory_hook: Move over or drop ten under
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Near a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights, moving over and slowing to at least ten miles per hour under the limit are alternatives, and you must do one of them.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does the ten-under speed drop interact with the fifty-mile-per-hour ceiling inside an emergency zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.memory_hook: At least ten under, max fifty
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: In an emergency zone, slowing to ten miles per hour under the posted limit is a minimum drop, and fifty miles per hour is an absolute ceiling no matter how high the posted limit is.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Who bears responsibility for parking only in safe designated spots, and what curbside clue warns of limits?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: You are responsible for parking only in designated areas so your vehicle is not a hazard, and colored curbs can signal parking limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Which four pedestrian, cyclist, or traffic spaces forbid parking at all times?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Never park in an intersection or on a crosswalk, a sidewalk or a bicycle lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Within how many feet of a traffic light, stop sign, or yield sign is parking prohibited?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.memory_hook: Stay thirty feet from control signs
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Do not park within thirty feet of a traffic signal, a stop sign or a yield sign.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: How many feet of clearance must you leave when parking near a driveway, alley, or private road?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Do not park within five feet of a driveway, an alley or a private road.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What parking clearance applies across the street from a fire station's driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Do not park within seventy-five feet of a fire station driveway when parking on the opposite side of the street.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: How do Washington's no-parking distances compare across driveways, traffic signs, and opposite-side fire stations?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.memory_hook: Five driveway, thirty sign, seventy-five fire
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: The thirty-foot gap applies to traffic signals, stop signs and yield signs, the five-foot gap to driveways, alleys and private roads, and the seventy-five-foot gap to a fire station driveway across the street.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Within how many feet of a pedestrian safety zone is parking illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Do not park within twenty feet of a pedestrian safety zone.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Where is parking banned on railroad tracks and around a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.memory_hook: Off tracks, fifty feet from crossing
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Never park on railroad tracks or within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: How many feet of open curb must you leave on each side of a fire hydrant?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Do not park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Which hazards match Washington's fifteen-foot, twenty-foot, and fifty-foot no-parking buffers?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.memory_hook: Fifteen hydrant, twenty zone, fifty rail
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Fire hydrants need a fifteen-foot gap, pedestrian safety zones a twenty-foot gap and railroad crossings a fifty-foot gap, while the tracks themselves allow no parking at all.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Which direction must a parked car face, and what is the maximum legal distance from the curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: A parked vehicle must face the same way as traffic and sit no more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What rules cover double-parking and parking in work zones, on bridges or tunnels, or along freeway shoulders?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.memory_hook: All banned; freeway shoulder emergency only
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Parking is banned beside an already parked vehicle, in a construction zone, on a bridge, overpass, tunnel or underpass, and on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: What parking rules do white painted curbs signal compared with yellow or red painted curbs?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: A white painted curb allows only short stops, while a yellow or red curb marks a loading zone or another restriction.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How do the twelve-inch curb-distance rule and painted curb colors apply together when parking?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.memory_hook: Within twelve inches, obey curb paint
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: The twelve-inch limit is a maximum distance from the curb, and white curbs allow brief stops while yellow or red curbs mean loading or other limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: How often should you engage the parking brake, and where does it matter most?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Set the parking brake every time you park, and especially on a hill.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: How do you perform the Dutch Reach when exiting a parked car, and whom does it protect?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.memory_hook: Mirrors first, open with far hand
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: The Dutch Reach means checking your mirrors, then opening the door with the hand farthest from it, which turns your body so you see approaching cyclists.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Under what age is it a crime to leave a child unattended in a parked car with the engine running?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Leaving a child younger than sixteen alone in a parked vehicle with the motor running is a crime.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Even with the engine shut off, under what age is leaving a child alone in a parked car a crime?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Leaving a child younger than twelve alone in a parked vehicle is a crime even with the motor off.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How does Washington's under-sixteen unattended-child law differ from its under-twelve unattended-child law?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.memory_hook: Under sixteen running, under twelve anytime
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: The under-sixteen rule covers a child left in a parked vehicle with the engine running, while the under-twelve rule covers a child left alone in any parked vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Under what four cabin conditions does leaving an animal alone inside a vehicle become a crime?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.memory_hook: Heat, cold, bad air, no water
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Leaving an animal alone in a vehicle is a crime when heat, cold, poor ventilation or lack of water could injure or kill it.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: If an unattended child or endangered animal is locked inside and nobody nearby can open up, what authority do police have?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.memory_hook: Enter reasonably with zero damage liability
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: If nobody nearby can open the vehicle, police may remove a child or animal by any reasonable means, and the officer or agency is not liable for the damage.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: What step-by-step sequence puts your car cleanly into an angled or perpendicular parking space?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: To pull into a perpendicular or angled space, check traffic, signal, creep forward while steering to the middle of the space, center between the lines, then stop and secure the vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: When backing out of a perpendicular or angled stall, how far straight back should you reverse before turning the wheel?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.memory_hook: Clear neighbor's bumper, then turn sharply
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: To leave a perpendicular or angled space, back straight out while watching traffic until your bumper clears the next vehicle, then turn the wheel sharply the way you want to go.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: As you start backing into a parallel space, what alignment cue tells you to turn the wheel sharply into the spot?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.memory_hook: Align front bumper with rear bumper
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: To parallel park, back slowly until your front bumper lines up with the rear bumper of the car you are parking behind, then turn the wheel sharply and back in.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: How do you complete a parallel-parking maneuver after angling back toward the rear vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.memory_hook: Stop short, pull forward within twelve
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Stop before you touch the bumper of the vehicle behind you, then pull forward so you end up no more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Which two reference points anchor the start and the final parked position of parallel parking?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.memory_hook: Match bumpers first, finish within twelve
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Entering a parallel space starts by backing until bumpers line up with the car you park behind, and it ends no more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: When pulling out of a parallel space, what clearance landmark tells you it is safe to merge into the travel lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.memory_hook: Signal, ease out past rear bumper
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: When leaving a parallel space, signal, steer forward slowly, and move into the nearest lane once your front door passes the rear bumper of the car ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: Parked facing uphill next to a tall curb, which way do you turn your wheels and how does the tire sit?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.memory_hook: Turn away; tire back touches curb
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: Facing uphill against a tall curb, turn the wheel away from the curb until the back of the front tire rests against it, so a rolling car stops at the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: Why can turning your front wheels toward the curb be safer when parked uphill beside a low or rounded curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.memory_hook: Low curb: turn toward, roll off-road
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Facing uphill with a low or rounded curb, turning the wheel toward the curb may be safer, because the car would then roll away from the road.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How does uphill wheel direction in Washington change between a tall curb and a low rounded curb?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.memory_hook: Tall turns away, low turns toward
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Uphill against a tall curb you turn the wheel away so the tire's back edge catches the curb, but with a low or rounded uphill curb turning toward it may be safer.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: Parked facing downhill alongside a curb, which way do your front wheels point?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.memory_hook: Downhill turns front tire into curb
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Facing downhill, turn the wheel toward the curb until the front of the front tire touches it.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: When parking on any hill that has no curb at all, which direction do you turn your wheels?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.memory_hook: No curb turns toward road edge
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: On a hill with no curb, turn the wheels toward the road edge so the car rolls away from traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: What steering direction do downhill curb parking and no-curb hill parking have in common?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.memory_hook: Both turn toward edge or curb
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Downhill the wheel turns toward the curb so the front of the tire meets it, and with no curb the wheels turn toward the road edge, away from traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: What rule governs the striped access aisle next to a disabled parking stall?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.memory_hook: Keep striped access aisle completely clear
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: The striped access aisle beside a disabled parking space must stay clear, and you can be fined for blocking it or parking there without the required placard.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: Who qualifies to apply for temporary or permanent disabled parking privileges, and who completes the form with them?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: A person whose disability limits or impairs walking may apply for temporary or permanent disabled parking by completing the application together with their physician.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: Under what condition is parking in an electric vehicle charging stall legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.memory_hook: Legal only while actively plugged in
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Parking at an electric vehicle charging station is illegal unless your vehicle is plugged into the charger.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: Whose rules on weight, hitches, brakes, and licensing apply when towing a boat, camper, or trailer?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.memory_hook: Follow manufacturer, state, and federal rules
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: When towing a boat, trailer or camper you must follow manufacturer, state and federal rules on weight, hookups, brakes and licensing.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: What is Washington's law on unsecured cargo, and how must small and large items be fastened?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.memory_hook: Unsecured loads illegal; strap cargo tight
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Driving with an unsecured load is illegal, so tie items down with rope, netting or straps and fasten large objects directly to the vehicle or trailer.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: When is carrying a dog or other animal outside the cab—such as in a pickup bed—legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.memory_hook: Only inside protective harness or crate
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Carrying an animal outside the cab, such as in a truck bed, is illegal unless it is in a protective harness or enclosure.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: What criminal offense applies when an animal is transported in a dangerous manner?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: Transporting an animal in a way that endangers it or the public is a misdemeanor under the state's animal cruelty laws.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: How does Washington's pickup-bed pet restraint rule pair with its dangerous-transport cruelty statute?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.memory_hook: Bed requires restraint; endangerment brings misdemeanor
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: An animal in a truck bed is legal only with a protective harness or enclosure, while transporting any animal in a risky way is a separate misdemeanor offense.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: Why does Washington treat driving with a loose pet—or a pet on your lap—as a legal problem?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.memory_hook: Loose lap pets cause illegal distraction
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: A loose pet or one on the driver's lap is a distraction, and any activity that pulls focus from safe driving is illegal.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: Why do standard Washington traffic laws apply aboard Washington State Ferries?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: Washington State Ferries are part of the state highway network, so every rule of the road applies there.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: What penalty applies to cutting into a ferry queue, and what must waiting drivers keep clear?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.memory_hook: Line-cutting draws fines; keep driveways clear
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: Cutting into a ferry line is a traffic offense that can bring a fine, and a holding lane must not block home driveways or intersections.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: In which two Washington counties is ocean-beach driving legal, and what legal status does the sand hold there?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.memory_hook: Grays Harbor and Pacific state highways
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: Ocean beach driving is allowed only in Grays Harbor and Pacific counties, where the beach counts as a state highway.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: What is the speed limit on legal Washington driving beaches, and who always holds right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: On the beach the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour, and walkers and cyclists always have the right-of-way.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Which county limit, speed cap, and right-of-way rule govern driving on Washington ocean beaches?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Beach driving is limited to two counties with a twenty-five miles per hour limit, and walkers and cyclists keep the right-of-way there at all times.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What four qualities define managing risk behind the wheel, and how should safe habits develop?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Managing risk means driving aware, predictable, smooth and skilled, and building safe habits on purpose until they become your normal style.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Which five recurring factors show up most often in fatal motor-vehicle crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: The common factors in fatal crashes are speed, impairment, distraction, unbelted occupants and inexperience.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: For which exact Washington age bracket are vehicle crashes among the leading causes of death and serious injury?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: In Washington, vehicle crashes are among the leading causes of death for people aged sixteen to twenty-five, a group more prone to fatal and serious injury crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: What does risk awareness mean in Washington driving, and what types of hazards does it include?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Risk awareness is the ability to spot present and possible hazards, including other road users, weather and distractions, so you can change what you do before a crash.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: How should your eyes, side vision, and mirrors work together continuously while you drive?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Keep your eyes scanning all the time, using peripheral vision and mirrors to track what is ahead, beside and behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Right after spotting a hazard ahead that calls for a speed or lane change, where must you check?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: After you spot a hazard that needs a change, check behind you, because traffic there affects what you can safely do.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Can driving risk ever be eliminated completely, and how do you keep it low?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Risk can never be removed completely, but you can lower it by identifying hazards and adjusting how you drive.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What is hazard perception, and what three mental and physical elements does it demand?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Hazard perception is scanning for risks and identifying them before they become problems, and it calls for attention, quick decisions and fitting reactions.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: How broadly does Washington define a road hazard, including everyday objects or your own planned turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: A hazard is anything that makes you change speed or direction, from a child darting into the road to a trash can, a speed limit sign or your own driveway turn.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Why do stationary items like a roadside trash can or upcoming driveway qualify as hazards just like a running child?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: A hazard is defined by needing a change in your speed or direction, so a harmless trash can or an upcoming driveway counts just as a running child does.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: How can hazards appear on the road, and what must you decide when several show up together?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Hazards can be still or moving and can come several at once, and the driver must decide which one needs the most urgent response.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: How does hazard perception differ from handling multiple hazards at the same moment?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Hazard perception is spotting risks before they become problems, while choosing which of several hazards needs the most urgent response is a separate driver duty.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What two advantages do you gain by easing off speed as you approach a hazard?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Slow down as you approach hazards to gain space and time for safe decisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What is situational awareness, and which nearby drivers may feel the biggest impact from your choices?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Situational awareness is constantly watching everything around you and predicting what to prepare for, and the drivers behind you may be the ones most affected by your choices.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: In exact order, what are the five steps of Washington's hazard management routine?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: The hazard management routine has five steps in order: plan, communicate, check, execute and evaluate.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: What scanning and decision happen during step one—the plan step—of the hazard management routine?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: In the plan step you scan around you, including the rearview mirror, and decide whether the change you want is safe.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What braking limit, mirror glance, and blind-spot scan belong to the check step?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: In the check step you set your position and speed so the change needs no more than medium braking, recheck mirrors, and look over your shoulder for walkers and cyclists.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: In Washington's five-step routine, which step turns on your signal and which step rechecks mirrors and your shoulder?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Signaling belongs to the communicate step, while rechecking mirrors and looking over your shoulder belong to the check step that follows it.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How hard should you ever need to brake if you set your speed and position properly during the check step?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: The check step aims for a change that needs at most medium braking, not hard braking, by setting your position and speed first.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: How should you carry out the execute step, and what is the goal of the final evaluate step?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: In the execute step you make the change smoothly without surprising anyone, and in the evaluate step you review how it went and adjust next time.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How do higher driving speeds affect seat-belt protection and your visual scanning window?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Higher speeds make seat belts less effective and leave less time to scan for walkers, cyclists and other vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What does speeding do to vehicle traction—especially in rain or snow—and to your stopping distance?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Speeding cuts vehicle and traction control, especially in rain or snow, and lengthens the distance needed to stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: What happens to crash impact force, injury severity, and fatality odds when vehicle speed rises?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Crash impact force rises with speed, so injuries become more severe and deaths more likely.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: What road conditions does a posted speed limit assume, and what additional speed duty does Washington law impose?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: A speed limit is the highest legal speed under ideal conditions, and Washington law also requires a speed that is safe for current conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Under Washington law, how is driving slower than the posted limit treated compared with driving over it?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Driving below the speed limit is allowed, but going over it is illegal.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Why is treating the posted speed sign as a goal speed illegal when roads, weather, or traffic deteriorate?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: The posted limit is a ceiling for ideal conditions, not a target, so a slower speed can be legally required when the road, weather or traffic is poor.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Around which visibility, surface, crowd, bridge, lot, or neighborhood settings should you actively reduce speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Slow down for sharp curves or hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, areas with pedestrians, children, cyclists or animals, parking lots, heavy traffic, narrow bridges and tunnels, and residential streets.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: Why do newer drivers face extra risk with vehicle spacing, and what two ways can space be measured?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Judging space takes practice, which is why new drivers face higher risk, and space can be judged by either distance or time.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Measured in vehicle lengths, how much minimum gap does the Washington guide say to keep behind the vehicle ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Near other vehicles, keep a gap to the vehicle ahead of at least twice the length of your own vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: What minimum car-length buffer does this Washington chapter state, alongside which two ways of judging space?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: The following gap in this guide is stated as at least two vehicle lengths behind the car ahead, and space may be judged by distance or by time.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: How big must your merge gap be in relation to surrounding drivers, and why is squeezing in risky?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Merge with enough room that nobody around you must swerve, slow or stop, because squeezing into a small gap is dangerous if the car ahead brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Who holds the right-of-way when you enter an interstate, and how should you use the on-ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Drivers already on the interstate have the right-of-way, so you adjust your speed up or down and use the whole on-ramp, your signal and mirrors to find a safe gap.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Between a driver already cruising on the interstate and a driver on the entrance ramp, who yields?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: On an interstate on-ramp the merging driver yields, because traffic already on the interstate holds the right-of-way.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: By what percentage does the Washington guide say zipper merging improves traffic flow, and how does it cut crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: The guide says zipper merging improves traffic flow by sixty percent and makes merging predictable, lowering the risk of crashes from sudden lane changes.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: When approaching a lane closure using a zipper merge, when should you move out of the closing lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: In a zipper merge at a lane closure, keep using both lanes until you reach the marked merge area instead of moving over early.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: Once traffic reaches the marked zipper-merge point, how should drivers alternate and manage speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: At the merge point, take turns, let one car from the ending lane go in front of you, and keep a steady speed matching the open lane.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: At a backed-up lane closure, why shouldn't drivers pile into the open lane early?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: At a slow lane closure the zipper method keeps both lanes in use up to the merge area, rather than everyone moving over early.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: What is eye-lead time, and how does it shift your driving from reacting late to acting early?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Eye-lead time is the defensive habit of scanning as far ahead and to the sides as you can, using mirrors for behind, so you see hazards early and act rather than react.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: How do you run the roadside marker exercise to sharpen your sense of driving time?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: To practice judging time, choose a marker you think is fifteen seconds ahead, then count until you reach it.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: How does the fifteen-second marker exercise relate to the broader habit of eye-lead time?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: The fifteen-second marker exercise trains you to estimate distance in seconds, while eye-lead time is the wider habit of scanning far ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: How does giving yourself enough time in traffic improve decision-making under pressure?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Having enough time lets you weigh and rank decisions in traffic, which reduces panic and impulsive moves.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: Who owns the right-of-way when you turn across oncoming traffic, and which side should your timing err on?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: When turning across oncoming traffic, remember that approaching traffic has the right-of-way, and allowing too much time is better than too little.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: How can you use a roadside marker to time oncoming traffic before turning across a lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: To judge a turn gap, count the seconds an oncoming car takes from a roadside marker to clear the road you want, then use that to estimate when the next car will arrive.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Before turning left across oncoming lanes, who yields and what should you do whenever a gap feels borderline?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Before a left turn across traffic the turning driver yields, and when the gap is uncertain the guide favors waiting for extra time.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: How big must your gap be when turning into a moving stream of traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Turning into a flow of traffic needs a gap long enough to finish the turn and reach the speed of the traffic you are joining without disrupting it.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What three habits define mindful driving in Washington?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Mindful driving means being mentally present with phone and entertainment off, prepared by scanning ahead, and proactive in adjusting to road, weather and traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: How many tasks can your brain genuinely focus on at once, and what must match your eye direction?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Your brain can focus on only one thing at a time, so line up your mental attention with where your eyes are looking.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: How brief a distraction can trigger a devastating crash, and where must you clear distractions from?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Even a distraction lasting a few seconds can have devastating results, so remove distractions from inside and outside the car.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Which three types of vision do drivers rely on, and what happens to all three as speed climbs?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Drivers use central, fringe and peripheral vision, and higher speeds lower the quality of all of them.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What specific part of the scene does central vision, fringe vision, and peripheral vision each handle?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Central vision shows detail straight ahead, fringe vision sees edges without sharp focus, and peripheral vision covers what is off to your side.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: How do focus sharpness and direction separate central, fringe, and peripheral vision?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Central vision is for detail straight ahead, fringe vision is seen but not sharp, and peripheral vision is what lies to your sides.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: What is your path of travel, and how do you redirect it when hazards, weather, or turns arise?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Your path of travel is the route you drive between places, and you will change it for hazards, weather or a new direction by picturing a new target area.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What does line of sight cover, and how should your attention move between it and your path of travel?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Line of sight is everything between you and the target area you picked, and you switch attention between it and your path of travel quickly and often.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: How does your path of travel differ from your line of sight?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: Path of travel is the route you drive, while line of sight is only the stretch between you and the target area you chose on that route.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Across which seven road, vehicle, and personal elements must you divide your attention while driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Your attention must be shared among your path, line of sight, target area, hazards, your vehicle inside and out, other road users and yourself.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How fast may you safely travel at night in relation to your headlights, and how far do beams normally reach?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: At night, drive slowly enough to stop within the reach of your headlights, which is usually four hundred feet.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: When should you use high-beam headlights at night, and when must you dim to regular beams?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Use high beams whenever no vehicles are coming toward you, and switch to regular headlights when traffic approaches.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: Which headlight setting must you use whenever you are following behind another vehicle at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Use regular headlights, not high beams, when you are following another vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: What change in traffic ahead tells you to switch out of high beams into regular headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: High beams are for roads with no oncoming vehicles, and you dim to regular headlights as soon as traffic approaches.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Where should you aim your eyes if an approaching driver leaves blinding high beams on?
