sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: If an oncoming driver keeps high beams on, look toward the right side of the road instead of into the lights.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Why do you shift your gaze toward the right side of the road instead of flashing back or staring at oncoming brights?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Facing an oncoming driver with high beams on, you shift your eyes toward the right side of the road rather than looking into the glare.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: How should you scan ahead and to the sides beyond your bright headlight pool at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: At night, look past your headlight beams for dark shapes and glance to the sides to find the pavement edge and side hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: During which two lighting conditions should you never wear sunglasses or colored lenses while driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Do not wear sunglasses or colored lenses at night or on overcast days, because tinted lenses cut your vision.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: How should you adjust your following distance after dark, especially on unfamiliar roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Lengthen your following distance at night, and especially on unfamiliar roads after dark.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Under which three curve or surface conditions must you slow down beforehand to maintain control?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Slow down before a sharp curve, on slippery pavement, or when water is on the road so you keep control of the vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: When must you shed speed for a curve, and how do uphill versus downhill curves change pedal input?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Reduce speed before you enter a curve, not in it, to keep traction; uphill curves may need more gas and downhill curves more braking.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: Where within your own lane should you position the car as you approach a curve, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Approach a curve positioned slightly toward the outside of your lane for more room and a better view around it.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: How should you manage throttle, brakes, and steering while traveling through the middle of a curve?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Inside a curve, hold a steady speed and steer gently, avoiding sudden braking, sudden acceleration or jerky steering that can upset balance.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: What two habits belong to exiting a curve as the road straightens out?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: Leaving a curve, speed up gradually and check your mirrors before merging or changing lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: What is the three-part speed pattern before entering, while inside, and when leaving a curve?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Speed comes off before the curve, stays steady inside it, and builds back gradually on the way out.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: In curve physics, what is vehicle roll versus vehicle yaw, and how do you keep both balanced?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: Roll is how much the vehicle tilts in a turn and yaw is its side-to-side movement, and adjusting speed and steering balances both in curves.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: Which way does inertia push your car in a curve, and why does jerking the wheel backfire?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Inertia tries to keep the car going straight, so a sudden turn of the wheel in a curve works against you and steering must be smooth.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: How does higher speed change kinetic energy and the time and space needed to turn or stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: More speed means more kinetic energy and more time and space needed to stop or turn, so slowing for curves helps you keep traction.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: What physical force lets tires grip the pavement, and what weather conditions slash it in curves?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Friction between tires and road is what lets you grip, and rain, snow or ice can sharply reduce it in curves, so slow down even more there.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How does the Washington guide distinguish inertia, kinetic energy, and friction?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: Inertia is the pull to keep going straight, kinetic energy is what grows with speed, and friction is the grip between tires and road.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: What speed adjustment is required whenever pavement turns slick, even if the posted sign allows faster travel?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: On slippery roads you must adjust to conditions, which can mean driving below the posted limit.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Why are the first few minutes of rain on a hot day extraordinarily slick?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: When rain begins on a hot day, the road is very slippery for the first few minutes because heat brings oil in the asphalt to the surface until it washes off.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: After rain starts falling on hot pavement, when is skidding danger highest and why does it ease later?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: When rain starts on a hot day the danger is at the start, since the road stays very slippery for the first few minutes until the surfaced oil washes away.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: Which two big adjustments do snowy roads require from every driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: Snowy roads call for a much larger following distance and a greatly reduced speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: When must you mount snow tires or chains in Washington, and what winter hardware boosts grip?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: Use snow tires or chains where they are required, and in winter chains or studded tires can improve traction.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Which two road features freeze over first even when surrounding pavement stays bare and wet?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Shady spots on cold, wet days and bridges or overpasses can be icy even when the rest of the road is not.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: Does ice get grippier or slicker as air temperatures warm from deep cold up toward freezing?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: Ice warming from below freezing to near freezing gets wet on top and becomes even more slippery.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: Where does surprise ice linger on clear days, and why does warming toward freezing worsen grip?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Bridges, overpasses and shady spots can be icy while the rest of the road is clear, and ice that warms toward freezing turns wet and makes the road more slippery, not less.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: What is black ice, and at what thermometer range must you stay on guard even when pavement looks dry?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: Black ice is a thin, hard-to-see coating of ice, so stay alert whenever temperatures are near or below freezing even if you see no ice.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: What causes tires to skid, what driving inputs trigger one on slick roads, and what is your best defense?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: A skid happens when tires lose their grip, made more likely by high speed and slick roads when you turn or stop suddenly, and the best defense is avoiding one.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: In what order do you use the pedals during a skid, and why shouldn't you stomp non-ABS brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: In a skid, first lift your foot off the accelerator, then press or pump the brakes; without antilock brakes, stomping the pedal can worsen the skid.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: How does braking behavior in a skid differ between a car with antilock brakes and one without?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Antilock brakes let you keep steering while braking in a skid, whereas without them a quick hard press on the pedal can deepen the skid.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: Which direction do you turn the steering wheel during a skid, and how long do you keep adjusting?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: During a skid, steer the way the vehicle is moving and keep correcting until the tires regain traction in the direction you steer.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: What happens beneath your tires during hydroplaning, and what is the number-one way to prevent it?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: Hydroplaning is water building up between tires and road so they lose traction, and slowing down on wet roads is the best prevention.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.front: What four calm actions should you take with pedals, wheel, and eyes if your car starts hydroplaning?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.expected_back: If you hydroplane, lift off the accelerator, brake gently, hold the wheel steady without jerking it, and look where you want to go.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How does your steering response in a dry-or-icy skid differ from your steering response while hydroplaning?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: In a skid you steer in the direction the car is moving and keep correcting, but when hydroplaning you hold the wheel steady and avoid any jerk or overcorrection.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Why does the Washington guide warn against hard braking while hydroplaning, especially without antilock brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Without antilock brakes, pressing the pedal hard while hydroplaning can make it worse, which is why the guide says to brake gently.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What number should you call immediately when witnessing road rage happening right now?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Report road rage that is happening right now by calling nine one one at once.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Which eight location, vehicle, weapon, and role details help dispatchers when you report aggressive driving to nine-one-one?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: When you call nine one one about an aggressive driving act, give where the vehicles were last seen, the plate if known, direction of travel, the road, vehicle colors, any weapons, what happened and whether you were a victim or witness.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Which agency places cutting road rage and aggressive driving at the heart of its mission, and how do residents help?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Cutting road rage and aggressive driving is central to the mission of the Washington State Patrol, and reports from residents help improve safety.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Does witnessing an aggressive driving act use a non-emergency line or the same number as live road rage?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Road rage in progress goes straight to nine one one, and the same number is used to report a witnessed aggressive driving act.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What defines an informed driving decision, and what three safety payoffs follow from making them?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: An informed decision weighs every factor before you act, and such decisions raise your awareness, encourage responsible driving and lower the risk of crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Which three personal foundations shape every choice you make behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Your decisions are shaped by your knowledge of traffic laws, your experience with safe practices, and the capabilities that come with your age and brain development.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Why are teen drivers biologically prone to misjudging risk, and what two temptations must safety beat?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: In teen drivers the brain area that handles judgment and decisions is still maturing, so teens may take more risks or misjudge situations and must put safety ahead of speed and peer pressure.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What crash vulnerability and ability shifts come with aging — and does age alone make older drivers unsafe?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Physical and mental abilities shift with age and older drivers can be hurt more seriously in crashes, yet many stay safe and capable drivers late in life.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Contrast the biological reason teen drivers need extra care with the reason older drivers do?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Teens face a still-developing judgment center in the brain, while older drivers face physical and mental changes with age, two different reasons the guide gives for extra care.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Walk through the three steps — inform, prepare, and final check — of the Washington guide's decision approach?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: The guide's decision approach has three steps: inform yourself with mirror checks and signal your plan to others, prepare the vehicle so you reach the hazard at the right position and speed, and make a final check before the maneuver.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: In Washington's three-step decision sequence, what two steps must already be done right before your final check?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: In the guide's decision approach the final check comes last, after informing yourself and others and after preparing your position and speed, right before the maneuver.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Which three qualities should describe every speed, lane, or direction change you make on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: In every change you make on the road, aim to be aware, predictable and smooth.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Which three adjustments solve most road hazards — and what communication rule keeps others safe meanwhile?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Solving a problem on the road usually means changing your speed, shifting your lane position, or changing your path to reach a safe place to reassess, while telling others your plan so you do not surprise them.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What four words form the OODA acronym, and why is it described as a continuous loop?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: The OODA loop is Observe, Orient, Decide, Act, and it is called a loop because each situation leads straight into the next one.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Match Observe, Orient, Decide, and Act to the specific job each performs on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: In the OODA loop, Observe spots what changed, Orient uses your knowledge to judge what the change means for safety, Decide picks the safest action, and Act carries it out smoothly with clear signals.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How does the Observe step differ from the Orient step inside the OODA loop?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Observe is noticing that something changed, whereas Orient is working out what that change means for your safety and others before you Decide.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Name the guide's four distraction groups and give real examples inside each one?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Distractions fall into four groups: inside the vehicle such as phones, food, the radio and passengers; outside such as billboards and crashes; physical such as fatigue or discomfort; and mental such as daydreaming, worry or strong emotion.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Classify fatigue and body aches versus daydreaming, worry, and strong emotions — and is a phone required?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Fatigue and discomfort count as physical distractions, while daydreaming, worry and strong emotions are mental distractions, so a distraction need not involve a phone.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Which four lane, speed, sign, and following mistakes commonly give away a distracted driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Distracted drivers tend to drift from their lane, drive too fast or too slow, miss signals, stop signs and vulnerable road users, and follow too closely.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Which three habits prevent distraction, and what three mental or physical benefits do you gain?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: To avoid distraction, plan ahead, put the phone away and stay observant, which lets you react faster, decide better and feel less stress and fatigue.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: How broadly does Washington define distracted driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Washington defines distracted driving as any activity that pulls attention away from the main job of driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: May experienced adult drivers hold a phone, tablet, or gaming device while driving in Washington — and what about hands-free?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: No driver of any age or experience may hold an electronic device such as a phone, tablet or gaming device while driving, though hands-free use is permitted.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: For full-license Washington drivers, what exact physical line separates illegal device use from permitted use?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The Washington rule bans holding any electronic device while driving for every driver, while hands-free use stays permitted, so the test line is holding, not talking.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What financial penalties apply to a Washington distracted-driving citation — especially if you offend again?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: An officer can ticket you for breaking the distracted driving law, the fines can be heavy, and fines for violations after your first can be doubled.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Does Washington double distracted-driving fines on the very first ticket or on subsequent violations?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Doubling applies to distracted driving fines after your first violation, not to the first ticket itself.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Which five habits — covering awareness, controls, predictability, judgment, and growth — mark a smart driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Smart drivers are aware inside and outside the car, in control of gas, brake, steering and position, predictable through signals and smooth moves, thoughtful in decisions and intentional in learning.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Which four types of human attention does the Washington guide identify?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: The guide names four kinds of attention: switching from one focus to another, divided across several tasks, focused on one task, and sustained over a long time.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Match switching, divided, focused, and sustained attention to how your mind operates in each mode?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Switching attention jumps quickly from one thing to another, divided attention handles several things at once, focused attention puts the whole mind on one task, and sustained attention holds it over a long time.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: Which five pre-drive and cabin steps protect your attention behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Help your attention by removing in-car distractions, being well rested, silencing and stowing electronics, limiting passengers and pets, and refusing to multitask.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: How does the Washington guide distinguish 'searching' from 'scanning'?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Searching means actively checking around you with your eyes, while scanning adds turning your head, neck and body to see as much as possible.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: Which visual habit relies on your eyes alone, and which adds head, neck, and body movement?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Searching uses your eyes alone to check around you, while scanning also moves your head, neck and body to widen what you can see.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: How should your visual ability to search and scan cap your driving speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Drive at a speed that still lets you search and scan well, because constant searching underpins safe driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: When scanning ahead, what clues near parked cars and beyond the lead vehicle help you avoid sudden swerves?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Scanning ahead means watching for things to steer around, blockages that could hide people, feet, wheels or shadows near parked cars, and what is happening beyond the car in front, so you avoid sudden braking or swerving.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Which four intersection, crosswalk, roadside, and pre-turn checks make up effective side scanning?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Scanning to the side means watching left and right at intersections, watching for crossing walkers and cyclists, watching for movement behind foliage, and doing a mirror and over-shoulder check before turning.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Before which five maneuvers or hills must you check behind for trailing vehicles and cyclists?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Look for vehicles and cyclists behind you before a lane change, before turning across a bike lane, and when slowing, backing, or heading down a long or steep hill.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Why should you check mirrors more frequently in dense traffic, and what three responses can protect you?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Look behind more often in heavy traffic so that a tailgater or fast-approaching vehicle gives you time to react by changing lanes, tapping the brakes, or adjusting speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: Which six safety, courtesy, conflict, and environmental habits define respectful driving in Washington?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Respectful driving means everyone buckled up, being fit to drive, showing empathy, respecting others' space, avoiding conflict no matter who is at fault, and caring for the road environment.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: What do traffic advisories report, who issues them, and through which five channels do drivers receive them?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Traffic advisories are alerts about current or coming conditions, incidents or closures from transportation officials, traffic centers or navigation apps, delivered by electronic road signs, radio, websites, social media and apps.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: What two major hazards make Washington's littering fines so steep, and what must drivers and passengers do?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Road litter can cause crashes and burning litter can start wildfires, so Washington's littering fines are severe and you and your passengers must secure loads and dispose of trash properly.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: How do Washington state law and local ordinances split littering penalties, and whom can you ask locally?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: State law sets minimum fines for littering and illegal dumping, and local ordinances may differ, so ask local police, the sheriff or a city or county clerk which rules apply.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Does Washington state law cap maximum littering fines everywhere or establish only the minimum baseline?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: State law fixes only the minimum littering fines, and cities and counties may set their own different rules on top of it.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: What deadly gas builds up when a parked car idles — especially in a garage — and which four habits cut emissions?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Leaving a parked car running, especially inside a garage, can release deadly carbon monoxide, so shut the engine off when parked a while, drive smoothly, keep tires inflated and carpool when you can.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: Which model years fall under Washington's Clean Car Law, and what three transactions are blocked if a car fails?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Washington's Clean Car Law says a vehicle built in two thousand nine or later must pass strict clean air standards before anyone can register, license or sell it.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: Pinpoint the exact model-year cutoff and three blocked actions under Washington's Clean Car Law?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: The Clean Car Law covers vehicles built in two thousand nine and later and blocks registering, licensing or selling one that fails the clean air standards.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: Which four reflection questions help you review a drive afterward — and what happens without regular self-review?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: After or during a drive, evaluate yourself by asking whether anything surprised you, whether you surprised anyone, whether your driving was legal, proficient and smooth, and what to change next time, because skills fade without review.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Which three attitudes form the foundation for safely sharing Washington roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Courtesy, respect and awareness of others are the key to sharing Washington roads, and your care could save a life, including your own.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Where do pedestrians and crossing bicyclists hold legal right-of-way on Washington streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Always yield to pedestrians, who, like bicyclists, hold the right-of-way at every crosswalk and intersection, marked or unmarked.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: How far across must a pedestrian get before you roll forward, and how does a cane, wheelchair, or service animal change that?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Wait until a pedestrian has cleared your lane plus one more lane before going, but for someone crossing with a wheelchair, a cane, a guide dog or another service animal, stay stopped until the whole street is crossed.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How does Washington's waiting rule contrast an unaided walker with someone using a wheelchair, cane, or guide dog?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: A pedestrian without a mobility aid must clear your lane and one more before you go, but a pedestrian with a wheelchair, cane or service animal must reach the far side of the street.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Which groups on foot deserve heightened scanning because distraction, youth, or unfamiliarity hides your approach?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Watch for people who cannot see you, are distracted, or may be confused, such as children, road workers, tourists or someone on a phone.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Why must you keep your hand off the horn near a pedestrian accompanied by a service animal?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Interfering with a service animal is unlawful, and you should not honk near one because the noise can confuse or frighten the animal or its handler.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: How do the yellow and red warning lights on a school bus mirror standard intersection signals?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: School bus lights work like traffic signals: red means stop, and yellow means use caution and slow down.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What happens to the ticket amount if you illegally pass a stopped school bus flashing red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Passing a stopped school bus doubles the fine, and it is unlawful to pass a bus while its red lights flash.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: Which same-direction lanes must halt for a school bus's red flashers, and what rule applies to center turn lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Every driver going the same direction as the bus must stop for flashing red lights and the extended stop sign, including drivers in any turn lane, and a center turn lane may never be used to pass.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: Why is a shared center turn lane never a legal shortcut past a stopped school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: A center turn lane is not a way around a stopped school bus, because drivers in every turn lane must stop too.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: Which three equipment cues on a stopped school bus must finish resetting before you roll again?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: You may move again only once the lights stop flashing, the stop sign folds back and the metal arm returns to the front bumper, and you should keep watching for children afterward.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Who must stop on a two-lane road when a school bus activates red flashers and its stop paddle?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when the bus's red lights flash and its stop sign is out.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: On a multilane road, who always stops for a school bus, and what two features appear in the guide's oncoming exception?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: On a multilane road, drivers behind the bus always stop, while the guide's exception for oncoming drivers names two conditions, a road of three or more lanes and lanes split by a median or barrier, without saying whether one alone is enough.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: On a two-lane street, when can oncoming traffic resume moving past a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: On a two-lane road, oncoming drivers stop for a school bus with flashing red lights just like drivers behind it, and they move on only after the lights stop, the sign retracts and the arm returns to the bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Does Washington's multilane school-bus exception ever excuse drivers traveling behind the bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: The multilane exception helps only oncoming traffic; anyone traveling behind the bus on any multilane road must still stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What is your legal duty when a same-direction transit bus flashes its turn signal to pull back from the curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Yield to a transit bus going your direction that has signaled and is pulling back into traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: Why shouldn't you linger alongside a semi-truck or bus, and what mirror check reveals whether the driver sees you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Large trucks and buses have blind zones on each side, so do not ride alongside them for long, and if you cannot see the driver's mirrors the driver cannot see you.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How many feet does a loaded truck with good brakes need to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A loaded truck with good brakes at fifty-five miles per hour needs four hundred fifty feet to stop completely, so cutting in front of one without room is dangerous.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What visual cue in your inside mirror confirms enough gap to merge ahead of a truck, and how should you drive next?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Before merging in front of a large vehicle, wait until both of its headlights show in your rearview mirror, then keep up with traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Why is spotting a single truck headlight in your mirror too soon to merge back, and what mistake must you avoid afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Before merging ahead of a large vehicle you need both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, not just one, and after merging you keep pace with traffic rather than slowing in front of it.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: How much lane space can big trucks need for corners or roundabouts, and why must you hold back mid-turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Large vehicles may need more than one lane to turn and two lanes in a roundabout, and passing one while it turns is a frequent cause of crashes, so wait until the turn is done.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How should you position yourself around hazmat-placarded rigs, and what should you anticipate on long steep hills?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Keep away from vehicles placarded as carrying hazardous materials when you can, and expect slow large vehicles in the right lane on long, steep grades.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: What visibility hazard makes tailgating an active snowplow dangerous?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Snowplows can throw snow up and off the road in a blizzard-like cloud, so do not follow them closely.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: How do motorcycle legal rights compare with cars, and why do riders need extra following cushion—especially in rain?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Motorcyclists share the same rights and traffic laws as other drivers, but they are smaller, harder to see and more vulnerable, so leave extra following room, more still on wet or slick roads.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: May you squeeze alongside a motorcycle inside the same lane if the rider is positioned near one edge?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane width, so never move into its lane beside it, even if the rider is far to one side.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: What look sequence protects motorcycles before a right turn, and what judgment error hits oncoming riders?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Motorcycles hide easily in blind zones, so before a right turn look left, right and left again with a shoulder check, and remember drivers often misjudge an oncoming motorcycle's speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Which everyday street flaws can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or swerve inside the lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Gravel, debris, pavement seams, potholes and even manhole covers can force a rider to change speed or lane position, so expect those moves.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: Which two quirks of motorcycle deceleration and turn indicators can mislead nearby drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Riders may slow by easing the throttle without showing a brake light, and some motorcycle turn signals do not cancel on their own, so stay alert beside them.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Why shouldn't you trust a motorcycle's brake lamp or blinking turn signal by itself?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: A motorcycle can slow down with no brake light showing, and its turn signal may still blink after the turn, so neither light alone tells you what the rider will do.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: What legal rights and duties apply to bicyclists on the road, and why are crashes so severe for them?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Bicyclists carry the same rights and duties as vehicle drivers, and because bikes are small and hard to see, riders face a high risk of serious injury or death.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: Can a bicyclist claim the entire travel lane, and what minimum gap applies when trailing behind one?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: A bicyclist may legally use the full lane, you may not share a lane with one, and when following a bicyclist you leave at least three feet of space.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: What legal status does a bicyclist riding through a marked or unmarked crosswalk hold?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: A bicyclist riding in a crosswalk counts as a pedestrian, so you must yield in marked and unmarked crosswalks alike.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: How does a bicyclist's legal role shift between riding down a street lane and rolling across a crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A bicyclist on the road is treated as a vehicle with a right to the full lane, but a bicyclist in a crosswalk is treated as a pedestrian you must yield to.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: How do you legally overtake a bicyclist on multilane versus two-lane roads, and when must you hold back?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: To pass a bicyclist, move over a full lane when two lanes run your way, or use the other lane only without oncoming traffic, pass slowly on their left with at least three feet from your widest point, and do not pass just before a right turn.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: From what part of your vehicle is the three-foot bike-passing buffer measured, and how do two-lane passes work?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: The three-foot passing gap for a bicyclist is measured from the widest part of your vehicle, and with one lane each way you use the other lane only when no traffic is coming.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: How are Washington bike lanes typically painted, and which two maneuvers let a motorist cross or enter one?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Bike lanes are often green with solid white lines and a bicycle symbol, and you may drive in one only to turn or to cross it to park at the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: Where are motorists permitted to cross railroad tracks, and what do flashing red crossing lights signify?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Cross railroad tracks only at designated crossings, and flashing red lights there mean a train is coming and you must stay outside the gates.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: Why do trains always hold right-of-way, and what if crossing bells and lights trigger while the gate stays up?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Trains always have the right-of-way and can need up to a mile to stop, so stop for flashing lights and bells even if the gate is up, and never go around a gate.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Within what distance window from the nearest rail must you stop when train warnings, flaggers, horns, or signs apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Stop fifteen to fifty feet from the nearest rail when signals flash, a gate is lowering or down, a flagger signals, a train is close or sounds its horn, or a stop sign is posted.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: What are the exact near and far boundaries of Washington's railroad stop zone, and do raised gates excuse active flashers?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: The railroad stop zone is no closer than fifteen feet and no farther than fifty feet from the nearest rail, and flashing lights with bells mean stop even when the gate is still up.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: What immediate step comes first if your vehicle stalls across railroad tracks, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Never stop on the tracks, and if your vehicle stalls at a crossing, get everyone out right away, because trains can come from either direction on any track.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Which phone number do you call first for an obstruction on or near railroad tracks, and when do you dial nine-one-one?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: If something is on or near the tracks, phone the number shown on the crossing's blue and white Emergency Notification System sign, quote the crossing ID, or dial nine one one if there is no sign.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Between nine-one-one and the blue-and-white Emergency Notification System plaque, which takes priority at a rail hazard?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: A problem on the tracks goes first to the number on the blue and white Emergency Notification System sign, and nine one one is the fallback only when no sign is posted.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: How much space must you keep from a light-rail train, and what rule governs stopping on its rails?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: Near light rail, keep at least one car length between you and the train and never stop or park on the tracks.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: Which vehicles carry a rear orange triangle, and what three habits make passing one safe?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Farm vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less display a triangle emblem on the back, and passing one calls for patience, a full lane change where possible and at least three feet of clearance.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: How must you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle with lights or sirens, and how do you merge back afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: For a fire truck, ambulance or police car using lights or sirens, pull right and stop at once, then signal and rejoin traffic only after it passes, in the order you were in before.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: Once a police car, fire engine, or ambulance clears your stopped line, how do drivers pull back onto the road?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle you pull to the right and stop as soon as you see or hear it, and you signal and rejoin traffic in your original order only once it has gone by.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Where should you bring a disabled vehicle to a stop, and which two blind road spots must you avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: When your vehicle has trouble, get it off the road if you can, or stop where others can see it clearly, never just past a hilltop or around a curve.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Which vehicle lights go on during a roadside breakdown, and how far behind your car should flares sit?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: For a breakdown, switch on your emergency flashers and headlights and set flares two hundred to three hundred feet behind the vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: If you have no flares during a breakdown, how do you warn approaching drivers and signal distress on the car?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Without flares, stand somewhere safe and wave traffic around, and signal an emergency by raising the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna, mirror or door handle.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How does warning approaching traffic with flares compare with warning them when you carry none?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Breakdown flares go two hundred to three hundred feet behind your vehicle, and with no flares you wave traffic around from a safe place instead.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: What four actions with wheel and pedals keep you safe right after a sudden tire blowout?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly, keep going straight, lift off the accelerator and let the car slow on its own, braking only gently if needed.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Why shouldn't you brake firmly right after a tire blows out the way you might for an obstacle?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: After a blowout you let the car slow by itself and brake only gently if needed, rather than braking firmly as you might for a hazard ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: What three things should you do if a flat tire strands you somewhere unsafe to jack up the car?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: If you cannot reach a safe spot to change a flat, turn on hazard lights, stay inside the vehicle and call for help.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: How do steering and braking behave if your engine dies mid-drive, and how should you pull off?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: If the engine dies while driving, hold the wheel firmly, since steering gets harder but still works, and brake with steady pressure rather than hard while you pull off.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Once you safely coast to the shoulder with a stalled engine, what sequence follows?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: After the engine dies and you stop, try a restart, and if it fails raise the hood, turn on hazard lights and call for help.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Which backup lights can help you see and be seen if your headlights suddenly go dark, and what must you do?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: If your headlights suddenly fail, turn on hazard lights, turn signals or fog lights if you have them and leave the road as soon as you can.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What four steps in order handle a stuck accelerator when the car keeps speeding up?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: If the accelerator sticks and the car keeps speeding up, keep your eyes on the road, shift quickly to neutral, pull off when safe and turn off the engine.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: How does handling a dead engine while moving differ from handling a stuck accelerator?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: A dead engine calls for steady brake pressure and pulling off, while a stuck accelerator calls for shifting quickly into neutral before pulling off and shutting the engine down.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Which three built-in communication tools alert other road users when a risk appears?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Your lights, horn and hand signals are the tools for warning other road users that a risk is present.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Who bears responsibility for preventing collisions, and can skillful driving guarantee you never experience one?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Every driver is responsible for preventing crashes, which can call for evasive moves, yet even a good driver can still end up in a collision.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Which three everyday failures does the Washington guide name as the usual causes of collisions?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: The guide names three usual causes of collisions: too much speed, too little space and poor situational awareness.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: What is the number-one rule after any collision, and when must nine-one-one and police be notified?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: After a crash, never drive away, and if anyone is hurt or killed, call nine one one because police must be notified.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: Where should drivable crashed vehicles and occupants relocate right after a collision?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Move a crashed vehicle to the roadside close to the collision site as soon as you can, and stay out of the traffic lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: Which three steps protect a crash scene from oncoming traffic and fuel fires?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: At a crash, warn others with flares or other devices, switch off the wrecked vehicles, and do not smoke because spilled fuel can catch fire.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: What must you try first if you bump an unattended parked car, and what must a written note include?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: If you hit a parked vehicle you must try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a visible note with the date, time and your contact details.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: After striking a parked vehicle, can you simply drop a note and leave without looking for the owner?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Hitting a parked car means first trying to find its owner, and leaving a note with date, time and contact details is the fallback when you cannot.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Which five pieces of driver and policy info should crash-involved drivers swap, plus what visual step?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Drivers in a crash exchange names, contact details, driver license numbers, insurance companies and policy numbers, and should photograph the damage.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Within how many days must you file a Washington state collision report if no police officer files one?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: State law requires you to file a collision report form within four days of a crash when a police officer does not file one for you.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Does every Washington crash require you to submit your own four-day collision form, or only certain crashes?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: The collision report deadline is four days and applies only when a police officer does not file the report for you.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: Under what sole circumstance should you move an injured crash victim before medics arrive?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Do not move injured people unless they are in a burning vehicle or other immediate danger.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: When helping a crash victim who isn't walking and talking, which two vital checks come first in order?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Help anyone who is not walking and talking by checking breathing first and then bleeding.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: In what three-step escalation order does the Washington guide list bleeding control?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: For bleeding the guide lists hand pressure first, then a bandage or dressing, then a tourniquet.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: Putting vital checks and wound care together, what comes first and how do the three bleeding steps progress?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Breathing is checked before bleeding, and for bleeding hand pressure comes before a dressing, with a tourniquet listed last.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: May you give water to an injured crash victim, and how do you help prevent shock?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Give injured people nothing to drink, not even water, and cover them with a blanket or coat to keep them warm and help prevent shock.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What location anchors and scene summary should you give the nine-one-one dispatcher first?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: On a nine one one call, stay calm and give your location with nearby landmarks or mile markers, then briefly describe the vehicles, damage and injuries.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: When may you hang up on nine-one-one after reporting a crash, and what extra details might dispatchers ask?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Stay on the line with the nine one one dispatcher until help arrives, ready to add details such as vehicle types, plate numbers and hazards.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: What must you do if a downed power line rests on your car, and how should you treat every wire?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: If a power line touches your vehicle, do not get out; turn off the engine, call nine one one and wait inside for responders, treating every line as live.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What should you do immediately if your tires roll onto a downed power line?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: If you drive over a power line, stop at once, because moving forward or backing up risks electrocution, and stay inside until told it is safe.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How far back should bystanders stay when power lines touch a vehicle or a transformer box is hit?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: When lines fall on your vehicle or you hit a transformer box, the ground nearby may be energized, so urge people to stay at least thirty-five feet away.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: If your car catches fire while touching a live wire, how must you exit and move away?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: If fire starts while a power line touches your vehicle, jump clear with arms at your sides and both feet landing together, without touching the vehicle, then shuffle thirty-five feet away.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Which two downed-power-line safety rules in Washington both use the exact distance of thirty-five feet?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: The thirty-five-foot figure appears twice: it is how far bystanders should stay from an energized vehicle and how far you shuffle after jumping clear of one.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: When a power line touches or lies under your car, what is the sole emergency that justifies leaving the cabin?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Staying inside is the rule for any power line contact, including driving over one, and the only exit the guide describes is jumping clear when a fire starts.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: What three rules apply as you drive past someone else's collision scene?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Passing a crash, do not block responders, obey anyone authorized to direct traffic there, and keep your eyes on driving because slowing to stare causes congestion.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: Which nine medical, lighting, warmth, power, tire, and warning supplies belong in a well-stocked car emergency kit?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.memory_hook: Aid, light, warmth, cables, spare, flares
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: A vehicle emergency kit can hold a first aid kit, flashlight, blanket, water, jumper cables, tools, a backup charger, spare tire and jack, and reflective triangles or flares.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: Why should your glovebox kit include important phone numbers written on paper?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Keep a paper list of important phone numbers in case your phone dies and you must call from another phone.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: How do law enforcement officers signal a traffic stop, and how should you pull over?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Police signal a stop with flashing lights, a siren or both, and you respond by signaling and pulling to the right side of the road as soon as it is safe.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Once stopped on the shoulder for police, what should you shut off and where must you stay?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Once stopped for police, turn off the engine and any radio or audio, and stay in the vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What three visibility and hand habits apply during a nighttime police stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: At a night stop turn on your interior lights, keep your hands on the wheel, and follow all instructions given to you or your passengers.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: When the officer walks up, what should you do with the window, any weapon onboard, and reaching for papers?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: When the officer comes up, lower the window on that side, say right away if a weapon is in the vehicle, and wait for instructions before reaching for documents.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: Which three documents do officers normally request, and what should you say before retrieving them?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: An officer will usually ask for your driver license, proof of insurance and vehicle registration, so say where they are before you reach for them.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: During a police stop, should you grab your license and registration while the officer walks up or wait?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: At a traffic stop you tell the officer where your documents are and wait for instructions before reaching, rather than reaching for them first.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.front: If you disagree with a traffic stop or officer conduct, what shouldn't you do roadside, and what two proper channels exist?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.expected_back: You may respectfully ask the officer questions, but if you disagree, do not argue; you can contest the decision in court or contact the officer's agency to ask for a supervisor.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Which channel handles contesting an officer's ticket decision versus reporting concerns about an officer's conduct?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Disagreeing with an officer's decision is handled by contesting it in court, while a concern about the officer's conduct goes to the officer's agency with a request for a supervisor.

sec14-card-sec14-F38.front: Does signing a Washington traffic citation admit guilt, and what can happen if you refuse to sign?
sec14-card-sec14-F38.expected_back: You must sign a traffic ticket, signing does not admit guilt, and refusing to sign can lead to arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F39.front: Within how many days must you follow the response instructions on the back of a Washington traffic ticket?
sec14-card-sec14-F39.expected_back: Follow the instructions on the back of a ticket within fifteen days or your driving privileges can be suspended.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: What two legal truths apply to signing a Washington traffic ticket at the roadside and responding afterward?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: The ticket response window is fifteen days to avoid suspension, and signing the ticket is required but is not an admission of guilt.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Which two exams must every new Washington driver pass, and what distinct skill does each measure?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Every new driver must pass two exams: the Driving Knowledge Exam, which checks understanding of Washington's rules of the road, and the Driving Skills Exam, which checks the ability to apply them.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Which driving exam must be passed first, and how long does that passing result give you to finish the second?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: The knowledge exam must be passed first, and from that point you have two years to complete the skills exam.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Is a new driver ever allowed to take the skills exam before passing the knowledge exam?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Passing the knowledge exam opens a two-year window for the skills exam, and the skills exam can never be taken first.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Who is allowed inside the car during your driving skills exam—including the two narrow exceptions?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: During the skills exam only you and the examiner may ride in the vehicle, with exceptions made for service animals and sign language interpreters.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which registration, insurance, lighting, and restraint items must your skills-exam vehicle pass before pulling out?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: The skills-exam vehicle must be legally licensed and registered, carry proof of current liability insurance naming the policy holder or describing the vehicle, and have working brake lights, signal lights and seat belts.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: At which two types of locations can you schedule and take your Washington driving exams?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: You can take the exams either at an approved driver training school exam location or by booking a driver licensing office appointment in License Express.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which two instructional components make up approved Washington driver training for students under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Approved driver training for new drivers under eighteen combines classroom lessons with behind-the-wheel training from a licensed instructor, offered by private schools and some school districts.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Why do driving schools offer adult traffic safety courses for untrained drivers over eighteen, newcomers, or rusty drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Drivers over eighteen who never took driver training face a higher crash risk, so some schools run adult traffic safety courses for beginners, newcomers to the United States, or anyone wanting a refresher.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What family session must teen driver training schools offer, and what practice-hour split does it cover?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Driver training courses for students under eighteen must offer a parent orientation class that explains the requirement of forty daylight hours and ten night hours of practice driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Should calendar age alone decide when someone stops driving, or which three personal factors matter instead?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Age alone should not decide whether someone keeps driving, but changes in vision, fitness and reflexes can raise safety concerns, so drivers should assess them and adjust habits or choose other transportation.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: What two ways can you replace a Washington license that is lost, stolen, destroyed, or worn unreadable?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: A lost, stolen, destroyed or unreadable license can be replaced online at dol.wa.gov, or as a duplicate in person at any driver licensing office.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Where on your Washington license is the expiration date printed, and how early before expiry may you renew?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Your expiration date is near the bottom of the license, and you may renew as early as one year before it expires, online through License Express or at a licensing office.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What extra cost can hit a late renewal, and after how many expired years must you retake both exams?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Renewing after expiration may add a fee, and a license that has been expired eight or more years means retaking both the skills and knowledge exams.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: How does Washington's one-year early-renewal rule contrast with its eight-year long-expired rule?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: You may renew up to one year before expiration, but if the license has been expired eight or more years you must retake both exams.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: How soon and where must you report a new residential address—and how does changing your legal name differ?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: After a move you must update your address in License Express within ten days, but a name change has to be made at a driver licensing office.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Which personal update belongs in License Express within ten days, and which forces an in-person office trip?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: An address change is done in License Express within ten days, while a name change requires a visit to a driver licensing office.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Where can Washingtonians register to vote, and which teen age group can pre-register during a license or ID visit?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: You can register to vote at sos.wa.gov or at a licensing office, and residents aged sixteen and seventeen may pre-register when they apply for a license or ID card.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Which two optional federal or research registrations appear on a Washington license or ID application?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: When applying for a license or ID card you may register with the U.S. Selective Service System and may say whether you are a twin for the state research registry.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which intermediate, minor-possession, ticket-accumulation, and suspended-driving violations can strip your driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Grounds for losing driving privileges include breaking intermediate restrictions, a minor possessing alcohol, drugs or firearms, piling up moving violations, and driving while suspended or revoked.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Which five fleeing, impairment, reckless, work-zone, or unpaid-ticket offenses cost driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Privileges can also be lost for fleeing police, driving under the influence, racing or reckless driving, endangering a construction or emergency worker, or letting traffic citations go unresolved.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Which major crash crimes, insurance failure, or medical-skill check can also end your driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: Vehicular assault, vehicular homicide, hit and run, a felony involving a vehicle, driving uninsured, and failing a competency evaluation are further grounds for losing privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Until what age can an alcohol, drug, or firearm offense delay a minor's Washington driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A minor who commits an alcohol, drug or firearm offense risks having the license delayed until age seventeen.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: What three non-traffic minor offenses can hold back your driver license eligibility until age seventeen?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Minors who commit an alcohol, drug, or firearm offense risk having their driver license delayed until age seventeen.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What testing, fee, and under-eighteen family requirements apply when reinstating a lost license?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: To get a license back you must retake the knowledge and skills exams even if you passed them before, pay a reissue fee on top of the usual fees, and, if under eighteen, have a parent or guardian's consent.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Under RCW forty-six point six one five hundred two, what conduct on the road is illegal?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Washington law, RCW forty-six point six one.five hundred two, makes it illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: How can someone sitting inside a parked car still violate Washington's DUI law under RCW forty-six point six one five hundred three?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Under RCW forty-six point six one.five hundred three the DUI law also covers being in physical control of a vehicle, even a parked one, which means being able to take control of its engine or operation.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How do Washington's five-hundred-two and five-hundred-three sections work together to cover impaired motorists?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Driving under the influence and being in physical control of a parked vehicle are both covered by the DUI law, under two separate sections, RCW forty-six point six one.five hundred two and RCW forty-six point six one.five hundred three.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: What chemical-testing agreement does every person automatically accept simply by driving on Washington roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Under the Implied Consent Law, RCW forty-six point two zero.three hundred eight, anyone who drives in Washington has agreed to be tested whenever an officer suspects alcohol or drug impairment.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: What blood alcohol concentration triggers DUI at age twenty-one and up versus under age twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: A blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or higher is DUI for drivers aged twenty-one and older, while drivers under twenty-one face the same consequences at zero point zero two percent.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What active blood THC level triggers DUI for drivers twenty-one and older compared with drivers under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: More than five nanograms of active THC per milliliter of blood is DUI for drivers aged twenty-one and older, while drivers under twenty-one face the same consequences for anything above zero nanograms.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Which exact BAC and active-THC pairs appear in the Washington guide's limits table for adults versus minors?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: The guide's limits table lists adults at a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or more and THC of five point zero zero ng or more, and minors under twenty-one at a BAC of zero point zero two percent or more and THC above zero point zero zero ng.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Which age group faces the tighter Washington alcohol ceiling—zero point zero eight or zero point zero two?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The alcohol limit is zero point zero eight percent for drivers twenty-one and older but zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one, so the younger limit is the stricter one.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Why is Washington's under-twenty-one cannabis driving threshold described as a zero-tolerance standard?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The THC limit is more than five nanograms per milliliter of blood for drivers twenty-one and older but anything above zero for drivers under twenty-one, which is a zero-tolerance rule.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: For how long can refusing an officer's impairment check cost your driving privilege?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Refusing a test can cost your driving privilege for ninety to seven hundred thirty days or until you turn twenty-one, whichever is longer, with the length depending on factors such as how many violations you have.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: When someone under twenty-one refuses an impairment check, does the day-count or birthday cutoff end first or last?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Refusing an impairment test can cost your driving privilege for ninety to seven hundred thirty days, or until age twenty-one, whichever is longer, depending on factors such as prior violations.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: How long do alcohol and drug driving offenses remain on your Washington record, and what fallout follows a DUI arrest?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Alcohol and drug offenses stay on your driving record for life, and a DUI arrest can bring license loss, heavy fines, criminal penalties, jail time and higher insurance rates.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Alongside a ninety-day-to-four-year suspension, which four monitoring, insurance, and treatment conditions can follow a DUI conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: A DUI conviction can combine a suspension of ninety days to four years with a probationary license, an ignition interlock device, proof of financial responsibility, and an alcohol assessment and treatment report.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: What suspension window applies to driving privileges after a Washington DUI conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Penalties for a driving under the influence conviction can include suspending driving privileges for ninety days to four years.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: What three licensing steps can DOL require before restoring privileges after a DUI conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: A DUI conviction can also require you to reapply for a license, retake the knowledge and skills tests, and pay the reissue fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: Which three actions involving alcohol or cannabis inside a vehicle violate Washington's open container law?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: The open container law makes it a traffic infraction for anyone in a vehicle on the road to drink alcohol or use cannabis, hold opened or partly used alcohol or cannabis, or hide either in unlabeled or mislabeled containers.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Where is the only legal place to transport previously opened alcohol or cannabis—and what cabin spots are barred?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Opened alcohol or cannabis may be carried only in the trunk or a truck bed, never in a storage compartment the driver can reach.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Does stashing a recorked bottle or opened cannabis pouch in a closed cabin compartment satisfy Washington law?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Opened alcohol or cannabis may ride only in the trunk or truck bed, so no storage compartment within the driver's reach qualifies.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Beyond standard cross streets, which everyday junctions and entrances legally count as intersections in Washington?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: An intersection is any spot where two or more roads meet, including cross streets, roundabouts, calming circles, side streets, driveways and shopping center or parking lot entrances.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Does an intersection lose its legal crosswalk status when no white stripes are painted across the asphalt?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.memory_hook: Every corner counts, painted or bare
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Every intersection is legally a crosswalk, whether or not a crosswalk is painted.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which stops, yields, multi-way glances, and mirror-plus-shoulder checks precede entering a Washington intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Before entering an intersection, stop and yield to pedestrians and traffic in it, look each way multiple times, and check side mirrors and over your shoulder for any cyclist, motorcyclist, or pedestrian entering your path.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: How should you handle a cross street when parked cars or hedges block your sightline at the stop line?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: If your view of the cross street is blocked after stopping at the stop line, creep forward slowly until you can see, which also lets crossing drivers spot your front end first.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: In what exact order do stopping at the line and creeping forward happen at a sight-blocked corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Stopping at the stop line comes first, and creeping slowly forward is a second step used only when the view of the cross street is still blocked.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What far-side space check must pass before you pull into an intersection or start a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Do not start across or into a turn unless there is room to finish without blocking the intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Around which seven busy community and commercial spots must your intersection scan widen with extra care?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Scan the whole area around an intersection with extra care near shopping centers, parking lots, construction, busy sidewalks, playgrounds, parks and schoolyards.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What job do right-of-way rules perform at junctions, and what does the law mean by yielding?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Right-of-way rules set the order in which vehicles move through an intersection, and the law decides who must yield, meaning give it up.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Who moves first at a four-way stop, and how does Washington break a simultaneous arrival tie?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrived, and when two arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left yields to the one on the right.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Does yielding to the right govern every four-way stop sequence or only simultaneous arrivals?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: At a four-way stop the first to arrive goes first, and only a near tie is settled by yielding to the vehicle on your right.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: At a four-way stop, which opposing movements outrank a driver preparing to turn left?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: At a four-way stop, a driver turning left must yield to vehicles going straight or turning right.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Between a driver continuing straight and a driver turning at a two-way stop, who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: At a two-way stop, the vehicle going straight has the right-of-way and turning vehicles must yield to it.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How do turning yield duties compare between a four-way stop and a two-way stop?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: A left-turning driver yields to straight and right-turning traffic at a four-way stop, while at a two-way stop any turning driver yields to the one going straight.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Into which lane must every Washington left or right turn finish, and when can you shift lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Washington law requires you to turn, left or right, into the lane nearest the direction you are coming from, and you may change lanes only after finishing the turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What lane discipline is required throughout an intersection equipped with multiple side-by-side turn lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: With more than one turn lane, stay in the same lane through the whole turn so you never drift into the next lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: How far ahead must you signal before turning across oncoming lanes, and what must be clear first?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet before turning left or right across oncoming traffic, then wait for a safe gap and check that the street you are entering is clear of vehicles, walkers and bicyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: What minimum signal distance and finishing-lane rule pair together on turns across oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Signaling one hundred feet ahead is the minimum before a turn across oncoming traffic, and the turn itself must end in the lane nearest your starting side, with lane changes only afterward.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: Why must you check behind you and yield to approaching bicyclists before turning?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Check behind you for bicyclists and yield to them before you turn, since they may be closing on you faster than you think.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: When are U-turns legal in Washington, and which two terrain features always rule one out?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: In Washington a U-turn is generally legal unless a sign forbids it, but you need clear sight in every direction, so never make one on a curve or near the top of a hill.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Even without a No U-Turn sign posted, why do curves and approaching hilltops forbid turning around?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: U-turns in Washington are allowed by default unless a sign bans them, yet a curve or an approaching hilltop still rules one out because you cannot see in every direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What defines a cross intersection, and how can traffic be controlled there?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: A four-way junction carrying at least one lane in each direction is called a cross intersection; it may be controlled by lights, signs or markings, and you apply the right-of-way laws there.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How is a T-intersection laid out, and which road holds right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: A T-intersection is a three-way junction where one road ends at a through road, and a yield or stop sign there shows that through traffic has the right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Who holds priority where a minor road angles into a major highway at a Y-intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: At a Y-intersection a minor road joins a major route, often with a stop sign on the minor road, and cars on the major road have the right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: What shared priority principle links T-intersections and Y-intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: At a T-intersection the through road has priority, and at a Y-intersection the major road has priority, so in both the driver on the ending or minor road waits.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Who holds right-of-way at a marked mid-block crosswalk even when no stop sign stands beside it?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: At a mid-block crosswalk, pedestrians in a marked crosswalk always have the right-of-way, and drivers should stop for walkers and bicyclists even with no stop sign.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: How do cars circulate around a traffic calming circle, how are approaches signed, and which rules govern priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: A traffic calming circle has a painted or raised center island that traffic circles counterclockwise, may post stop or yield signs on every approach, a few of them or none, and uses the ordinary right-of-way rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What unusual path might fire engines, buses, or delivery trucks need inside a small neighborhood calming circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Calming circles are built for passenger cars, so give fire trucks, buses and delivery trucks room, since they may need to go clockwise around the island.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Which two traits set a neighborhood calming circle apart from a full highway roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: A calming circle uses ordinary intersection right-of-way rules and may have no signs at all, and large vehicles there may even circle clockwise.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: How does entry and travel direction work at a roundabout, and which road users is it built to handle?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: In a roundabout every approaching vehicle yields on entry and then travels counterclockwise around a raised center island, and roundabouts are designed to serve cars, large trucks, buses, bicyclists and pedestrians alike.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Why must you hang well back from semi-trucks inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Large vehicles may drive over a roundabout's truck apron and use both lanes, so give them plenty of space and stay well back from trucks.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Which two ways may a bicyclist navigate a roundabout, and where should a lane-riding cyclist position?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: A bicyclist may ride through a roundabout either as a pedestrian or as a vehicle, and when riding as a vehicle should take the middle of the lane to be seen.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: For what low speed range are Washington roundabouts engineered?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Slow down as you approach, because roundabouts are designed for speeds of fifteen to twenty-five miles per hour

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: When do you select your roundabout lane, and how do you handle lane changes once circling?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Use the lane choice sign to pick your lane for a right turn, going straight or a left turn before you enter, then stay in that lane until you leave the roundabout.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Walk through the crosswalk, look, yield, and steering sequence for entering and exiting a roundabout?
