sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Stop for pedestrians and bicyclists in the crosswalks on both entry and exit, look left and yield to all traffic already circulating, then enter to the right going counterclockwise when there is a gap.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Which direction do you yield before entering a roundabout, and what lane rule governs you inside?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Entering a roundabout you look left and yield to traffic already circling, and once inside you hold your lane until your exit rather than changing lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What should you do if an ambulance or fire truck approaches while you are already inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, drive on through it and then pull over, as at any other intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: Why must you continue out of a roundabout before pulling over for flashing emergency lights?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: In a roundabout, an approaching emergency vehicle means continue through and then pull over, not stop in the circle.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: How does a diverging diamond interchange reroute traffic, and what safety benefit does that create?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: A diverging diamond is a newer Washington interchange that shifts traffic to the opposite side of the road so left turns onto and off freeway ramps flow better, with fewer crossing points and less crash risk.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: How do signals and paint guide you through a diverging diamond, including freeway left turns and exiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: In a diverging diamond, markings and signals guide you to the left side of the road, you turn left onto the freeway without stopping or yielding to oncoming traffic, and you cross back to the right after the overpass or underpass.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Why doesn't a left turn onto a freeway ramp inside a diverging diamond require stopping for oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: In a diverging diamond the left turn onto the freeway needs no stop and no yielding to oncoming traffic, because the design removes conflicts with oncoming vehicles, though you still follow the signs and markings.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: What defines an uncontrolled intersection, where do they usually appear, and do right-of-way laws still apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: An uncontrolled intersection has no signs, the normal right-of-way rules still apply, and such intersections are usually on local roads and streets.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: In which four situations must you yield when approaching an unsigned, uncontrolled Washington intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection you must yield if a vehicle is already in it, if you are entering or crossing a state highway from a secondary road, if you are moving from an unpaved to a paved road, or if you are turning left with a vehicle coming from the opposite direction.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: At an uncontrolled intersection, who yields when a secondary or gravel road meets a state highway or paved street?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection the driver coming from a secondary or unpaved road yields to the one on the state highway or paved road.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: What five traffic jobs do painted pavement lines, arrows, words, and symbols handle?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Painted road markings (lines, arrows, words and symbols) divide lanes, show where passing or lane changes are allowed, mark turn lanes and walkways, and show where to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Which two boundaries does a solid white edge line mark along the roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.memory_hook: Marks road edge and bike lane
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: A solid white line marks the edge of the road and also separates a bike lane from motor traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Where must you position your vehicle when driving along an unmarked roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.memory_hook: No paint means keep far right
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: On a road with no markings at all, keep as far to the right as you safely can.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in the traffic directions they separate?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.memory_hook: Yellow splits opposite, white splits same
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines divide lanes moving the same way.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How can you tell from lane and center stripes whether a street carries one-way or two-way traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: White and yellow lane or center lines show whether traffic moves in one or two directions: yellow separates opposite-direction traffic and white separates same-direction lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What warning do shorter, closer-spaced dashed white lines give about your current lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.memory_hook: Short white dashes mean lane ending
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Short dashed white lines warn that your lane is ending, so you must merge or exit.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How do standard dashed white lines differ in meaning from shorter dashed white lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.memory_hook: Standard allows changes, short warns merge
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Ordinary dashed white lines can be crossed when safe, but the shorter dashed white lines warn that your own lane is about to end.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: What three forms can a roadway median take, and is driving on or across one ever legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.memory_hook: Open, concrete, or painted; never cross
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: A median can be an open space, a cement divider, or eighteen-inch solid yellow pavement markings with stripes, and driving within, over or across any median is illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: When are you allowed to cross a dashed white line separating two lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: You may cross a dashed white line between lanes to change lanes when it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What does a single solid white line between same-direction lanes instruct you to do?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.memory_hook: Single solid white means stay put
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A single solid white line tells you to stay in your lane unless a special situation forces a change.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What rule applies wherever double solid white lines separate two lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Double solid white lines act as a barrier between lanes, and crossing them is illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does lane-changing permission step down across dashed, single solid, and double solid white lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.memory_hook: Dashed change, single stay, double illegal
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Dashed white permits a safe lane change, single solid white asks you to stay put except in a special situation, and double solid white makes crossing illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What passing maneuver does a single dashed yellow centerline permit on a two-lane road?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.memory_hook: Pass in oncoming lane when safe
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: A dashed yellow centerline on a two-way, two-lane road means you may use the oncoming lane to pass when it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What two things can a single solid yellow line mark, and may you cross it to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: A solid yellow line can mark the road edge or a no-passing zone, and you must not cross it to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What passing rule applies when double solid yellow lines run down the middle of a roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.memory_hook: Neither direction may cross to pass
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Double solid yellow centerlines mean no passing for traffic in either direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: When a solid yellow stripe and a dashed yellow stripe sit side by side, how do you know who can pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.memory_hook: Dashed your side passes, solid waits
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Where a solid and a dashed yellow line run side by side, you may not pass if the solid line is on your side, but may pass when safe if the dashed line is on your side.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How does a dashed yellow centerline contrast with single or double solid yellow lines for passing?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.memory_hook: Dashed yellow allows, solid yellow bans
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: A dashed yellow centerline allows passing when safe, while a single solid yellow line or double solid yellow lines forbid passing.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Along a mixed solid-and-dashed yellow centerline, which stripe governs your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.memory_hook: Obey the stripe touching your lane
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: With one solid and one dashed yellow line, the line on your own side decides: solid means no passing for you, dashed means you may pass when safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Once you pull into a marked intersection turn lane, what are you legally required to do?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.memory_hook: Enter turn lane, complete the turn
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Once you enter a marked turn lane, which is usually found at a major intersection, you must complete the turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Are you allowed to cross the solid exterior yellow stripe to enter a center lane painted with left-turn arrows?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.memory_hook: Yes, cross into center turn lane
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: You are allowed to cross the solid yellow line on your side to move into a center lane marked with left turn arrows.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: How does the rule against crossing solid yellow to pass interact with entering an arrow-marked center turn lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.memory_hook: Bans passing, allows center turn entry
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: A solid yellow line on your side bans passing, but you may still cross it to enter a center lane marked with left turn arrows.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Which maneuvers are legal inside a shared two-way center lane, and what oncoming hazard exists there?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.memory_hook: Left turns and legal U-turns only
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: A shared center lane is only for left turns in either direction, into or out of the roadway, or for U-turns where they are permitted, and oncoming drivers may be using it too.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What passing rule and maximum travel distance apply inside a shared center turn lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.memory_hook: Never pass; three hundred feet max
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Never pass in a shared center lane, and do not drive more than three hundred feet in it.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Why must you keep your stay inside a shared center lane brief and never use it to overtake traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.memory_hook: Turn only, stay under three-hundred feet
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: A shared center lane is for turning, never for passing, and you should not stay in it longer than three hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Which vehicles are HOV lanes built for, and what symbol and stripe set them apart?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: HOV lanes are for carpools, vanpools and buses, carry a diamond symbol on signs and pavement, and are set off from other lanes by a solid white line.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: What rider count is needed to enter an HOV lane, and which two-wheeled vehicle qualifies automatically?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.memory_hook: Meet posted rider count, or motorcycle
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: To use an HOV lane your vehicle must meet the occupancy posted on the signs, and motorcycles may use it as well.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What makes a roadway lane a reserved lane, and what is a common transit example?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Reserved lanes are set aside by signs or pavement markings for a special use, such as a transit lane that only buses may use.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which four vehicle types ride free in express toll and HOT lanes, and how can a solo car driver use them?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Express toll and high occupancy toll lanes are free for buses, vanpools, carpools and motorcycles, while a solo driver may pay the toll for a faster trip.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What account does the Washington driver guide recommend for paying state tolls automatically at the lowest rate?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.memory_hook: Good To Go saves money automatically
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: The guide recommends a Good To Go! account as the best way to pay Washington tolls, since it saves money on every state toll road and pays automatically.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Inside an express toll or high-occupancy toll lane, which drivers actually pay the toll?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: In an express or high occupancy toll lane the toll is only for drivers who do not qualify for the free ride that buses, vanpools, carpools and motorcycles get.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Why do reversible lanes flip traffic direction, and when do they typically open?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.memory_hook: Flips direction for commutes or events
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Reversible lanes switch direction to add capacity, usually on fixed commute schedules, and may also open for major events or incidents.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What pavement stripes typically border a reversible lane, and what must you check before entering?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Reversible lanes are usually marked with double-dashed white lines, so check the overhead signs before driving in one.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Above a reversible lane, what do a green arrow, a red X, and a steady yellow X each command?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.memory_hook: Green go, red blocked, yellow vacate
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Over a reversible lane, a green arrow means you may use it, a red X means you may not, and a steady yellow X means it is changing direction so you should leave it as soon as safely possible.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Between double-dashed pavement paint and overhead lane signals, which one tells you whether a reversible lane is open right now?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Reversible lanes are usually marked with double-dashed white lines, but the overhead signals, not the paint, tell you whether you may use the lane right now.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: How does a red X above a reversible lane differ in urgency from a steady yellow X?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.memory_hook: Red bars entry, yellow clears lane
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: A red X over a reversible lane bars you from it, while a steady yellow X means the lane is switching direction and you should get out of it soon and safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: At a crosswalk, when does your legal duty to yield to a pedestrian begin?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.memory_hook: Yield inside or stepping into crosswalk
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: You must yield to anyone in a crosswalk or about to step into one.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: What must you do when pedestrian-activated lights embedded in a crosswalk start flashing?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Some crosswalks have in-pavement lights that pedestrians switch on, and you must yield while those lights flash.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: Does an intersection still count legally as a crosswalk when no white crosswalk lines are painted?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: An intersection counts legally as a crosswalk even where no crosswalk is painted.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: How are standard bike lanes and buffered bike lanes marked on the pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.memory_hook: Solid white, bike symbol, crosshatched buffer
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Bike lanes are marked with solid white lines and bike symbols, and some add a buffer of two solid white lines with diagonal crosshatching between them.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: What part of the road does a crosshatched bike buffer belong to, and when is a car allowed to cross it?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.memory_hook: Part of bike lane; turns only
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: A crosshatched bike lane buffer belongs to the bike lane, so enter it only to make a legal turn after checking it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: Where must your front bumper stop when approaching a stop sign or red light with a painted stop line or crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.memory_hook: Stop before stop line or crosswalk
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: At a stop sign or signal with a stop line, stop before your vehicle reaches the line, or the crosswalk if there is one.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: How are fire lanes marked, where might cities paint them, and what two actions are banned there?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.memory_hook: Red markings; zero parking or stopping
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: Fire lanes, usually marked by red stripes or a red curb and sometimes painted in front of fire stations, are places where you may not park or stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: What do diagonal yellow stripes painted across a patch of pavement tell drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: Yellow stripes painted on the pavement mark an area where you may not drive.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: Why is sitting at the wheel inside a fire lane still illegal, and where besides red curbs do fire lanes appear?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.memory_hook: Bans stopping too, including station fronts
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: A fire lane forbids stopping as well as parking, and some communities paint one on the road in front of a fire station, not only along a red curb.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: What does a painted bicycle sharrow mean, and how much space must you leave when passing a cyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.memory_hook: Shared lane; pass with three feet
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: A sharrow marks a lane shared with bicycles, so slow down, watch for riders and leave at least three feet when passing one.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: What turn restriction and stopping rule apply when you approach an intersection painted with a bicycle box?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.memory_hook: No right on red; cyclists first
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: Near a bicycle box you may not turn right on red, and you must wait behind the white line until the box is clear because cyclists go first on green.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: What is Washington's school-zone speed limit around schools and playgrounds, and how are these zones marked?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.memory_hook: Twenty miles per hour near schools
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: The school zone speed limit is twenty miles per hour on the roads around a school or playground, which may be marked by signs, pavement markings and flashing lights.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: Where does the twenty-mile-per-hour school limit apply, and how do you know which hours enforce it?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: The twenty miles per hour school zone limit covers the roads near a school building or playground, and posted signs may clarify the times when it applies.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: Why must you still slow down through a highway work zone even when no road crew is visible?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.memory_hook: Always slow; narrow lanes, rough road
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: In a work zone always slow down, even when no workers are present, because lanes are narrower and pavement can be rough.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: What hazards should you scan for entering a work zone, and how should your focus and following gap adjust?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.memory_hook: Drop distractions, add gap, expect stops
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: Approaching a work zone, watch for signs, cones, barrels, big vehicles and crew, cut distractions, lengthen your following distance and be ready to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: Until which sign must you obey work-zone restrictions, and when do work zones demand extra caution?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.memory_hook: Obey until End Road Work sign
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: Keep obeying posted work zone signs until you pass the End Road Work sign, and take extreme care in work zones at night.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: What kind of roadside situation creates an emergency zone in Washington?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: An emergency zone forms around an unplanned roadside event needing immediate attention, such as a crash, a broken-down vehicle or a person in distress.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What personal identifier appears on every Washington license, permit, and ID card—and what letters often start it?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Every Washington license, permit and ID card carries a personal Washington number that often starts with the letters WDL.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: What is Washington's secure online DOL portal called, and why must every new driver open their own profile?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: License Express is the secure DOL website, and each new driver must open an account in their own name because services cannot be obtained through someone else's account.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How many listed residency conditions—such as keeping a home, voting, filing taxes, or state aid—trigger Washington resident status?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: You count as a Washington resident when any single listed condition applies, such as keeping a home here for personal use, being registered to vote here, filing taxes with a Washington address, or receiving state public assistance.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: How many days does a licensed newcomer aged eighteen or older have to obtain a Washington driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: A new resident aged eighteen or older who is licensed in another state has thirty days to get a Washington driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What must a new Washington resident pass if their out-of-state driver license has already expired?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: If a new resident's out-of-state license has expired, they must pass both the knowledge exam and the skills exam before Washington will license them.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which Washington license does a licensed newcomer under eighteen apply for, and what two items must DOL verify?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A new resident under eighteen with another state's license applies for a Washington Intermediate Driver License, and DOL must approve their driver education and confirm at least six months of instruction-permit time.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: How does Washington's transfer path for a licensed adult newcomer differ from a licensed newcomer under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: A licensed adult newcomer gets thirty days to switch to a Washington license, while a newcomer under eighteen must enter the intermediate license system instead.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Is REAL ID a single card or a federal law, what Washington credential satisfies it, and where do standard cards fail?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: REAL ID is a law rather than a card, and an enhanced license or ID is one of several options that satisfy it; a standard license will no longer be accepted at airport security, border crossings or secure federal buildings.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What personal DOL identifier must you obtain before submitting an instruction permit application?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: You must already have a WDL number before you apply for an instruction permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: How young can you apply for an instruction permit when enrolled in driver training, and what is the pre-class window?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: When you enroll in driver training you may apply for a permit as young as fifteen, online or at an office, from one to ten days before the course starts.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: At what age may you test for a permit without taking driver training, and when can you take the skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Without driver training you may take the knowledge exam after turning fifteen and a half and get the permit once you pass, but the skills exam and license must wait until you are eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: How long does a Washington instruction permit stay valid compared with a passing knowledge exam score?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: An instruction permit is valid for one year and can be renewed for a fee, while a passing knowledge exam score stays valid for two years.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: By how much time does enrolling in a driver training course beat the non-course path for getting a permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: The permit age with a driver training course is fifteen, while the permit age through the knowledge exam without a course is fifteen and a half, so the course path starts half a year sooner.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Between your instruction permit and your passing knowledge exam score, which expires in one year and which in two?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The permit itself lasts one year, but the knowledge exam score lasts two years, so the two expiry periods must not be swapped.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which four core age, residency, permit-time, and schooling milestones unlock a first license at sixteen or seventeen?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: To get a first license at sixteen or seventeen you must have held the permit for at least six months, be at least sixteen, live in Washington, and complete a traffic safety course at an approved driver training school.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What minimum classroom and behind-the-wheel hours must an out-of-state safety course meet to count in Washington?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: A traffic safety course finished in another state counts only if it meets Washington's minimum of thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How many day and night practice hours must a teen log, beside whom, and who attests to them?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: A teen applicant must log at least forty hours of daytime and ten hours of nighttime driving beside a licensed driver with three or more years of experience, attested by a parent, guardian or responsible adult.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: What ticket, conviction, and substance record must a teen hold before applying for an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: A teen applicant must go six months with no traffic violations or convictions before applying, and must have no alcohol or drug offenses while driving on the permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which two facts does a parent or guardian certify when signing a teen's in-person authorization form?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: For an in-person teen application a parent or guardian signs an authorization form certifying at least fifty hours of driving experience and no traffic infractions or violations during the previous six months.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How many years of licensed driving experience must a teen's practice supervisor hold?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: Teen applicants ages sixteen to seventeen must complete at least forty hours of day driving and ten hours of night driving with a licensed driver who has three or more years of experience, attested to by a parent, guardian, or responsible adult.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How do Washington's daytime and nighttime teen practice minimums connect to the parent authorization total?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: The forty daytime plus ten nighttime practice hours add up to the fifty hours that the parent or guardian certifies on the authorization form.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Within what timeframe must a driver training school upload a teen's passing exam results into DOL's system?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Once a teen passes each exam, the driver training school has twenty-four hours to record the scores in the DOL system.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: How long does the temporary license issued at a licensing office stay valid while your plastic card mails out?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: An in-person applicant leaves the office with a temporary license good for forty-five days, and the official card arrives later by mail.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: When a teen completes licensing online, what acts as the temporary license—and why does it fail as ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: When a teen completes the license online, the printed receipt is the temporary license, but it carries no photo and so cannot serve as identification.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does an in-person forty-five-day temporary license compare with an online license receipt?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: The in-person temporary license lasts forty-five days, while the online receipt also acts as a temporary license but cannot be used as identification because it has no photo.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: What four licensing pathways exist for an adult first-time Washington applicant?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: An adult first-time applicant has four routes: transfer another state's license, pass both exams, pass the knowledge exam and practice on a permit beside a licensed driver with five or more years of experience before the skills exam, or use an exam waiver to get a permit and finish a training course before both exams.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: When an adult eighteen or older practices on an instruction permit, how much experience must their supervising driver have?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: An adult age eighteen or older choosing the permit option passes the knowledge exam, gets a permit, practices driving with a licensed driver who has five or more years of experience, and then passes the skills exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: What happens if your DOL vision screening shows you need glasses or contact lenses to see clearly?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: DOL screens your vision before issuing a license, and if you need glasses or contacts that requirement is noted on the license, so wear them every time you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: What extra credential must be added to your personal license before operating a motorcycle or commercial motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: Driving a motorcycle or a commercial motor vehicle requires an extra endorsement added to your personal driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Through which two restricted stages do sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds progress before earning an unrestricted license?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Drivers aged sixteen and seventeen move through two restricted phases, first the instruction permit and then the intermediate driver license, before they hold an unrestricted license.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: During the first six months of an intermediate license, which passengers under age twenty are allowed in your car?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: In the first six months of an intermediate license you may not carry any passenger under age twenty unless that person is an immediate family member.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: After your first six intermediate months—until age eighteen or one year—how many non-family passengers under twenty may ride?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: After those first six months, and until you turn eighteen or reach one year on the license, whichever is first, you may carry no more than three passengers under age twenty who are not immediate family.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Between which early-morning hours is solo intermediate driving barred, who can accompany you, and when does curfew lift?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: An intermediate driver may not drive from one a.m. to five a.m. unless a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least twenty-five rides along, and this night limit ends after one year of safe driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: May an intermediate license holder talk or text using hands-free dashboard Bluetooth—and what lone exception exists?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Intermediate license holders may not use a cell phone or wireless device while driving, even hands-free, except to report an emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: How does the non-family under-twenty passenger cap change after the first six months on an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: In the first six months of an intermediate license no passenger under twenty is allowed except immediate family, whereas afterwards up to three such passengers are allowed.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: In Washington's intermediate rules, how does the age-twenty cutoff differ in purpose from the age-twenty-five cutoff?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The passenger limit age is under twenty, but the night-hours escort must be a parent, guardian or licensed driver at least twenty-five, so the two ages answer different questions.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What happens after a first, second, and third violation or at-fault crash on an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: For an intermediate driver, a first violation or at-fault collision keeps the current restrictions until age eighteen, a second brings a six-month suspension or suspension until eighteen if that comes sooner, and a third suspends the license until eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does the suspension length on a second intermediate violation differ from a third violation?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: A second intermediate violation brings a six-month suspension or suspension until eighteen, whichever ends first, while a third suspends the license all the way to eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Under which two circumstances may an intermediate holder drive at any hour carrying passengers?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: An intermediate driver may drive at any hour with passengers when the trip is for agricultural purposes, or after one year with no crash and no traffic offense.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: Do you need to visit DOL for a brand-new card to drop intermediate restrictions when you turn eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Intermediate restrictions drop away automatically at eighteen, so no new license is required then, and an updated card can wait until renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: To which age group does DOL mail an early warning letter after a first moving ticket—and why?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: DOL mails an early warning letter to drivers aged eighteen to twenty-one after their first moving violation, because a driver's crash risk doubles after that first violation.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: What driving does a Washington agricultural permit authorize under eighteen, and what is its minimum age?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: An agricultural permit lets a driver under eighteen drive within a set area for farm work, and the juvenile agricultural permit has no minimum age.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Does holding an agricultural permit replace an instruction permit or waive practice hours for your first license?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: An agricultural permit never substitutes for an instruction permit and does not waive any requirement for a first Washington license, including practice driving.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: What is the key trade-off between a juvenile agricultural permit and a standard instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: An agricultural permit allows farm-work driving in a set area with no minimum age, but unlike the instruction permit it does not count toward a first license.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What single habit is the most effective way to protect yourself and cut fatal-injury risk in a crash?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Wearing a seat belt correctly is the single most effective way to protect yourself and sharply cuts your risk of a fatal injury in a crash.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Where must the shoulder strap and lap belt sit — and which three shoulder-belt placements are off-limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: The shoulder belt goes snugly across the middle of the chest and shoulder, never behind your back, under your arm, or across the neck or face, and the lap belt holds the hips snugly below the stomach.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Under Washington's occupant-restraint statutes, who inside a moving vehicle must be belted or in an approved child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Under RCW forty-six point six one.six hundred eighty-seven and RCW forty-six point six one.six hundred eighty-eight, all occupants of a moving vehicle need a fastened seat belt or an approved child restraint, and driving or riding without one is illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Which six strap, knee, foot, and headrest checks confirm proper seating and seat-belt fit?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Check that the belt is not twisted, the lap portion sits on the upper thighs and the cross strap falls over mid-shoulder, with knees bending at the seat edge, feet on the floor and headrest in line with your ears.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Match the headrest, lap belt, and cross strap to the exact body landmark each must align with?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: The headrest lines up with your ears, while the lap belt rests on the upper thighs and the cross strap on mid-shoulder, three separate fit checks.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which safety standards and dual instructions govern child restraints — and who can inspect your setup?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Child restraints must meet Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards and be installed following both the vehicle and the seat maker's instructions, and a certified child passenger safety technician can check the installation.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How long should a child remain in each restraint stage, and how must children under age two ride?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Keep a child in each restraint stage as long as that seat allows, and a child from birth until age two must use a car seat that faces the rear.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What restraint requirement and facing options apply to children aged two through four?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Children aged two to four must ride in a car seat with a harness, which may face either rearward or forward.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: From age four onward, what height and age window typically require a car or booster seat until adult belts fit?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Children aged four and older stay in a car or booster seat until the vehicle's lap and shoulder belts fit properly, usually between ages eight and twelve, and the booster stage covers kids from four years old up to a height of four feet nine inches.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: What must riders taller than four feet nine inches wear once old enough for an adult seat belt?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Anyone taller than four feet nine inches who is old enough for a seat belt must wear a properly fitting belt.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Why is riding unbelted dangerous around airbags, and which age group belongs strictly out of the front seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Airbags work together with seat belts, so an unbelted occupant risks serious injury or death when an airbag deploys, and children under thirteen should never ride in the front seat.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does age four serve as the handoff between Washington's harnessed-seat stage and booster-seat stage?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Children aged two to four ride in a harnessed car seat, while from age four they move to a car or booster seat until the adult belt fits, so the harness stage and the booster stage meet at age four.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Contrast what lets a child graduate from a booster seat against Washington's front-seat age rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Leaving the booster depends on belt fit and a height over four feet nine inches, typically between ages eight and twelve, whereas the front-seat rule is a separate age line of under thirteen.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Where on the steering-wheel rim — and at which clock numbers — should your hands rest for maximum control?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: For the best control, hold the outside of the wheel on its top half, picturing the wheel as a clock face with hands at about nine and three.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Which five driving situations call for hand-over-hand steering, and how do your arms execute and finish the turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Hand-over-hand steering, starting from nine and three or ten and two, is for low-speed turns, limited visibility, intersections, parking and skid recovery: reach one arm across the other, pull, release the lower hand, and straighten the wheel as the turn ends.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: When is one-hand steering appropriate, and for what single maneuver is twelve o'clock hand placement recommended?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Use one-hand steering when backing up or when you must reach for controls such as wipers, flashers or lights, and the twelve o'clock hand position is recommended only for backing while you turn your body to look behind.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: What two safety advantages come from hand-to-hand push-pull steering never crossing arms or releasing the rim?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Hand-to-hand steering never crosses the arms and never lets go of the wheel, so the arms stay out of the airbag area and corrections can be made instantly.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Contrast the twelve o'clock one-hand grip with the hand positions used for normal forward driving?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: One-hand steering with the hand at twelve is recommended only when backing, which differs from the nine and three or ten and two positions used for forward driving.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Which four braking-pressure levels does the Washington guide name, and how do you master picking the right one?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: The guide names four braking levels, light, medium, firm and emergency, and judging the right pressure is a skill that grows with practice in your vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Which two braking levels should handle everyday driving, what mental picture guides smooth stops, and why skip sudden stops?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Aim to need only light and medium braking, brake as if a cup of water sat in your lap, and avoid needless hard stops that could surprise drivers behind you.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: During an emergency stop, what control benefit does ABS give, what does it NOT shorten, and how does the car feel?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: An antilock brake system lets you keep steering during an emergency stop but does not shorten your stopping distance, and you may feel the car shake when it engages.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Where should a new driver practice firm or emergency braking to experience how ABS feels?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Practice firm or emergency braking in a large open paved area to feel the ABS stop the wheels from locking.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Summarize the three test facts about Antilock Brake Systems during hard emergency stops?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: An Antilock Brake System lets drivers keep better steering control during emergency braking without shortening stopping distance, and the vehicle may shake slightly when it engages.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: How does the cup-of-water image guide acceleration across creeping traffic versus dodging a hazard?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Smooth acceleration follows the same cup-of-water idea, ranging from simply easing off the brake in stop-and-go traffic to speeding up quickly to avoid a hazard.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: Why does even weight across all four tires matter, and which three upkeep habits preserve it?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Keeping weight evenly spread across all tires keeps the vehicle stable, helped by regular maintenance, correct tire pressure and alignment checks.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: What is vehicle pitch, and which end takes the weight under acceleration versus hard braking?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Pitch is the forward and backward weight shift: accelerating loads the rear of the vehicle, while a sudden stop loads the front.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: What is vehicle roll — and during a left turn, onto which side does centrifugal force push the weight?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Roll is the side-to-side weight shift, and in a left turn centrifugal force pushes the weight onto the outside, or right side, of the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What is vehicle yaw, and what steering mistake triggers that rear-end zig-zag?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Yaw is the zig-zag that happens when you steer sharply from side to side, because the front wheels follow the steering while the rear may slide out of line.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Contrast the direction of weight transfer in vehicle pitch versus vehicle roll?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Pitch shifts weight front to back, so acceleration loads the rear and hard braking loads the front, unlike roll, which shifts weight side to side in turns.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Why is picking 'left side' wrong when asked where vehicle weight rolls during a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: In a left turn the weight rolls onto the right, or outside, side of the vehicle, not onto the side you are turning toward.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Which four parts of your car serve as visual reference points, and which four maneuvers do they guide?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Vehicle reference points such as the left headlight, center of the hood, side mirrors and rear bumper help you judge distance when parking, turning, backing and stopping.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: How close is your front bumper to an intersection stop line when that painted line appears right under your side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: When the stop line appears under your side mirror at an intersection, your front end is roughly three to six inches from that line.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: How far is your car from the lane edge when the center of your hood lines up visually with the lane stripe?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: When the center of your hood lines up with the lane marking, your vehicle is roughly three to six inches from the edge of the lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Does the side-mirror stop-line reference measure side clearance or forward bumper distance — and what is the gap?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: The side-mirror reference point is a forward check: with the stop line under the mirror, the front of the vehicle sits about three to six inches from the line.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: What vehicles can vanish completely inside your blind zones, and who bears legal responsibility for checking them?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Blind zones are areas you cannot see from the driver's seat that can fully hide a car, motorcyclist or bicyclist, and you are responsible for knowing what is in them.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: How do mirror adjustments pair with head checks — and what must your hands do while glancing over your shoulder?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Shrink blind zones by setting the rearview mirror to see out the back window without stretching and setting the side mirrors by the traditional or enhanced method, then still turn your head with the wheel held straight to check.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: Which six forward, mirror, and shoulder directions belong in a complete regular scan?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: A regular scan covers the road ahead, the rearview mirror, both side mirrors and over both shoulders.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: How do you avoid riding in other drivers' blind zones, and what are the huge blind zones around buses, RVs, and trucks called?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Stay out of other drivers' blind zones by adjusting your speed, and take extra care around buses, motor homes and commercial vehicles, whose large blind zones are called no zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: What does it mean whenever you cannot see a large truck, bus, or RV's side mirrors?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: If you cannot see a large vehicle's mirrors, its driver cannot see you.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: What two speed tweaks clear another vehicle's blind zone, and which three large vehicle types carry bigger no zones?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Other drivers' blind zones are handled by speeding up or slowing down until they can see you, and buses, motor homes and commercial vehicles have larger ones called no zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: How often must you recheck and adjust your mirrors before driving — and use them once moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Recheck and adjust your mirrors every time you get behind the wheel, and keep checking them for changes while you drive.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: Walk through the outside, cabin, cockpit-setup, and personal-readiness checks of a complete pre-drive routine?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: A good pre-drive routine checks outside the vehicle for tire debris, glass, leaks and obstacles such as children or pets, checks inside for warning lights, clear windows and secured items, confirms mirrors, seat, wheel, belt and a silenced phone, and checks that you feel healthy, focused and calm.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What three facts appear on a Washington vehicle title, and where must you never store that document?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Leaving your Certificate of Ownership inside the glovebox hands a car thief the exact document needed to forge a sale.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Must every Washington vehicle be registered with DOL—and how can someone without a driver license register one?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Every car needs DOL registration, and legally exempt non-drivers file a Driver License Exemption form instead.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: How long do new Washington residents have to register their vehicles, and how fast should an out-of-state purchase be registered?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Moving in grants a thirty-day grace window, whereas bringing home a car bought across state lines calls for immediate registration.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which two core ownership and identity items are required to register a vehicle in Washington?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Lost out-of-state titles require a replacement from that issuing state alongside a Washington license for every listed owner.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: What two steps must you take with the fresh registration slip issued each year when you renew your tabs?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Unlike your title stored safely at home, your signed annual registration belongs inside the car for traffic stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Does updating your driver license address automatically update your vehicle registration address—and where do you change it?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Assuming one address change covers both leaves tab-renewal notices mailing to your old house—update vehicle records separately.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Why must a Washington driver who moves complete two separate address updates with DOL?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Changing your driver license file leaves your vehicle registration file untouched until you update that second record.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Where must Washington plates be mounted, in what condition, and what rule governs license-plate frames?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Washington enforces front and rear plates, and decorative frames cannot touch or hide a single character or tab.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Which two immediate steps must you take when selling, trading, gifting, or disposing of a vehicle—and within how many days?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Leaving old plates attached or skipping the five-day Report of Sale leaves you billed for the buyer's tolls or impound fees.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Does filing a Report of Sale transfer ownership—and how many days does the buyer have to transfer the signed title?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Only signing and dating the title transfers ownership, and buyers waiting past fifteen days pay late-transfer penalties.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Is a car dealership legally required to file your Report of Sale on a trade-in?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Dealers may file as a courtesy without being legally bound, so submitting your own Report of Sale guarantees protection.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: After a private vehicle sale in Washington, how does the seller's filing deadline compare with the buyer's transfer deadline?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Keep those two clocks straight—five days for the seller's Report of Sale and fifteen days for the buyer's title transfer.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What coverage must Washington motorists carry, and where must proof of that coverage stay?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Driving without carried or glovebox proof of active liability insurance triggers roadside citations.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: What are Washington's three minimum dollar limits for single-person injury, multi-person injury, and property damage liability?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Memorize twenty-five thousand per person, fifty thousand for two or more hurt, and ten thousand for property.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: Across Washington's twenty-five, fifty, and ten-thousand-dollar liability minimums, which category carries the lowest dollar floor?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Hospital trauma costs dwarf fender repairs, setting injury minimums at twenty-five and fifty thousand above ten thousand for property.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: Why should you review the owner's manual and locate every control and gauge before driving a different vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Hunting for wiper switches or misunderstanding unfamiliar safety tech at sixty miles per hour pulls eyes off traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Which three cockpit items should you adjust every time you climb into a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Dialing in wheel, seat, and mirrors before shifting out of park ensures effortless pedal reach and full sightlines.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: How far should your chest sit from the steering wheel, how should your elbows bend, and where belongs your headrest?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Sitting closer than ten inches puts your chest inside an inflating airbag's punch zone, while ear-high headrests stop whiplash.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Which crash injury does the ten-inch chest gap prevent, and which crash injury does an ear-level headrest prevent?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Front spacing gives explosive airbags room to cushion safely, while rear head support catches neck snap in rear-end hits.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Who bears legal and safety responsibility for keeping a vehicle roadworthy and answering dashboard warning lights?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Ignoring dashboard warning lamps or scheduled service turns minor wear into sudden highway brake or tire failures.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What is Washington's minimum safe tire tread depth, and what happens when tires wear shallower?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Bald rubber below two thirty-seconds of an inch cannot channel rainwater away, making the car skate across wet asphalt.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Where do you look up the exact recommended air pressure for your vehicle's tires?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Tire sidewalls print maximum pressure rather than your car's handling spec—always check the driver door jamb or manual.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Which four cleaning, fluid, winter-clearing, and mirror-hanging habits keep every window clear?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped frost porthole or dangling mirror charms hides pedestrians and cross traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: Why does Washington state a single universal fraction for tire tread depth yet point you to a door label for tire pressure?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Every passenger tire hits hydroplaning danger below two thirty-seconds, whereas ideal inflation varies by vehicle weight and design.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Do Vehicle Safety Technology and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems take over legal responsibility for driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Cameras and radar assist attentive humans—they never replace eyes on the road or shift legal blame off the driver.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Name three real-world situations where blind-spot or camera driver-assist systems can miss hazards or stop working?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Muddy radar bumpers, faded lane paint, slim cyclists, or cars merging from two lanes over all fool electronic alerts.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: When is the lone time Washington's guide advises turning vehicle safety features off?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Keep active safety tech armed every day unless heavy snow or downpours trigger constant false chimes that distract you.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: How do forward collision avoidance tools work alongside adaptive cruise control?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Forward alerts and auto-braking guard against sudden obstacles while adaptive cruise slows automatically behind slower traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Which distinct hazards do lane-keeping assist, blind-spot detection, and cross-traffic alert each watch for?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Cross-traffic radar shines when backing out between tall SUVs while lane-keeping and blind-spot monitors guard highway lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What does automatic high-beam control handle, and how do pre-crash tensioners or post-collision brakes help?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Auto-dimming prevents blinding oncoming traffic, while belt pre-tensioning and post-impact braking stop secondary collisions.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: Why must you still look two lanes across before merging even when your mirror blind-spot light stays off?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Side radar watches only the neighboring lane, missing a driver two lanes away swooping into that same middle gap.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: Between which sunset and sunrise marks does Washington law mandate headlights—and when else does the guide recommend them?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Turning full headlights on thirty minutes post-sunset to pre-sunrise—and in rain, fog, snow, or smoke—keeps you visible.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: For which two lighting reasons do daytime running lights fail as a legal substitute for headlights?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Relying on daytime running lamps in rain or dusk leaves the back of your car completely unlit to trailing traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Even though daytime running lights glow automatically up front, what stays dark on your vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Drivers seeing dashboard glow often forget their rear lamps remain off until the main headlight switch turns on.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Where are high beams appropriate, and at what exact distances must you dim for oncoming versus followed vehicles?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Blinding an approaching driver head-on inside five hundred feet or flooding mirrors within three hundred feet invites crashes.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Between oncoming traffic and a vehicle you are following, which requires dimming high beams farther out—five hundred or three hundred feet?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Direct windshield glare hits oncoming eyes harder than mirror reflection, demanding the longer five-hundred-foot dim distance.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: How should you alert a trailing driver before slowing or stopping somewhere unexpected?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps three or four quick taps catches the following driver's eye before you brake hard.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: From at least how far behind your vehicle must your red brake lights be clearly visible?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Cracked, smoked, or mud-covered tail lenses that fade inside one hundred feet rob trailing traffic of stopping notice.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: How many feet ahead of a turn or lane change must you start signaling, even on an empty street—and what comes afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Signaling every time—even when nobody appears nearby—protects unseen cyclists, and canceling stops false turn cues.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Which two Washington rear-visibility and turn-communication rules share the exact one-hundred-foot figure?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Pairing one hundred feet for visible red brake lamps with one hundred feet for advance turn signals locks both in.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Using your left arm out the window, which positions signal slow-or-stop, a left turn, and a right turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Knowing left-arm hand signals backs you up if a turn bulb burns out and decodes cyclists ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: What never changes across all three Washington driver hand signals?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Every hand signal reaches out the driver's left window—only pointing down, straight, or skyward changes the message.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Under which two trouble situations should you switch on your vehicle's flashing hazard lights?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Four-way hazard flashers warn approaching traffic that your car is disabled or halted unexpectedly so drivers pass wide.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Which four personal, legal, vehicle, and emotional traits define a good driver in the Washington guide?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Knowing traffic rules means little unless paired with spatial awareness of your car and a level head.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Why should a learner practice safe habits — like over-the-shoulder blind-zone checks — with deliberate intent?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Once shoulder checks and signaling run on muscle memory, your conscious brain stays free for surprise hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: How can a bad cold, a headache or tight shoulders, and mental stress each degrade your driving — and whom should you ask?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Minor illness fogs thinking and stiff necks block shoulder checks, so consult a doctor whenever a condition worries you.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: What self-check belongs before turning the key, and what should you do if you feel unwell yet must travel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Handing the keys to a healthy driver beats pushing through fever, dizziness, or exhaustion on live roads.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: What screening must every applicant pass before Washington issues a driver license?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Clear eyesight underpins safe hazard detection, making the vision check mandatory before any license prints.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: If your license carries a corrective-lens restriction, when must you wear them — and what lens type is barred after dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Prescription sunglasses or tinted lenses starve your eyes of dim contrast at night and violate safe vision rules.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: Keep the two corrective-lens rules straight — what must stay on every drive versus what stays off after sunset?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Drivers who only pack prescription sunglasses get stuck after dusk when dark tints become unsafe.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What two crucial jobs do peripheral side vision and clear sharp sight perform while you look ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Corner-of-the-eye motion catches merging cars or kids on curbs while sharp acuity judges closing distances.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: If night driving challenges your eyes, when should you drive, and where do you look to beat oncoming headlight glare?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Guiding off the white right-edge line shields your pupils from blinding oncoming beams.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Which three night adjustments — to aim, speed, and gap — ensure you can stop within the pavement your headlights illuminate?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlight beam means an unlit fallen branch or deer appears too close to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Contrast how you beat blinding oncoming glare at night with how you keep stopping distance inside your beams?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Shifting eyes right solves temporary glare, whereas aimed lamps and lower speed solve dark stopping reach.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Which warning sounds alert drivers to trouble, how does hearing loss sneak up, and how do deaf drivers compensate?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Deaf or hard-of-hearing motorists drive safely by scanning mirrors and intersections more actively with their eyes.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What does Washington law forbid regarding earbuds, headphones, or noise-canceling headsets — and what single-ear exception exists?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Sealing off both ears with music or noise cancellation blocks emergency sirens, leaving only compliant single-ear hands-free legal.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: May a Washington instruction-permit or intermediate-license holder use a hands-free cell phone while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: New teen drivers face a total mobile-device ban behind the wheel, closing the adult hands-free allowance.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: Contrast the one-ear hands-free allowance for full-license drivers against the rule for permit and intermediate holders?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Exam questions dangle single-ear Bluetooth as bait for intermediate drivers when novices get zero mobile use.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: Beyond alcohol and drugs, what else counts under the guide's definition of impaired driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Anything that clouds clear thinking, slows reflexes, or weakens car control — including exhaustion — impairs you.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Which four financial, license, and freedom penalties hit DUI offenders — and does driving experience ever offset drinking?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Veteran drivers lose reflexes to alcohol just like beginners while facing steep fines, insurance spikes, suspension, and jail.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Which single impairing substance shows up most often in impaired-driving crashes, and how should you treat suspected impaired drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Spotting a weaving or erratic driver calls for backing way off rather than crowding beside them.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: How does alcohol change alertness, eyesight, scanning speed, multitasking, and risk confidence behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Alcohol deals a double blow — shrinking vision and lane-keeping skill while tricking your brain into feeling bold.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Which four personal and group habits keep you and your friends out of impaired-driving crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Lining up a sober ride beforehand prevents bad late-night choices and protects friends from driving impaired.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: At what age is recreational cannabis legal in Washington — and at what age or amount is driving after cannabis legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Legal store purchase at twenty-one never legalizes driving high — zero cannabis is safe behind the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Which five mental and physical driving skills degrade after using cannabis?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: THC warps time and distance perception while slowing coordination and making drivers sleepy.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Why doesn't turning twenty-one let a Washington adult drive after consuming recreational cannabis?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Driving after any cannabis stays unlawful across every age bracket regardless of adult possession laws.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Does buying a medicine legally at a pharmacy or store excuse driving impaired under Washington criminal law?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Impaired driving remains a crime whether caused by doctor prescriptions, store allergy pills, or illegal drugs.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How can everyday cold, allergy, or headache remedies and prescription medicines impair a driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Common antihistamines trigger heavy drowsiness while strong prescriptions mimic alcohol's hit to vision, judgment, and reflexes.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does Washington criminal law compare impairment from a doctor's prescription, an over-the-counter tablet, and an illegal drug?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Showing an officer a valid pill bottle never excuses weaving across lanes while medicated.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: When must you hold off driving with a medicine, and how should you read a 'heavy machinery' bottle warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: A two-ton automobile is heavy machinery, so stay off the road whenever starting a new pill or higher dose.
sec05-card-sec05-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Test new doses, machinery means cars

visual_sync.text_span: Test new doses, machinery means cars

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Why shouldn't a commuter ignore a medicine warning about 'operating heavy machinery' just because they work at a desk?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Pharmacy warning labels count your everyday car right alongside forklifts and construction rigs.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: What can happen when a mild medicine mixes with a second medicine or alcohol, and whom should you check with?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Chemical interactions amplify sedation unexpectedly, making label checks or a quick pharmacist question essential.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What is polydrug use, how do mixed substances interact, and where does it rank among fatal-crash impairments?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Combining alcohol with cannabis or pills multiplies impairment past either substance alone and tops fatal-crash toxicology.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Connect what happens when substances combine in polydrug use to its rank in deadly crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Two moderate doses stacked together overwhelm reflexes fast, making polydrug impairment number one in fatal wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Which four triggers cause driver fatigue, and how does exhaustion compare with alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Hard work, monotony, sickness, or short sleep degrades sight and judgment before putting you to sleep mid-lane.
sec05-card-sec05-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Strain or sleep loss mimics alcohol

visual_sync.text_span: Strain or sleep loss mimics alcohol

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Which memory, eye, mood, and lane-keeping clues tell you to pull off the road and rest immediately?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Forgetting recent miles, missing signs, blinking hard, tailgating, or buzzing rumble strips means microsleep is seconds away.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Alongside heavy eyelids, which three vehicle-handling mistakes warn that fatigue has already set in?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Waiting for a yawn ignores the fact that wandering lanes, crowding bumpers, and hitting rumble strips already signal danger.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: How can two drivers manage trip fatigue — and what is the fix when driving solo and feeling drowsy?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Rolling windows down or blasting music fails against sleep debt, whereas parking safely for a twenty-minute nap restores alertness.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: How many hours of sleep do most people need before a road trip, and how often should you schedule rest stops?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Starting rested on seven to nine hours plus stopping every hundred miles or two hours prevents highway fatigue.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Separate when the twenty-minute nap applies from when the hundred-mile or two-hour break rule applies?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Scheduled breaks prevent tiredness ahead of time, while a twenty-minute nap rescues a solo driver already nodding off.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: What subtle pedal habit can creep in without an anxious driver even realizing it?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Tense leg muscles push speed upward unnoticed when nerves spike, making speedometer checks helpful.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Which breathing image and two counting exercises does the guide suggest to cool down while safely parked?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Inhaling through your nose and exhaling gently or counting to twenty or backward from one hundred by threes resets calm.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: How does Washington classify aggressive driving, what intent defines it, and which six risky behaviors accompany it?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Speeding, tailgating, weaving, skipping signals, blowing controls, and crowding walkers turn impatience into purposeful endangerment.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: What core element separates aggressive driving from a simple mistake, and what offense category applies?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Forcing nearby drivers to brake or swerve to protect themselves marks deliberate aggressive driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: Which three penalties hit illegal street racing or unauthorized street demonstrations — and who besides the driver faces them?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Organizers, instigators, and helpers blocking intersections face steep fines, jail, and losing cars right alongside racers.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: How does road rage escalate past aggressive driving into a criminal offense, and what everyday pressures feed it?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Weaponizing a car or object out of traffic anger crosses straight from traffic court into criminal prosecution.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: Why does Washington treat road rage as a crime rather than a traffic ticket — and can passengers commit it?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Violent assaults with vehicles or weapons are crimes whether launched from the driver's seat or passenger window.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Which five mental or driving warning signs reveal that you are slipping into road rage yourself?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Flashing high beams, leaning on the horn, weaving, racing yellows, or brake-checking to punish someone means cool down now.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: If an angry driver targets your car, what four de-escalation and destination steps protect you?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Pulling into your own home driveway traps you alone, whereas open public businesses and calling police keep you safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Where online can you look up Washington's current rules of the road, and how long does that duty last?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Legislators update statutes over time, so claiming you learned an older rule years ago never excuses a traffic citation.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which half of a Washington roadway do you travel on, and when may a driver briefly enter the left side?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Returning promptly to the right lane after a legal two-lane pass minimizes exposure to hidden oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: On a multilane highway, how are the right and left lanes used, and does passing lift the speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Camping in the left lane clogs highway flow, and exceeding the posted limit while overtaking still earns a speeding ticket.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: May you use a carpool lane for passing, and when is driving on the shoulder ever allowed?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Weaving in and out of HOV lanes or sneaking down paved shoulders surprises high-speed traffic and stranded motorists.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Between the general left lane, a carpool lane, and a highway shoulder, which one serves passing?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Permit questions pair all three spaces to test that only the standard left travel lane serves overtaking.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Why must you continue to the next exit instead of backing up if you overshoot a freeway ramp?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Backing down a highway shoulder or travel lane invites catastrophic high-speed rear-end collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What does Washington law say about hitchhiking or stopping to pick up a hitchhiker along a freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Pedestrians on high-speed shoulders and cars braking unpredictably beside freeway lanes create lethal crash hazards.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Which three roadside categories make up traffic control devices, and whose job is obeying them?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Overlooking a painted turn arrow or regulatory sign carries the exact same legal weight as running a signal.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Which three groups of people can direct traffic in special situations, and how do their orders rank against signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Live flaggers, crossing guards, and police see immediate scene hazards that automated overhead timers cannot detect.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: How must every approaching driver treat an intersection when the overhead traffic lights go dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Blowing straight through a power-outage intersection causes T-bone wrecks when cross-street drivers expect everyone to take turns.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Why is cruising nonstop through an unlit, broken traffic signal illegal in Washington?
