sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Every dark signal defaults immediately to full stop-and-yield-right rules, even on the wider main arterial.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What does a solid red signal require, and when is turning right on red permitted?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Rolling a right-on-red without halting behind the line first is one of the top automatic ticket and test errors.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Under what street layout and conditions does Washington allow a left turn at a red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: After halting completely and checking for prohibiting signs, Washington permits turning left onto any clear one-way street.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How does a flashing red signal compare with an illuminated red arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Flashing red lets you proceed in turn after halting, whereas a steady red arrow locks down that arrow's path.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How do your movement rules differ across a solid red ball, a flashing red ball, and a red arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Sorting all three red lenses prevents waiting needlessly on flashing red or turning illegally against a red arrow.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How should you respond approaching a solid yellow signal versus already being inside the intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Flooring the gas to beat an upcoming red invites high-speed cross-traffic or left-turn collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Which roadside sign matches a flashing yellow traffic light in Washington, and how do you proceed?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Treat a flashing amber lens like a yield sign at an uncontrolled junction, moving only when right-of-way is yours.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How does a solid yellow signal's command differ from a flashing yellow signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Steady yellow announces an imminent red halt, whereas flashing yellow keeps traffic flowing under yield rules.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: If the signal turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, how should you manage your speed?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Clearing smoothly at the posted limit avoids both panic-braking in the box and reckless speeding past it.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What transition does a yellow arrow warn about, and whom must you yield to?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Protected turn time is ending, so prepare to halt rather than darting across closing oncoming headlights.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What conditions still constrain you even when your signal shows a solid green light?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Green grants permission only after clearing traffic, crossing pedestrians, and emergency vehicles have passed safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when you want to turn left on a solid circular green light?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Positioning where your sightline stays open and waiting for a true gap prevents classic left-turn T-bone crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What priority and conflict protection does an illuminated green arrow provide?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Opposing through lanes and conflicting crosswalks are held on red while your green arrow stays lit.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How does turning left on a solid green circle contrast with turning left on a green arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Mistaking a circular green ball for a protected green arrow causes instant head-on intersection collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Are flashing green traffic lights used in Washington, and where nearby do they warn of pedestrians?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Cross-border drivers heading north into British Columbia see pedestrian-activated flashing greens that never appear on Washington roads.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: How do you obey a red-and-green ramp meter when entering a Washington freeway?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Spacing cars one green cycle at a time smooths mainline freeway merging and prevents entrance bottlenecks.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What message category belongs to red, orange, yellow, white, green, blue, and brown road signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Spotting background color from blocks away tells you whether a sign bans, warns, regulates, guides, or points to services and parks.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: Which three vulnerable road-user zones do fluorescent yellow-green signs highlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: High-visibility neon pigment cuts through rain and dusk right where kids, walkers, and cyclists cross.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How do orange, standard yellow, and fluorescent yellow-green warning signs split up hazards?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Separating temporary roadwork from permanent curve warnings and active school crossings sharpens your scan instantly.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: What distinguishes white, green, blue, and brown signs along Washington highways?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: White demands legal compliance while green steers routes, blue locates gas or hospitals, and brown flags parks.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Where do you halt at a stop sign, and how does a yield sign adjust your approach?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Stop signs demand zero wheel motion at the line or corner, whereas yield signs let you merge smoothly if clear.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What mandatory action separates every stop sign from a yield sign?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Treating an octagon like a yield sign is a classic rolling-stop citation even on an empty street.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: Why can an officer ticket you for driving too fast even when your speedometer reads below the posted limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Ice, fog, and slick rain shrink safe stopping grip well below clear-day maximum numbers.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What does a posted minimum speed limit sign require, and why does it exist?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Crawling below a highway's posted floor turns your car into a rolling chicane for fast-approaching traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How do posted maximum and minimum speed limits frame safe highway travel?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Maximums cap dry-weather speed while minimums prevent dangerously slow blockages in fast lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Which three violations do Washington's marked automated safety cameras capture, and who receives the ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Marked roadside cameras log license plates and mail infractions straight to the registered vehicle owner.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: How do yellow speed warning plaques differ from overhead digital variable speed limit signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Static yellow plaques suggest safe curve speeds, while electronic gantries lower legal limits and close blocked lanes ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: What universal rule does a red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol communicate?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Spotting that red slash over a left, right, or U-turn arrow cancels the maneuver instantly.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What does a Do Not Enter sign look like, and what urgent action does a Wrong Way sign demand?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Seeing Wrong Way means you are already facing oncoming headlights and must halt safely and turn around immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: How do Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs split up preventing head-on entries?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Do Not Enter guards the ramp mouth before you turn in, whereas Wrong Way catches drivers already traveling backward.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: Who may enter a shared center left-turn lane, and which two uses are strictly banned there?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Using a two-way turn chute as a passing or travel lane sets up head-on collisions with opposing turners.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Whom must every driver yield to inside a Washington highway work zone, and what happens to fines when crews are present?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Workers and flashing-yellow maintenance trucks operate steps from live traffic, triggering automatic doubled penalties.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: Which roadside stops and amenities do blue motorist service signs point toward?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Blue highway panels let travelers exit smoothly for medical care, charging plugs, or fatigue breaks.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What information do green destination boards provide, and what do route shield shapes and colors reveal?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Distinct shield outlines tell you at a glance whether you are following an interstate, federal, state, county, or city route.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Does the driver guide illustrate every road sign in Washington, and what is your legal responsibility?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Local city and county traffic signs bind drivers just as strictly as standard state highway plaques.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: What traffic flow setup does an added-lane warning sign announce for vehicles joining on the right?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Because the entering ramp continues as its own dedicated travel lane, neither stream needs to squeeze over immediately.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Besides roadside flares or warning signs, how do response vehicles mark an active emergency zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Any color of flashing emergency beacon ahead warns you that workers or stranded people are standing yards from live lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: What two options satisfy Washington law when you approach a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Giving a full buffer lane protects roadside crews best, and dropping at least ten below the limit covers you when boxed in.
sec11-card-sec11-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Change lanes or drop ten under

visual_sync.text_span: Change lanes or drop ten under

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What is the absolute maximum speed allowed through an emergency zone in Washington?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Even on a seventy-mile-per-hour interstate, dropping ten under is not enough because fifty is the hard legal cap.
sec11-card-sec11-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Never exceed fifty in emergency zones

visual_sync.text_span: Never exceed fifty in emergency zones

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Beyond police cars, fire engines, and ambulances, which five working rigs count as roadside response vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Drivers often forget sanitation, utility, and tow operators get the exact same Move Over protection as patrol cars.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Passing a flashing roadside response vehicle, must you both change lanes and slow ten under, or choose one?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Moving over a lane and slowing ten under are legal alternatives, provided your speed also stays at or below fifty.
sec11-card-sec11-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Move over or drop ten under

visual_sync.text_span: Move over or drop ten under

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How does the ten-under speed drop interact with the fifty-mile-per-hour ceiling inside an emergency zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: On a sixty-five highway, slowing only ten to fifty-five still breaks Washington's absolute fifty-mile-per-hour emergency ceiling.
sec11-card-sec11-R02.must_match_memory_hook: At least ten under, max fifty

visual_sync.text_span: At least ten under, max fifty

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Who bears responsibility for parking only in safe designated spots, and what curbside clue warns of limits?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Blaming missing signs never excuses a hazardous park job when curb paint or road geometry marks a restriction.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Which four pedestrian, cyclist, or traffic spaces forbid parking at all times?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Leaving a car in any of those four spaces blocks sightlines and forces walkers or riders into moving lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Within how many feet of a traffic light, stop sign, or yield sign is parking prohibited?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Tall SUVs and vans parked closer than thirty feet hide stop signs and red signals from approaching drivers.
sec11-card-sec11-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Stay thirty feet from control signs

visual_sync.text_span: Stay thirty feet from control signs

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: How many feet of clearance must you leave when parking near a driveway, alley, or private road?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Hugging right up to a driveway apron blocks turning radius and blinds drivers backing out into street traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What parking clearance applies across the street from a fire station's driveway?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Long hook-and-ladder rigs swing wide across the entire street width when rolling out of station bays.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How do Washington's no-parking distances compare across driveways, traffic signs, and opposite-side fire stations?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Stacking five, thirty, and seventy-five in ascending order keeps you from swapping sign and fire-house numbers.
sec11-card-sec11-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Five driveway, thirty sign, seventy-five fire

visual_sync.text_span: Five driveway, thirty sign, seventy-five fire

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Within how many feet of a pedestrian safety zone is parking illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Keeping twenty feet clear preserves sightlines around transit islands and raised pedestrian refuge areas.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Where is parking banned on railroad tracks and around a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Parked cars inside fifty feet block flashing crossbucks and hide approaching trains from crossing motorists.
sec11-card-sec11-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Off tracks, fifty feet from crossing

visual_sync.text_span: Off tracks, fifty feet from crossing

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: How many feet of open curb must you leave on each side of a fire hydrant?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Firefighters need fast, unobstructed hose-coupling access when seconds count at a structure fire.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Which hazards match Washington's fifteen-foot, twenty-foot, and fifty-foot no-parking buffers?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Pairing fifteen-hydrant, twenty-safety-zone, and fifty-railroad locks down the second trio of distance questions.
sec11-card-sec11-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Fifteen hydrant, twenty zone, fifty rail

visual_sync.text_span: Fifteen hydrant, twenty zone, fifty rail

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Which direction must a parked car face, and what is the maximum legal distance from the curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Parking nose-against-traffic forces a blind head-on pullout, and sticking past twelve inches clips passing lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What rules cover double-parking and parking in work zones, on bridges or tunnels, or along freeway shoulders?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Bridges, tunnels, and active construction zones have zero safe shoulder margin, and freeway stops belong strictly to emergencies.
sec11-card-sec11-F14.must_match_memory_hook: All banned; freeway shoulder emergency only

visual_sync.text_span: All banned; freeway shoulder emergency only

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: What parking rules do white painted curbs signal compared with yellow or red painted curbs?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: White curb paint permits brief passenger drop-offs, whereas yellow and red mark loading zones or no-parking limits.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How do the twelve-inch curb-distance rule and painted curb colors apply together when parking?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Tucking neatly within twelve inches never saves you from a ticket if yellow or red paint restricts that curb.
sec11-card-sec11-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Within twelve inches, obey curb paint

visual_sync.text_span: Within twelve inches, obey curb paint

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How often should you engage the parking brake, and where does it matter most?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Relying only on a transmission's Park pawl lets sloped gravity strain or snap the pin.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: How do you perform the Dutch Reach when exiting a parked car, and whom does it protect?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Reaching across your body with your right hand naturally pivots your shoulders to spot cyclists in the bike lane.
sec11-card-sec11-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Mirrors first, open with far hand

visual_sync.text_span: Mirrors first, open with far hand

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Under what age is it a crime to leave a child unattended in a parked car with the engine running?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: An unattended running vehicle risks accidental gear shifts, vehicle theft, or carbon-monoxide buildup with a minor aboard.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Even with the engine shut off, under what age is leaving a child alone in a parked car a crime?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Closed cabins overheat or freeze rapidly and leave young children vulnerable even when the ignition is off.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How does Washington's under-sixteen unattended-child law differ from its under-twelve unattended-child law?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Exam distractors flip those two ages constantly, so tie sixteen to running engines and twelve to any parked car.
sec11-card-sec11-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Under sixteen running, under twelve anytime

visual_sync.text_span: Under sixteen running, under twelve anytime

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Under what four cabin conditions does leaving an animal alone inside a vehicle become a crime?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Sunlit car interiors climb dozens of degrees within minutes, turning a quick errand into fatal heatstroke for a trapped pet.
sec11-card-sec11-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Heat, cold, bad air, no water

visual_sync.text_span: Heat, cold, bad air, no water

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: If an unattended child or endangered animal is locked inside and nobody nearby can open up, what authority do police have?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Officers can break glass or force locks to save a trapped child or pet without owing repair costs.
sec11-card-sec11-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Enter reasonably with zero damage liability

visual_sync.text_span: Enter reasonably with zero damage liability

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: What step-by-step sequence puts your car cleanly into an angled or perpendicular parking space?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Creeping in slowly while centering between painted stall lines leaves door room on both sides.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: When backing out of a perpendicular or angled stall, how far straight back should you reverse before turning the wheel?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Cranking the steering wheel too early swings your front fender sideways right into the parked car beside you.
sec11-card-sec11-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Clear neighbor's bumper, then turn sharply

visual_sync.text_span: Clear neighbor's bumper, then turn sharply

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: As you start backing into a parallel space, what alignment cue tells you to turn the wheel sharply into the spot?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Waiting until your front bumper matches the lead car's rear bumper keeps your nose from clipping its tail.
sec11-card-sec11-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Align front bumper with rear bumper

visual_sync.text_span: Align front bumper with rear bumper

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: How do you complete a parallel-parking maneuver after angling back toward the rear vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Tapping bumpers fails a road test, so halt clean and straighten forward within twelve inches of the curb.
sec11-card-sec11-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Stop short, pull forward within twelve

visual_sync.text_span: Stop short, pull forward within twelve

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Which two reference points anchor the start and the final parked position of parallel parking?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Examiners grade both bookends closely: smooth bumper clearance going in and twelve-inch curb alignment when parked.
sec11-card-sec11-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Match bumpers first, finish within twelve

visual_sync.text_span: Match bumpers first, finish within twelve

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: When pulling out of a parallel space, what clearance landmark tells you it is safe to merge into the travel lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Wait until your front door clears the ahead car's rear bumper so your right fender swings out cleanly.
sec11-card-sec11-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Signal, ease out past rear bumper

visual_sync.text_span: Signal, ease out past rear bumper

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: Parked facing uphill next to a tall curb, which way do you turn your wheels and how does the tire sit?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Letting the back edge of your front tire kiss the tall curb wedges the car instantly if brakes slip.
sec11-card-sec11-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Turn away; tire back touches curb

visual_sync.text_span: Turn away; tire back touches curb

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: Why can turning your front wheels toward the curb be safer when parked uphill beside a low or rounded curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: A rounded curb may be too shallow to catch a tire turned away, so aiming toward it guides any roll off traffic.
sec11-card-sec11-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Low curb: turn toward, roll off-road

visual_sync.text_span: Low curb: turn toward, roll off-road

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How does uphill wheel direction in Washington change between a tall curb and a low rounded curb?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Washington's guide highlights curb height specifically because a mountable rolled curb cannot reliably block backward tire roll.
sec11-card-sec11-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Tall turns away, low turns toward

visual_sync.text_span: Tall turns away, low turns toward

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Parked facing downhill alongside a curb, which way do your front wheels point?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Resting the front edge of your tire against the curb blocks gravity from rolling the nose into traffic.
sec11-card-sec11-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Downhill turns front tire into curb

visual_sync.text_span: Downhill turns front tire into curb

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: When parking on any hill that has no curb at all, which direction do you turn your wheels?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Pointing toward the shoulder ensures a runaway car rolls off the roadway rather than diagonally across lanes.
sec11-card-sec11-F30.must_match_memory_hook: No curb turns toward road edge

visual_sync.text_span: No curb turns toward road edge

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: What steering direction do downhill curb parking and no-curb hill parking have in common?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: In both setups turning right toward the roadside either wedges against concrete or steers clear of travel lanes.
sec11-card-sec11-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Both turn toward edge or curb

visual_sync.text_span: Both turn toward edge or curb

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: What rule governs the striped access aisle next to a disabled parking stall?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Wheelchair lifts and ramps unfold into those painted stripes, so blocking the aisle draws fines even with a placard.
sec11-card-sec11-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Keep striped access aisle completely clear

visual_sync.text_span: Keep striped access aisle completely clear

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: Who qualifies to apply for temporary or permanent disabled parking privileges, and who completes the form with them?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Medical certification from the applicant's physician verifies whether a temporary or permanent privilege fits.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: Under what condition is parking in an electric vehicle charging stall legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Even owning a battery-electric car does not let you use a charging bay as regular parking unplugged.
sec11-card-sec11-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Legal only while actively plugged in

visual_sync.text_span: Legal only while actively plugged in

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: Whose rules on weight, hitches, brakes, and licensing apply when towing a boat, camper, or trailer?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Overloading tongue weight or skipping required trailer brakes causes violent fishtailing and runaway downhill stops.
sec11-card-sec11-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Follow manufacturer, state, and federal rules

visual_sync.text_span: Follow manufacturer, state, and federal rules

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: What is Washington's law on unsecured cargo, and how must small and large items be fastened?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Flying mattresses, lumber, and yard debris cause severe highway swerve-and-strike crashes across Washington freeways.
sec11-card-sec11-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Unsecured loads illegal; strap cargo tight

visual_sync.text_span: Unsecured loads illegal; strap cargo tight

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: When is carrying a dog or other animal outside the cab—such as in a pickup bed—legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Unrestrained dogs slide or leap from open truck beds during routine braking or sharp highway swerves.
sec11-card-sec11-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Only inside protective harness or crate

visual_sync.text_span: Only inside protective harness or crate

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: What criminal offense applies when an animal is transported in a dangerous manner?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Washington's animal-cruelty statutes back safe-transport rules with criminal misdemeanor liability when an animal or bystander is put at risk.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: How does Washington's pickup-bed pet restraint rule pair with its dangerous-transport cruelty statute?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Even beyond open truck beds, any risky transport setup that endangers the animal or public triggers misdemeanor cruelty charges.
sec11-card-sec11-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Bed requires restraint; endangerment brings misdemeanor

visual_sync.text_span: Bed requires restraint; endangerment brings misdemeanor

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: Why does Washington treat driving with a loose pet—or a pet on your lap—as a legal problem?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: A startled dog jumping onto your steering arms or brake pedal pulls focus away from safe driving.
sec11-card-sec11-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Loose lap pets cause illegal distraction

visual_sync.text_span: Loose lap pets cause illegal distraction

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: Why do standard Washington traffic laws apply aboard Washington State Ferries?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Car decks and terminal lanes belong legally to the state highway system, so every road rule follows you aboard.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: What penalty applies to cutting into a ferry queue, and what must waiting drivers keep clear?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Jumping ahead in a ferry holding queue is a ticketable traffic offense, and stopped queues cannot block intersections or driveways.
sec11-card-sec11-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Line-cutting draws fines; keep driveways clear

visual_sync.text_span: Line-cutting draws fines; keep driveways clear

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: In which two Washington counties is ocean-beach driving legal, and what legal status does the sand hold there?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Because designated ocean beaches count as state highways in those two coastal counties, license, belt, and DUI laws apply on sand.
sec11-card-sec11-F41.must_match_memory_hook: Grays Harbor and Pacific state highways

visual_sync.text_span: Grays Harbor and Pacific state highways

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: What is the speed limit on legal Washington driving beaches, and who always holds right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: Families, clam diggers, and cyclists share open sand without painted lanes, so drivers yield right-of-way everywhere at twenty-five max.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Which county limit, speed cap, and right-of-way rule govern driving on Washington ocean beaches?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Combining Grays Harbor and Pacific counties with a twenty-five limit and universal pedestrian-cyclist priority covers every beach question.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What four qualities define managing risk behind the wheel, and how should safe habits develop?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Safe driving isn't luck—practicing deliberate, predictable control every trip turns protective habits into your everyday default.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Which five recurring factors show up most often in fatal motor-vehicle crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Eliminating speed, substances, phone glances, unfastened belts, and rookie overconfidence knocks out the biggest deadly crash drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: For which exact Washington age bracket are vehicle crashes among the leading causes of death and serious injury?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Drivers and riders from sixteen to twenty-five face outsized fatal and serious-injury crash risk while experience builds.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What does risk awareness mean in Washington driving, and what types of hazards does it include?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Catching other road users, shifting weather, and cabin distractions early lets you adjust smoothly before trouble develops.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: How should your eyes, side vision, and mirrors work together continuously while you drive?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Staring at one bumper creates tunnel blindness—keep scanning ahead while peripheral vision and mirrors cover sides and rear.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Right after spotting a hazard ahead that calls for a speed or lane change, where must you check?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Slamming brakes or swerving blindly invites a rear-end hit—knowing who follows behind dictates your safest move.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Can driving risk ever be eliminated completely, and how do you keep it low?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Sharing pavement always carries baseline danger, yet spotting hazards early and adapting speed or position shrinks crash odds.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: What is hazard perception, and what three mental and physical elements does it demand?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Reading trouble before it blooms requires steady attention, quick decision-making, and a measured response that fits traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How broadly does Washington define a road hazard, including everyday objects or your own planned turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Not every hazard looks dramatic—a curbside trash bin, speed sign, or your own driveway turn counts alongside darting kids.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Why do stationary items like a roadside trash can or upcoming driveway qualify as hazards just like a running child?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Washington tests the functional definition—anything requiring you to slow down or steer differently qualifies as a hazard.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: How can hazards appear on the road, and what must you decide when several show up together?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: When stationary and moving hazards stack up simultaneously, tackle whichever threat carries the most immediate danger first.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: How does hazard perception differ from handling multiple hazards at the same moment?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Spotting potential trouble early is step one, whereas sorting stacked threats by urgency decides which hazard gets handled first.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: What two advantages do you gain by easing off speed as you approach a hazard?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Easing your pace opens both physical room and extra seconds to read traffic and choose cleanly.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: What is situational awareness, and which nearby drivers may feel the biggest impact from your choices?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Tracking everything around you lets you anticipate trouble, remembering that drivers behind you absorb sudden braking hardest.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: In exact order, what are the five steps of Washington's hazard management routine?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: DMV loves testing sequence—always communicate your intent before your final check, smooth execution, and post-move evaluation.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What scanning and decision happen during step one—the plan step—of the hazard management routine?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Before touching your signal or wheel, sweep your surroundings and rearview mirror to judge whether the move makes sense.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: What braking limit, mirror glance, and blind-spot scan belong to the check step?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Adjust lane placement and speed early enough to avoid hard stops, glance at mirrors again, and check blind spots.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: In Washington's five-step routine, which step turns on your signal and which step rechecks mirrors and your shoulder?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Signaling early alerts nearby drivers during communicate, then mirror and shoulder checks verify nobody slipped into your gap.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: How hard should you ever need to brake if you set your speed and position properly during the check step?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Adjusting speed and spacing early avoids panic stops that catch following traffic off guard.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: How should you carry out the execute step, and what is the goal of the final evaluate step?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Smooth inputs prevent startling nearby road users, and quick self-review sharpens your judgment for future traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How do higher driving speeds affect seat-belt protection and your visual scanning window?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Faster travel strips effectiveness from your seat belt while compressing the seconds available to spot walkers and cyclists.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: What does speeding do to vehicle traction—especially in rain or snow—and to your stopping distance?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Excess speed erodes tire traction on slick pavement while stretching the pavement needed to bring the car to rest.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: What happens to crash impact force, injury severity, and fatality odds when vehicle speed rises?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Even modest speed jumps multiply collision energy, driving up severe trauma and fatal outcomes.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What road conditions does a posted speed limit assume, and what additional speed duty does Washington law impose?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Posted numbers apply only on clear, dry roads—Washington law requires slowing down whenever weather, road surface, or traffic worsens.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Under Washington law, how is driving slower than the posted limit treated compared with driving over it?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Easing under the posted number is completely lawful when conditions call for care, whereas exceeding it breaks the law.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Why is treating the posted speed sign as a goal speed illegal when roads, weather, or traffic deteriorate?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Driving the posted number in rain, fog, or heavy congestion violates Washington's safe-speed-for-conditions requirement.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Around which visibility, surface, crowd, bridge, lot, or neighborhood settings should you actively reduce speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Ease speed anywhere sightlines shrink or conflicts rise—blind hills, curves, wet roads, walkers, lots, heavy traffic, narrow bridges, and neighborhoods.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: Why do newer drivers face extra risk with vehicle spacing, and what two ways can space be measured?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Accurately reading buffers comes with seat time, and drivers gauge safe cushions using either physical lengths or seconds.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Measured in vehicle lengths, how much minimum gap does the Washington guide say to keep behind the vehicle ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Holding at least double your own car's length keeps you out of bumper-to-bumper pockets near other traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: What minimum car-length buffer does this Washington chapter state, alongside which two ways of judging space?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Keep both facts paired for the exam—at least two own-vehicle lengths ahead, judged by either physical distance or time.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: How big must your merge gap be in relation to surrounding drivers, and why is squeezing in risky?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Forcing your nose into a tight pocket leaves zero braking margin if the car ahead taps its brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when you enter an interstate, and how should you use the on-ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Through freeway traffic owns the lane, so signal early, check mirrors, and match speed along the entire on-ramp.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Between a driver already cruising on the interstate and a driver on the entrance ramp, who yields?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Never expect freeway traffic to brake or move over for you—entering traffic adjusts speed to fit an open gap.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: By what percentage does the Washington guide say zipper merging improves traffic flow, and how does it cut crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Taking predictable turns at one merge point boosts flow sixty percent and eliminates sudden early lane-change collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: When approaching a lane closure using a zipper merge, when should you move out of the closing lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Abandoning the ending lane half a mile early wastes road capacity—fill both lanes smoothly right up to the taper.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: Once traffic reaches the marked zipper-merge point, how should drivers alternate and manage speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Letting one ending-lane car slip ahead while matching the open lane's steady pace keeps everyone rolling.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: At a backed-up lane closure, why shouldn't drivers pile into the open lane early?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Using both lanes all the way to the marked merge zone keeps queues shorter and speeds even.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: What is eye-lead time, and how does it shift your driving from reacting late to acting early?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Sweeping far downroad, to the sides, and into mirrors reveals trouble early enough for calm choices instead of panic.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: How do you run the roadside marker exercise to sharpen your sense of driving time?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Guessing an object fifteen seconds downroad and counting till you pass it calibrates your real-world eye-lead gauge.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: How does the fifteen-second marker exercise relate to the broader habit of eye-lead time?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Counting fifteen seconds to a post trains distance-in-time estimation, supporting your wider habit of scanning far ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: How does giving yourself enough time in traffic improve decision-making under pressure?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: A healthy time cushion lets your brain weigh and rank options calmly rather than jerking the wheel impulsively.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: Who owns the right-of-way when you turn across oncoming traffic, and which side should your timing err on?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Approaching straight-through vehicles own the lane, and waiting for a generous gap beats gambling on a tight squeeze.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: How can you use a roadside marker to time oncoming traffic before turning across a lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Timing how many seconds one car takes from a fixed post to your intersection tells you whether the next gap fits.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Before turning left across oncoming lanes, who yields and what should you do whenever a gap feels borderline?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: T-bone left-turn crashes happen when drivers guess—if the gap looks uncertain, wait patiently for a bigger opening.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: How big must your gap be when turning into a moving stream of traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Pulling out requires enough space not just to clear the corner, but to accelerate smoothly without making approaching cars brake.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: What three habits define mindful driving in Washington?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Shutting off phones and entertainment keeps you present while ahead scanning and early weather or traffic adjustments keep you proactive.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: How many tasks can your brain genuinely focus on at once, and what must match your eye direction?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Daydreaming while staring through the windshield creates 'looked-but-failed-to-see' crashes—keep mental focus locked onto where your eyes point.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: How brief a distraction can trigger a devastating crash, and where must you clear distractions from?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Looking away for even two or three seconds covers blind football-field distances, so eliminate distractions both inside and outside.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Which three types of vision do drivers rely on, and what happens to all three as speed climbs?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Faster speeds blur side edges and narrow your visual cone, lowering the quality of central, fringe, and peripheral sight alike.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What specific part of the scene does central vision, fringe vision, and peripheral vision each handle?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Central sight reads crisp detail straight ahead, fringe frames unsharp borders, and peripheral catches motion out toward either side.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: How do focus sharpness and direction separate central, fringe, and peripheral vision?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Knowing which zone is sharp prevents relying on blurry peripheral sight alone—turn your central gaze briefly via mirrors when needed.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: What is your path of travel, and how do you redirect it when hazards, weather, or turns arise?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Whenever road conditions or turns alter your planned corridor, pick a fresh visual target area ahead to guide your wheels.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: What does line of sight cover, and how should your attention move between it and your path of travel?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Checking everything between your hood and your distant target while flicking back to your lane path spots blocks early.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: How does your path of travel differ from your line of sight?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Your path is the physical pavement corridor your tires travel, while line of sight is the visual stretch to your target.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Across which seven road, vehicle, and personal elements must you divide your attention while driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Fixating on one spot leaves blind gaps—rotate attention across path, sightline, target, hazards, cabin/exterior car, road users, and yourself.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How fast may you safely travel at night in relation to your headlights, and how far do beams normally reach?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Outrunning your four-hundred-foot headlight cone means any dark deer, stalled car, or walker appears too close to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: When should you use high-beam headlights at night, and when must you dim to regular beams?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: High beams maximize dark-road sightlines whenever nobody approaches, then dropping to low beams keeps oncoming drivers unblinded.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Which headlight setting must you use whenever you are following behind another vehicle at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Blasting high beams into a lead driver's mirrors blinds them from behind—stay on regular low beams when following.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: What change in traffic ahead tells you to switch out of high beams into regular headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Keep high beams working on empty stretches, then click down promptly as soon as oncoming headlights appear.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes if an approaching driver leaves blinding high beams on?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Staring into bright halogen or LED glare bleaches night vision—tracking the right road edge guides your lane safely.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Why do you shift your gaze toward the right side of the road instead of flashing back or staring at oncoming brights?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Looking right keeps your pupils from blinding out while still anchoring your car cleanly inside its lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: How should you scan ahead and to the sides beyond your bright headlight pool at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Peering past your beam cutoff spots unlit silhouettes early while side glances track pavement edges and roadside hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: During which two lighting conditions should you never wear sunglasses or colored lenses while driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Tinted and colored glasses block scarce contrast in darkness and gray overcast skies when eyes need every photon.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: How should you adjust your following distance after dark, especially on unfamiliar roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Depth perception and peripheral cues shrink in darkness, so add extra cushion behind lead taillights—especially somewhere unfamiliar.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Under which three curve or surface conditions must you slow down beforehand to maintain control?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Entering tight bends, icy patches, or wet puddles too fast overwhelms tire grip before steering can save you.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: When must you shed speed for a curve, and how do uphill versus downhill curves change pedal input?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Braking mid-corner upsets tire traction—shed speed on the straight approach, then feed light gas uphill or light brake downhill.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Where within your own lane should you position the car as you approach a curve, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Easing slightly toward the outer edge of your lane opens a longer view around the bend and widens your margin.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: How should you manage throttle, brakes, and steering while traveling through the middle of a curve?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Mid-curve weight shifts punish abrupt moves—skip sudden braking, hard gas, or jerky steering so tires hold balance.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: What two habits belong to exiting a curve as the road straightens out?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Roll onto the gas smoothly as wheels straighten and sweep mirrors before making any post-curve merge or lane change.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: What is the three-part speed pattern before entering, while inside, and when leaving a curve?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Nailing this rhythm—brake straight, hold even mid-corner, accelerate gently out—keeps all four tires planted.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: In curve physics, what is vehicle roll versus vehicle yaw, and how do you keep both balanced?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Matching entry speed with smooth steering keeps body tilt—roll—and side-to-side rotation—yaw—settled cleanly.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: Which way does inertia push your car in a curve, and why does jerking the wheel backfire?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Because momentum wants to keep traveling straight ahead, yanking the wheel fights tire grip instead of guiding weight smoothly.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: How does higher speed change kinetic energy and the time and space needed to turn or stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Extra kinetic energy demands bigger stopping and turning room, which is why shedding speed early preserves cornering traction.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: What physical force lets tires grip the pavement, and what weather conditions slash it in curves?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: All steering and braking run through four palm-sized tire patches whose friction plummets on wet, snowy, or icy bends.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How does the Washington guide distinguish inertia, kinetic energy, and friction?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Keep the physics trio crisp—inertia pulls straight, kinetic energy climbs with speed, and friction supplies tire-to-road grip.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: What speed adjustment is required whenever pavement turns slick, even if the posted sign allows faster travel?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Posted numbers assume dry grip, so slick rain, slush, or frost legally and practically calls for slower travel.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Why are the first few minutes of rain on a hot day extraordinarily slick?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Summer heat draws oil up out of asphalt pores, forming a greasy film with fresh rain until heavier downpours wash it off.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: After rain starts falling on hot pavement, when is skidding danger highest and why does it ease later?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: DMV tests this exact timing—slipperiness peaks in the opening minutes before continuing rain rinses surfaced oil away.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: Which two big adjustments do snowy roads require from every driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Packed snow stretches stopping distances dramatically, requiring both sharply reduced speed and a much wider following cushion.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: When must you mount snow tires or chains in Washington, and what winter hardware boosts grip?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Mountain passes post legal snow-tire and chain requirements, and winter chains or studded tires bite into packed snow and ice.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Which two road features freeze over first even when surrounding pavement stays bare and wet?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Cold air chills bridge decks from both top and bottom while tree-shaded stretches stay frozen without sunlight.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: Does ice get grippier or slicker as air temperatures warm from deep cold up toward freezing?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Classic physics surprise—ice warming near thirty-two degrees forms a microscopic water film on top that slashes traction.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: Where does surprise ice linger on clear days, and why does warming toward freezing worsen grip?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Expect surprise ice on shaded bends and overpasses, and remember near-freezing wet ice slides far worse than cold dry ice.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: What is black ice, and at what thermometer range must you stay on guard even when pavement looks dry?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Because black ice is transparent over dark asphalt, treat every road near or below freezing as potentially glazed.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: What causes tires to skid, what driving inputs trigger one on slick roads, and what is your best defense?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: High speed plus abrupt braking or sharp turns breaks tire traction on slick roads—preventing skids beats recovering.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: In what order do you use the pedals during a skid, and why shouldn't you stomp non-ABS brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Lift off the accelerator first before pressing or pumping brakes—stomping hard without antilock brakes locks wheels deeper into the slide.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: How does braking behavior in a skid differ between a car with antilock brakes and one without?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Antilock brakes prevent wheel lockup so steering keeps working, whereas jabbing non-ABS pedals hard worsens the slide.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: Which direction do you turn the steering wheel during a skid, and how long do you keep adjusting?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: Pointing the front wheels in the direction the car is moving—and smoothly correcting—lets rolling tread recapture grip.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.question_text: What happens beneath your tires during hydroplaning, and what is the number-one way to prevent it?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.teaching_text: When tires outrun their tread channels, a water wedge lifts rubber off asphalt—slowing down on wet pavement prevents lift-off.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.question_text: What four calm actions should you take with pedals, wheel, and eyes if your car starts hydroplaning?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.teaching_text: Ease off the gas, touch brakes gently if needed, hold the wheel straight without jerking, and look down your open lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How does your steering response in a dry-or-icy skid differ from your steering response while hydroplaning?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Skids need active steering corrections into the slide, whereas turned wheels during hydroplaning yank the car sideways once tires touch down.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Why does the Washington guide warn against hard braking while hydroplaning, especially without antilock brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Locking water-skimming wheels without ABS guarantees a spin when tires reconnect with pavement, so keep braking feather-light.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What number should you call immediately when witnessing road rage happening right now?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Violent road rage threatens lives in real time, warranting an immediate nine-one-one emergency call.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Which eight location, vehicle, weapon, and role details help dispatchers when you report aggressive driving to nine-one-one?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Giving road name, travel direction, vehicle colors, plate, weapons, actions, and victim-or-witness status guides troopers fast.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Which agency places cutting road rage and aggressive driving at the heart of its mission, and how do residents help?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Timely resident reports help Washington State Patrol troopers intercept dangerous drivers along problem corridors.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Does witnessing an aggressive driving act use a non-emergency line or the same number as live road rage?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Washington routes both active road-rage emergencies and witnessed aggressive driving straight through nine-one-one.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What defines an informed driving decision, and what three safety payoffs follow from making them?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Evaluating all surroundings first sharpens awareness, builds responsible habits, and cuts collision odds.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Which three personal foundations shape every choice you make behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Knowing rules, logging safe seat time, and recognizing age-related brain development all steer judgment.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Why are teen drivers biologically prone to misjudging risk, and what two temptations must safety beat?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Because prefrontal judgment circuits finish wiring in your twenties, resisting speed dares and loud friends saves lives.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What crash vulnerability and ability shifts come with aging — and does age alone make older drivers unsafe?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Frail bones raise crash injury severity for seniors, yet experience and self-regulation keep many driving safely.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Contrast the biological reason teen drivers need extra care with the reason older drivers do?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Teens battle an unfinished judgment center, whereas seniors adapt to changing physical and mental traits.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Walk through the three steps — inform, prepare, and final check — of the Washington guide's decision approach?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and signaling early lets you set lane position and speed before one last look commits.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: In Washington's three-step decision sequence, what two steps must already be done right before your final check?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Saving a last-second glance right before steering catches fast cars that entered after you signaled.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Which three qualities should describe every speed, lane, or direction change you make on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Telegraphing calm, gradual maneuvers prevents startling drivers sharing lanes around your car.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Which three adjustments solve most road hazards — and what communication rule keeps others safe meanwhile?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Slowing down, nudging lane position, or taking a safe turnout works cleanly when signals tell neighbors first.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What four words form the OODA acronym, and why is it described as a continuous loop?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Finishing one maneuver immediately creates a brand-new traffic picture that restarts observation.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Match Observe, Orient, Decide, and Act to the specific job each performs on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Spotting a brake light, judging gap risk, picking a slowdown, and braking smoothly turns theory into safety.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How does the Observe step differ from the Orient step inside the OODA loop?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Seeing a ball roll onto asphalt is Observe, while realizing a child may chase it is Orient.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Name the guide's four distraction groups and give real examples inside each one?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Phones and snacks sit inside, crashes sit outside, soreness is physical, and worry or daydreams are mental.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Classify fatigue and body aches versus daydreaming, worry, and strong emotions — and is a phone required?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Leaving your phone stowed never guarantees focus if exhaustion or heated worry hijacks your brain.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Which four lane, speed, sign, and following mistakes commonly give away a distracted driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Diverted eyes wander over lane stripes, swing speed erratically, blow stop signs or walkers, and crowd bumpers.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Which three habits prevent distraction, and what three mental or physical benefits do you gain?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Setting routes before rolling cuts stress and tiredness while sharpening reactions and choices.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How broadly does Washington define distracted driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Any task that steals attention from operating your vehicle safely counts, whether electronic or not.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: May experienced adult drivers hold a phone, tablet, or gaming device while driving in Washington — and what about hands-free?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Zero age or experience exemptions allow holding screens behind the wheel, leaving adult voice-activated use only.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: For full-license Washington drivers, what exact physical line separates illegal device use from permitted use?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Cradling a phone on speaker in your palm still breaks the holding ban even without pressing it to your ear.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What financial penalties apply to a Washington distracted-driving citation — especially if you offend again?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Getting caught holding a phone a second time doubles an already steep ticket fine.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Does Washington double distracted-driving fines on the very first ticket or on subsequent violations?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Watch exam wording closely — ticket one carries a heavy standard fine, while violation two and beyond double.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Which five habits — covering awareness, controls, predictability, judgment, and growth — mark a smart driver?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Combining crisp pedal-and-wheel control with clear signals and ongoing learning keeps every trip low-drama.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Which four types of human attention does the Washington guide identify?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Driving taps all four — shifting gaze, tracking mirrors and speed, locking onto hazards, and staying sharp on trips.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Match switching, divided, focused, and sustained attention to how your mind operates in each mode?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Knowing the difference explains why juggling texting and steering wrecks focused hazard response.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: Which five pre-drive and cabin steps protect your attention behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Clearing loose clutter, calming rowdy passengers or pets, sleeping well, and silencing phones keeps your mind sharp.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: How does the Washington guide distinguish 'searching' from 'scanning'?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Eye movement alone misses pillar and quarter-panel blind spots until your head, neck, and torso pivot too.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Which visual habit relies on your eyes alone, and which adds head, neck, and body movement?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: DMV questions flip these two definitions to test whether you remember scanning recruits your neck and shoulders.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: How should your visual ability to search and scan cap your driving speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Outrunning how fast your eyes and neck can check cross streets forces panic braking when surprises pop up.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: When scanning ahead, what clues near parked cars and beyond the lead vehicle help you avoid sudden swerves?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Spotting shoes or shadows under parked vans and brake lights three cars up buys smooth reaction time.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Which four intersection, crosswalk, roadside, and pre-turn checks make up effective side scanning?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Bushes and hedges hide approaching cyclists or joggers until a mirror-and-shoulder check clears your turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Before which five maneuvers or hills must you check behind for trailing vehicles and cyclists?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Turning right across a green bike lane without looking back hooks fast-moving cyclists straight into your door.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: Why should you check mirrors more frequently in dense traffic, and what three responses can protect you?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Catching a closing speeder early lets you change lanes, flash brake taps, or open space ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Which six safety, courtesy, conflict, and environmental habits define respectful driving in Washington?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Letting go of who caused a traffic mistake prevents conflict while protecting everyone's space and environment.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What do traffic advisories report, who issues them, and through which five channels do drivers receive them?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Checking overhead reader boards, radio, web, social feeds, or apps before leaving dodges crash closures.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: What two major hazards make Washington's littering fines so steep, and what must drivers and passengers do?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Loose cargo causes highway wrecks and tossed cigarette butts ignite dry brush wildfires.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: How do Washington state law and local ordinances split littering penalties, and whom can you ask locally?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Cities and counties can layer stricter dumping rules atop state minimums, verifiable through police, sheriffs, or clerks.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Does Washington state law cap maximum littering fines everywhere or establish only the minimum baseline?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Local county or city ordinances can enforce tougher anti-dumping rules beyond the state floor.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: What deadly gas builds up when a parked car idles — especially in a garage — and which four habits cut emissions?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Odorless carbon monoxide kills quickly inside garages, while shutting off, smooth driving, proper PSI, and carpooling cut pollution.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: Which model years fall under Washington's Clean Car Law, and what three transactions are blocked if a car fails?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Buying an out-of-state two-thousand-nine-or-newer vehicle that misses clean-air standards leaves you unable to register or sell it.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Pinpoint the exact model-year cutoff and three blocked actions under Washington's Clean Car Law?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Without clean-air compliance on two-thousand-nine-and-later models, registration, licensing, and resale all stop cold.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: Which four reflection questions help you review a drive afterward — and what happens without regular self-review?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Asking if anything surprised you or others keeps sharp driving habits from quietly slipping over time.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which three attitudes form the foundation for safely sharing Washington roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Staying patient and alert around vulnerable road users protects both pedestrians and everyone inside your own vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Where do pedestrians and crossing bicyclists hold legal right-of-way on Washington streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Assuming walkers lose priority just because white paint is absent at a corner is a classic Washington exam trap.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: How far across must a pedestrian get before you roll forward, and how does a cane, wheelchair, or service animal change that?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Rolling inches behind someone's heels leaves zero safety buffer, and mobility-aid users keep the entire roadway until curbside.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How does Washington's waiting rule contrast an unaided walker with someone using a wheelchair, cane, or guide dog?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing that standard walkers clear one adjacent lane while mobility-aid crossings freeze traffic curb to curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Which groups on foot deserve heightened scanning because distraction, youth, or unfamiliarity hides your approach?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Expecting distracted walkers or playing kids to spot your bumper first sets up preventable neighborhood strikes.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Why must you keep your hand off the horn near a pedestrian accompanied by a service animal?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Blasting a horn can disorient a working guide dog or startle its handler right inside live traffic lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: How do the yellow and red warning lights on a school bus mirror standard intersection signals?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Flashing amber warns that the bus is preparing to load kids, giving you time to brake smoothly before red locks in.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What happens to the ticket amount if you illegally pass a stopped school bus flashing red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Washington doubles school-bus passing penalties because children step directly across traffic around halted buses.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Which same-direction lanes must halt for a school bus's red flashers, and what rule applies to center turn lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Sneaking past a stopped school bus down a shared center turn chute is strictly unlawful and endangers crossing students.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Why is a shared center turn lane never a legal shortcut past a stopped school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Turn chutes carry the exact same stop duty as through lanes whenever red bus flashers activate.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Which three equipment cues on a stopped school bus must finish resetting before you roll again?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Wait until the front bumper crossing gate retracts completely and keep scanning for late-running kids near the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Who must stop on a two-lane road when a school bus activates red flashers and its stop paddle?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Students routinely cross oncoming asphalt from the front of the bus on undivided two-lane roads.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: On a multilane road, who always stops for a school bus, and what two features appear in the guide's oncoming exception?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Following traffic never gets an exemption regardless of road width, while the handbook cites three-plus lanes and physical dividers for oncoming cars.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: On a two-lane street, when can oncoming traffic resume moving past a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers on two-lane streets follow the exact same full-stop and three-part reset checklist as trailing traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Does Washington's multilane school-bus exception ever excuse drivers traveling behind the bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Even on wide boulevards, every lane moving the same direction as the bus must stop behind the extended paddle.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What is your legal duty when a same-direction transit bus flashes its turn signal to pull back from the curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Letting public buses merge cleanly keeps schedules moving and avoids tight sideswipes beside bus bays.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Why shouldn't you linger alongside a semi-truck or bus, and what mirror check reveals whether the driver sees you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Cruising beside a trailer hides your car inside huge no-zones where a single lane shift can crush you.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How many feet does a loaded truck with good brakes need to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Darting closely ahead of a heavy rig steals over a football field of braking distance that physics cannot replace.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What visual cue in your inside mirror confirms enough gap to merge ahead of a truck, and how should you drive next?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Waiting for the entire cab grille in your rearview mirror preserves cushion, and maintaining speed prevents forcing forty tons onto brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Why is spotting a single truck headlight in your mirror too soon to merge back, and what mistake must you avoid afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Pulling in with one lamp showing clips the truck's front safety zone, and lifting off the gas right afterward invites a rear-end hit.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: How much lane space can big trucks need for corners or roundabouts, and why must you hold back mid-turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Squeezing alongside a wide-swinging trailer causes classic pinch crashes as rear axles track across adjacent lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How should you position yourself around hazmat-placarded rigs, and what should you anticipate on long steep hills?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Keeping buffer around diamond hazmat placards lowers exposure risk, while scanning right lanes on grades catches climbing trucks early.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: What visibility hazard makes tailgating an active snowplow dangerous?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Plow blades hurl dense whiteout spray across lanes, blinding anyone tucked closely behind the spreader.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: How do motorcycle legal rights compare with cars, and why do riders need extra following cushion—especially in rain?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Slim profiles vanish in glare and two wheels stop or slip differently on slick pavement, demanding generous space.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: May you squeeze alongside a motorcycle inside the same lane if the rider is positioned near one edge?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Riders shift across their full lane to dodge wind blasts and potholes, so crowding beside them steals vital escape room.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: What look sequence protects motorcycles before a right turn, and what judgment error hits oncoming riders?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Narrow headlights fool human depth perception into thinking an approaching bike is farther and slower than reality.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Which everyday street flaws can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or swerve inside the lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Minor bumps that four tires shrug off can deflect a motorcycle wheel, requiring sudden lateral shifts within the lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: Which two quirks of motorcycle deceleration and turn indicators can mislead nearby drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Rolling off the throttle slows a bike rapidly without lighting the tail lamp, and forgotten blinkers can falsely promise a turn.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Why shouldn't you trust a motorcycle's brake lamp or blinking turn signal by itself?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Watching real closing gaps and rider head turns beats trusting signals that may stay dark or fail to self-cancel.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: What legal rights and duties apply to bicyclists on the road, and why are crashes so severe for them?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: With zero steel cage around them and a narrow silhouette, cyclists suffer catastrophic harm when drivers fail to spot them.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: Can a bicyclist claim the entire travel lane, and what minimum gap applies when trailing behind one?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Squeezing inside the same lane is unlawful, and keeping at least three feet behind gives riders room if a chain slips.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: What legal status does a bicyclist riding through a marked or unmarked crosswalk hold?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Whether painted stripes exist or not, a cyclist rolling across a crosswalk receives full pedestrian priority.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: How does a bicyclist's legal role shift between riding down a street lane and rolling across a crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Knowing both hats keeps you giving full-lane respect mid-block and full pedestrian yields at every corner.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: How do you legally overtake a bicyclist on multilane versus two-lane roads, and when must you hold back?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Never overtake a rider right before turning right across their bow, and measure three feet from your side mirror tip.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: From what part of your vehicle is the three-foot bike-passing buffer measured, and how do two-lane passes work?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Side mirrors jut out past door panels, and on two-lane streets you wait until the opposing lane is completely empty.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: How are Washington bike lanes typically painted, and which two maneuvers let a motorist cross or enter one?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Cruising or queueing down a painted bike lane is illegal; cars enter briefly only for corner turns or curbside parking.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: Where are motorists permitted to cross railroad tracks, and what do flashing red crossing lights signify?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Active red flashers announce a closing train, requiring every vehicle to stay completely clear of the gate perimeter.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: Why do trains always hold right-of-way, and what if crossing bells and lights trigger while the gate stays up?
