sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Locomotives need up to a mile to halt, and mechanical gate lag never excuses driving past active bells or flashers.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Within what distance window from the nearest rail must you stop when train warnings, flaggers, horns, or signs apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Stopping inside fifteen feet overhangs locomotive clearance, while stopping past fifty feet blocks upstream sightlines and traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: What are the exact near and far boundaries of Washington's railroad stop zone, and do raised gates excuse active flashers?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: DMV tests pair the fifteen-to-fifty-foot window with the trap scenario of flashing bells under a raised gate arm.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: What immediate step comes first if your vehicle stalls across railroad tracks, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Trains approach rapidly from either direction on any parallel rail, leaving zero seconds to troubleshoot a dead engine.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Which phone number do you call first for an obstruction on or near railroad tracks, and when do you dial nine-one-one?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Calling the railroad's direct Emergency Notification System line with the posted crossing ID halts trains faster than indirect relay.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Between nine-one-one and the blue-and-white Emergency Notification System plaque, which takes priority at a rail hazard?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Exam questions check that nine-one-one serves as your fallback only when no blue crossing plaque is posted.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: How much space must you keep from a light-rail train, and what rule governs stopping on its rails?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Quiet electric trains run along shared city streets where stopping across embedded tracks invites an instant collision.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: Which vehicles carry a rear orange triangle, and what three habits make passing one safe?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Wide farm implements move slowly and swing unexpectedly into field drives, rewarding calm full-lane passes with wide clearance.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: How must you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle with lights or sirens, and how do you merge back afterward?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Signaling back into traffic in your exact original queue order prevents multi-car cutoffs once the ambulance clears.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Once a police car, fire engine, or ambulance clears your stopped line, how do drivers pull back onto the road?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Jumping ahead of stopped cars ahead of you causes sideswipes right as every pulled-over driver restarts.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: Where should you bring a disabled vehicle to a stop, and which two blind road spots must you avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Stopping just over a crest or around a blind bend hides your car until approaching traffic is on top of you.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Which vehicle lights go on during a roadside breakdown, and how far behind your car should flares sit?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Running hazard flashers plus headlights and placing flares two hundred to three hundred feet back gives fast traffic stopping room.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: If you have no flares during a breakdown, how do you warn approaching drivers and signal distress on the car?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Stand clear of lanes to wave cars past, then pop the hood or tie white fabric visibly outside.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How does warning approaching traffic with flares compare with warning them when you carry none?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Flares guard two hundred to three hundred feet up-road, whereas without them you stand safely off-pavement waving traffic past.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: What four actions with wheel and pedals keep you safe right after a sudden tire blowout?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Slamming brakes after a blowout spins the car—grip firmly straight ahead, ease off gas, coast down, and touch brakes gently.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: Why shouldn't you brake firmly right after a tire blows out the way you might for an obstacle?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Hard braking on a shredded tire yanks steering toward the blown corner, so let momentum bleed off before gentle braking.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: What three things should you do if a flat tire strands you somewhere unsafe to jack up the car?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Changing a tire inches from highway traffic is deadly—flip on hazard flashers, remain inside the cabin, and phone roadside help.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: How do steering and braking behave if your engine dies mid-drive, and how should you pull off?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Power assist drops out so the wheel feels heavy—steer firmly and press the brake steadily without pumping away vacuum boost.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Once you safely coast to the shoulder with a stalled engine, what sequence follows?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Attempt restarting once safely parked; if the engine stays dead, pop the hood, switch on hazards, and call assistance.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Which backup lights can help you see and be seen if your headlights suddenly go dark, and what must you do?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Flipping on hazard flashers, turn signals, or fog lights throws enough emergency glow to guide you immediately off the roadway.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What four steps in order handle a stuck accelerator when the car keeps speeding up?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Never duck down to pry the pedal—keep eyes forward, slap neutral to disconnect engine power, pull off, then kill ignition.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: How does handling a dead engine while moving differ from handling a stuck accelerator?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: A stalled engine already lost power and needs firm steering with steady braking, whereas a stuck throttle needs neutral immediately.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Which three built-in communication tools alert other road users when a risk appears?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Flashing or signaling with lights, tapping the horn, or extending clear hand signals warns surrounding traffic before conflicts turn close.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Who bears responsibility for preventing collisions, and can skillful driving guarantee you never experience one?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Every driver owes active crash-avoidance—even evasive steering—yet another person's mistake can still involve a careful driver.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Which three everyday failures does the Washington guide name as the usual causes of collisions?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Almost every avoidable wreck traces back to going too fast, tailgating too close, or losing situational awareness.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: What is the number-one rule after any collision, and when must nine-one-one and police be notified?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Driving off turns a wreck into hit-and-run, and any injury or death requires calling nine-one-one immediately so police respond.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: Where should drivable crashed vehicles and occupants relocate right after a collision?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Leaving drivable cars and people standing inside active lanes invites a secondary high-speed pileup.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: Which three steps protect a crash scene from oncoming traffic and fuel fires?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Leaking gas vapors ignite easily—set warning devices, switch off wrecked ignitions, and ban smoking near the wreckage.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: What must you try first if you bump an unattended parked car, and what must a written note include?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Look for the owner first; if unfound, secure a visible note listing the date, time, and your contact information.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: After striking a parked vehicle, can you simply drop a note and leave without looking for the owner?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Washington puts finding the owner first—leaving a date-time-contact note applies only after you try and cannot find them.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Which five pieces of driver and policy info should crash-involved drivers swap, plus what visual step?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Collect names, contact info, driver-license numbers, insurer names, and policy numbers—and snap clear photos of vehicle damage.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Within how many days must you file a Washington state collision report if no police officer files one?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Whenever law enforcement doesn't submit a crash report, Washington gives drivers a strict four-day window to file.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: Does every Washington crash require you to submit your own four-day collision form, or only certain crashes?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: If an investigating officer files the state report, that covers it; otherwise you owe the form within four days.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: Under what sole circumstance should you move an injured crash victim before medics arrive?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Shifting someone with hidden neck or spine trauma risks paralysis, so move victims solely out of fire or active danger.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: When helping a crash victim who isn't walking and talking, which two vital checks come first in order?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Quiet victims need help most—verify an open airway and breathing first before moving on to control bleeding.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: In what three-step escalation order does the Washington guide list bleeding control?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Start right away with direct hand pressure, apply a bandage or dressing next, and reserve a tourniquet as step three.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: Putting vital checks and wound care together, what comes first and how do the three bleeding steps progress?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Keep the trauma ladder locked—breathing beats bleeding, and bleeding climbs from hand pressure to dressing to tourniquet.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: May you give water to an injured crash victim, and how do you help prevent shock?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Internal injuries or emergency surgery make even plain water dangerous—skip all drinks and drape a warm coat or blanket.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What location anchors and scene summary should you give the nine-one-one dispatcher first?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Giving exact mile markers or landmarks dispatches crews immediately while brief vehicle, damage, and injury counts size the response.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: When may you hang up on nine-one-one after reporting a crash, and what extra details might dispatchers ask?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Staying on the line until sirens pull up lets you relay plate numbers, vehicle types, or new hazards live.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: What must you do if a downed power line rests on your car, and how should you treat every wire?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Stepping out bridges lethal voltage to ground—shut off the engine, phone nine-one-one, and assume every wire is live.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: What should you do immediately if your tires roll onto a downed power line?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Pulling forward or backing off can snag live wires and electrocute you—halt immediately and wait inside for utility clearance.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: How far back should bystanders stay when power lines touch a vehicle or a transformer box is hit?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: High voltage radiates outward through surrounding soil and asphalt, making everything within thirty-five feet a shock zone.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: If your car catches fire while touching a live wire, how must you exit and move away?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Never touch metal and ground together—leap clear with arms tucked, land both feet together, and shuffle thirty-five feet out.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Which two downed-power-line safety rules in Washington both use the exact distance of thirty-five feet?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Thirty-five feet governs both sides of energized ground—how far helpers stay back and how far you shuffle after jumping.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: When a power line touches or lies under your car, what is the sole emergency that justifies leaving the cabin?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Rubber tires and cabin walls shelter you until crews cut power—only active fire justifies the feet-together jump-and-shuffle.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: What three rules apply as you drive past someone else's collision scene?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Slowing to gawk backs up traffic and triggers rear-end hits—keep responder lanes clear, follow traffic directors, and watch ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: Which nine medical, lighting, warmth, power, tire, and warning supplies belong in a well-stocked car emergency kit?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Packing first aid, flashlight, blanket, water, jumper cables, tools, backup charger, spare with jack, and triangles covers roadside surprises.
sec14-card-sec14-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Aid, light, warmth, cables, spare, flares

visual_sync.text_span: Aid, light, warmth, cables, spare, flares

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: Why should your glovebox kit include important phone numbers written on paper?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Most people memorize zero numbers today—if your smartphone dies, a paper list lets you call family from a borrowed phone.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: How do law enforcement officers signal a traffic stop, and how should you pull over?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Flashing lights, siren, or both command a stop—click your right turn signal and pull onto the right shoulder when safe.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Once stopped on the shoulder for police, what should you shut off and where must you stay?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Shutting off the motor and silencing music lets everyone hear clearly, and stepping out uninvited creates an immediate safety alarm.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: What three visibility and hand habits apply during a nighttime police stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Switching on cabin dome lights, resting hands visibly on the wheel, and following officer directions keeps night stops calm.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: When the officer walks up, what should you do with the window, any weapon onboard, and reaching for papers?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Roll down the officer-side window, state immediately if a weapon is inside, and wait for permission before reaching anywhere.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: Which three documents do officers normally request, and what should you say before retrieving them?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Announcing that your wallet or registration sits in the console or glovebox prevents sudden reaches from looking threatening.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: During a police stop, should you grab your license and registration while the officer walks up or wait?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Rummaging into pockets or gloveboxes before the officer arrives looks suspicious—keep hands on the wheel until told to reach.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.question_text: If you disagree with a traffic stop or officer conduct, what shouldn't you do roadside, and what two proper channels exist?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.teaching_text: Roadside arguments never erase a citation—ask polite questions only, then contest tickets in court or request an agency supervisor.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: Which channel handles contesting an officer's ticket decision versus reporting concerns about an officer's conduct?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Keep the two remedies distinct—judges weigh contested citations in court, while the police agency's supervisor reviews conduct.

sec14-card-sec14-F38.question_text: Does signing a Washington traffic citation admit guilt, and what can happen if you refuse to sign?
sec14-card-sec14-F38.teaching_text: Your signature merely promises you will respond to the notice—refusing to sign can turn a roadside ticket into an arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F39.question_text: Within how many days must you follow the response instructions on the back of a Washington traffic ticket?
sec14-card-sec14-F39.teaching_text: Ignoring a citation past fifteen days lets Washington suspend your driving privilege before you ever argue the ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: What two legal truths apply to signing a Washington traffic ticket at the roadside and responding afterward?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Sign at the stop without admitting fault to avoid arrest, then answer the ticket within fifteen days to protect your license.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Which two exams must every new Washington driver pass, and what distinct skill does each measure?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Knowing road rules on paper comes first, followed by proving behind-the-wheel control in live traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Which driving exam must be passed first, and how long does that passing result give you to finish the second?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Waiting past twenty-four months after passing your written check expires the score and requires retesting.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: Is a new driver ever allowed to take the skills exam before passing the knowledge exam?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Examiners never put an untested applicant onto public streets before written rule mastery is verified.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Who is allowed inside the car during your driving skills exam—including the two narrow exceptions?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Parents, friends, and instructors wait outside so only you, the examiner, and approved accommodations ride along.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which registration, insurance, lighting, and restraint items must your skills-exam vehicle pass before pulling out?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Showing up with a burned-out brake bulb, missing insurance proof, or jammed belt cancels your drive before leaving the lot.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: At which two types of locations can you schedule and take your Washington driving exams?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Applicants can test through certified driver training schools or book a state office slot inside License Express.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Which two instructional components make up approved Washington driver training for students under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Pairing theory classes with live instructor coaching builds safer habits through private schools or participating districts.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Why do driving schools offer adult traffic safety courses for untrained drivers over eighteen, newcomers, or rusty drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Skipping structured training at eighteen-plus leaves dangerous blind spots that adult beginner or refresher courses close.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: What family session must teen driver training schools offer, and what practice-hour split does it cover?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Walking parents through the forty-daylight and ten-nighttime practice requirement aligns home coaching with instructor lessons.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Should calendar age alone decide when someone stops driving, or which three personal factors matter instead?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Monitoring eyesight, physical mobility, and reaction speed lets drivers adapt habits or switch transit based on capability.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What two ways can you replace a Washington license that is lost, stolen, destroyed, or worn unreadable?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: You can request a replacement card at dol dot wa dot gov or pick up an in-person duplicate.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Where on your Washington license is the expiration date printed, and how early before expiry may you renew?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Checking the bottom line early lets you renew through License Express or an office up to twelve months ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: What extra cost can hit a late renewal, and after how many expired years must you retake both exams?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Letting a Washington license sit expired eight years or longer resets you back to written and road testing.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: How does Washington's one-year early-renewal rule contrast with its eight-year long-expired rule?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Keep one and eight distinct—one year ahead opens renewal while eight years past expiry triggers both exams.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: How soon and where must you report a new residential address—and how does changing your legal name differ?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Addresses update online inside License Express within ten days, whereas legal name updates require appearing at an office.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Which personal update belongs in License Express within ten days, and which forces an in-person office trip?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Identity documents for a name change must be verified at a counter rather than typed into License Express.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: Where can Washingtonians register to vote, and which teen age group can pre-register during a license or ID visit?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds signing up during licensing roll onto active voter rolls automatically at eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Which two optional federal or research registrations appear on a Washington license or ID application?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Applicants can complete federal Selective Service signup and opt into Washington's twin research registry on one form.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: Which intermediate, minor-possession, ticket-accumulation, and suspended-driving violations can strip your driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Even off-road alcohol, drug, or firearm possession by a minor—or driving while already suspended—revokes privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Which five fleeing, impairment, reckless, work-zone, or unpaid-ticket offenses cost driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Ignoring a court citation suspends your license just like reckless racing or endangering roadside emergency crews.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: Which major crash crimes, insurance failure, or medical-skill check can also end your driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Felony vehicle crimes, fleeing crashes, driving uninsured, or failing a DOL competency check all pull your card.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: Until what age can an alcohol, drug, or firearm offense delay a minor's Washington driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Committing a substance or firearm offense as a young teen blocks getting licensed at sixteen.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: What three non-traffic minor offenses can hold back your driver license eligibility until age seventeen?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: You do not even need to be behind a steering wheel for those three youth offenses to delay licensing to seventeen.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: What testing, fee, and under-eighteen family requirements apply when reinstating a lost license?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Prior passing scores do not carry over after losing your license—expect full retesting plus extra reissue fees.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: Under RCW forty-six point six one five hundred two, what conduct on the road is illegal?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Washington's primary DUI section covers impairment from prescription meds, cannabis, or street drugs alongside alcohol.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: How can someone sitting inside a parked car still violate Washington's DUI law under RCW forty-six point six one five hundred three?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Sitting impaired where you could start the engine or move the car triggers physical-control DUI even without rolling.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How do Washington's five-hundred-two and five-hundred-three sections work together to cover impaired motorists?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Pair both scenarios together—one statute bans impaired driving while its companion bans impaired physical control.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: What chemical-testing agreement does every person automatically accept simply by driving on Washington roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Whenever an officer has grounds to suspect alcohol or drug impairment, Implied Consent already covers testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: What blood alcohol concentration triggers DUI at age twenty-one and up versus under age twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Even a single drink can push an under-twenty-one driver past zero point zero two into full DUI penalties.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: What active blood THC level triggers DUI for drivers twenty-one and older compared with drivers under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Washington enforces strict zero-tolerance cannabis rules under twenty-one—any measurable active THC above zero counts.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: Which exact BAC and active-THC pairs appear in the Washington guide's limits table for adults versus minors?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Seeing all four numbers side by side keeps alcohol percentages separate from blood THC nanogram counts.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Which age group faces the tighter Washington alcohol ceiling—zero point zero eight or zero point zero two?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: At zero point zero two percent, drivers under twenty-one hit DUI at one-quarter of the adult threshold.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Why is Washington's under-twenty-one cannabis driving threshold described as a zero-tolerance standard?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Adults have a five-nanogram ceiling, whereas drivers under twenty-one have zero legal allowance for active THC.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: For how long can refusing an officer's impairment check cost your driving privilege?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Whichever runs longer—up to two full years or your twenty-first birthday—applies based on prior violations.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: When someone under twenty-one refuses an impairment check, does the day-count or birthday cutoff end first or last?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Watch the word longer—refusal keeps privileges suspended across the full ninety-to-seven-thirty span or until twenty-one.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: How long do alcohol and drug driving offenses remain on your Washington record, and what fallout follows a DUI arrest?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Unlike minor speeding tickets, Washington never erases substance offenses—expect criminal fines, jail risk, and surging insurance.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: Alongside a ninety-day-to-four-year suspension, which four monitoring, insurance, and treatment conditions can follow a DUI conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Returning to the road after DUI requires breath-interlock hardware, financial-responsibility filings, probation, and treatment compliance.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: What suspension window applies to driving privileges after a Washington DUI conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Notice conviction suspensions stretch all the way to four years—even longer than the seven-hundred-thirty-day refusal cap.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: What three licensing steps can DOL require before restoring privileges after a DUI conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: After serving a DUI suspension, you still face a fresh application, both driving exams, and reissue charges.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: Which three actions involving alcohol or cannabis inside a vehicle violate Washington's open container law?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Pouring drinks or stashing cannabis into unlabeled water bottles still triggers an open-container infraction for cabin occupants.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: Where is the only legal place to transport previously opened alcohol or cannabis—and what cabin spots are barred?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Gloveboxes, center consoles, and back seats within arm's reach all violate Washington's open-container rule.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Does stashing a recorked bottle or opened cannabis pouch in a closed cabin compartment satisfy Washington law?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Only an isolated trunk or exterior pickup bed keeps opened alcohol or cannabis legal on the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Beyond standard cross streets, which everyday junctions and entrances legally count as intersections in Washington?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Driveways, shopping-plaza aprons, roundabouts, and neighborhood calming circles all trigger full intersection scanning duties.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Does an intersection lose its legal crosswalk status when no white stripes are painted across the asphalt?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Pedestrians stepping between unpainted residential corners hold the exact same legal right-of-way as downtown zebra crossings.
sec09-card-sec09-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Every corner counts, painted or bare

visual_sync.text_span: Every corner counts, painted or bare

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which stops, yields, multi-way glances, and mirror-plus-shoulder checks precede entering a Washington intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Looking once misses fast-closing cyclists and motorcycles tucked behind door pillars or mirrors.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: How should you handle a cross street when parked cars or hedges block your sightline at the stop line?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Easing your nose out gradually opens your sightline while giving cross-street drivers an early visual warning.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: In what exact order do stopping at the line and creeping forward happen at a sight-blocked corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Rolling past the white bar without halting first fails the road test even when bushes hide cross traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What far-side space check must pass before you pull into an intersection or start a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Entering behind backed-up traffic leaves your car stranded sideways across cross-street lanes and crosswalks when signals flip.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Around which seven busy community and commercial spots must your intersection scan widen with extra care?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Playgrounds, parks, schoolyards, work zones, and retail entrances pour unpredictable walkers and cars into corners.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What job do right-of-way rules perform at junctions, and what does the law mean by yielding?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Nobody owns right-of-way automatically; statutes assign who gives up first move so paths never collide.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Who moves first at a four-way stop, and how does Washington break a simultaneous arrival tie?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: When two bumpers halt together, the driver positioned on the left lets the vehicle on the right go first.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Does yielding to the right govern every four-way stop sequence or only simultaneous arrivals?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Waving or grabbing turns out of arrival order confuses everyone; the right-hand rule settles near ties.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: At a four-way stop, which opposing movements outrank a driver preparing to turn left?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Cutting left across an opposing car heading straight or turning right creates an immediate intersection conflict.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Between a driver continuing straight and a driver turning at a two-way stop, who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Turning vehicles crossing or merging from a two-way stop must wait for straight-moving priority traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do turning yield duties compare between a four-way stop and a two-way stop?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Keeping straight traffic first in mind prevents cutting across opposing lanes at either stop setup.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Into which lane must every Washington left or right turn finish, and when can you shift lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Swinging wide into outer lanes mid-turn sideswipes opposing turners who expect you to hold your tightest lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What lane discipline is required throughout an intersection equipped with multiple side-by-side turn lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Drifting across dotted guide marks mid-corner pinches the car turning right alongside your fender.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: How far ahead must you signal before turning across oncoming lanes, and what must be clear first?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Signaling at least a hundred feet back alerts trailing drivers while you verify an open gap and clear crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: What minimum signal distance and finishing-lane rule pair together on turns across oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Road-test examiners grade both the hundred-foot advance blinker and landing cleanly inside the closest lane before shifting.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Why must you check behind you and yield to approaching bicyclists before turning?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Misjudging a cyclist's momentum leads to right-hook crashes when a car turns across their path.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: When are U-turns legal in Washington, and which two terrain features always rule one out?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Blind curves and hill crests hide fast-closing traffic, making a slow turnaround mid-roadway lethal.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Even without a No U-Turn sign posted, why do curves and approaching hilltops forbid turning around?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Washington's permissive default requires unobstructed visibility in every direction before swinging across lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What defines a cross intersection, and how can traffic be controlled there?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Whether signals, signs, or paint govern those four approaches, standard priority rules keep cross paths orderly.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How is a T-intersection laid out, and which road holds right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Drivers on the terminating stem face a stop or yield sign and wait for continuous cross-road traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Who holds priority where a minor road angles into a major highway at a Y-intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Minor-branch drivers typically face a stop sign and must wait for a clean gap along the main highway.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: What shared priority principle links T-intersections and Y-intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: In both three-leg layouts, continuous main-line traffic flows first while the terminating or minor approach yields.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at a marked mid-block crosswalk even when no stop sign stands beside it?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Painted mid-block stripes bind approaching drivers to stop without needing an octagon sign at the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How do cars circulate around a traffic calming circle, how are approaches signed, and which rules govern priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Residential calming circles may post stops, yields, or zero signs at all, relying on standard intersection priority.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What unusual path might fire engines, buses, or delivery trucks need inside a small neighborhood calming circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Tight residential islands are sized for sedans, forcing long wheelbases to swing left in front of the island.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Which two traits set a neighborhood calming circle apart from a full highway roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Expect unsigned approaches using everyday right-of-way rules and give long trucks room to swing left around the island.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: How does entry and travel direction work at a roundabout, and which road users is it built to handle?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Unlike tiny neighborhood circles, modern roundabouts engineer geometry for cars, semis, buses, cyclists, and walkers together.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Why must you hang well back from semi-trucks inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Long trailers climb the raised inner apron and sweep across both circular lanes simultaneously.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which two ways may a bicyclist navigate a roundabout, and where should a lane-riding cyclist position?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Taking the center of the circular lane keeps a riding cyclist visible and stops cars from squeezing past mid-curve.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: For what low speed range are Washington roundabouts engineered?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Shedding speed down into that gentle window makes entry gaps wider and prevents tire scrub around the island.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: When do you select your roundabout lane, and how do you handle lane changes once circling?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Reading the upstream lane-choice sign early eliminates mid-circle weaving across exit paths.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Walk through the crosswalk, look, yield, and steering sequence for entering and exiting a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Checking crosswalks on both entry and exit while yielding to left-side circling traffic covers every conflict point.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Which direction do you yield before entering a roundabout, and what lane rule governs you inside?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Circulating cars approach from your left, and staying locked in your chosen lane prevents exit cutoffs.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What should you do if an ambulance or fire truck approaches while you are already inside a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Stopping inside the curved single-lane ring traps the emergency rig behind your bumper.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Why must you continue out of a roundabout before pulling over for flashing emergency lights?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Just like any standard intersection, clearing the box first leaves wide room for emergency apparatus to pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: How does a diverging diamond interchange reroute traffic, and what safety benefit does that create?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Temporarily crossing lanes to the opposite side eliminates left-turn oncoming conflicts onto freeway ramps.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: How do signals and paint guide you through a diverging diamond, including freeway left turns and exiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Following lane markings keeps the crossover intuitive, giving you unopposed left-ramp entry before crossing back right.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Why doesn't a left turn onto a freeway ramp inside a diverging diamond require stopping for oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Because you already shifted to the left side at the entry signal, no opposing lane blocks the ramp mouth.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: What defines an uncontrolled intersection, where do they usually appear, and do right-of-way laws still apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Residential streets without stop or yield posts still enforce strict statutory priority at every corner.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: In which four situations must you yield when approaching an unsigned, uncontrolled Washington intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Yielding to cars inside the box, state highways, paved streets, and oncoming straight traffic covers every unsigned conflict.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: At an uncontrolled intersection, who yields when a secondary or gravel road meets a state highway or paved street?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Higher-tier state routes and paved surfaces always outrank minor or gravel approaches when signs are absent.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: What five traffic jobs do painted pavement lines, arrows, words, and symbols handle?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Roadway paint carries the exact same legal force as upright metal signs even when no signpost stands nearby.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which two boundaries does a solid white edge line mark along the roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Keeping that crisp white stripe to your right prevents shoulder drop-offs and keeps cars out of bicycle space.
sec10-card-sec10-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Marks road edge and bike lane

visual_sync.text_span: Marks road edge and bike lane

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Where must you position your vehicle when driving along an unmarked roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Cresting hills or rounding blind rural curves near the center invites head-on collisions when no centerline splits lanes.
sec10-card-sec10-F03.must_match_memory_hook: No paint means keep far right

visual_sync.text_span: No paint means keep far right

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in the traffic directions they separate?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Glancing at the stripe color on your left instantly tells you whether neighboring cars are oncoming or traveling with you.
sec10-card-sec10-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Yellow splits opposite, white splits same

visual_sync.text_span: Yellow splits opposite, white splits same

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How can you tell from lane and center stripes whether a street carries one-way or two-way traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Confusing white lane dividers for a centerline can trick drivers into turning the wrong way onto one-way streets.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What warning do shorter, closer-spaced dashed white lines give about your current lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Spotting tighter white dashes early gives you time to signal and merge smoothly instead of braking at the taper.
sec10-card-sec10-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Short white dashes mean lane ending

visual_sync.text_span: Short white dashes mean lane ending

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: How do standard dashed white lines differ in meaning from shorter dashed white lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Standard dashes mark continuing lanes you may cross optionally, whereas short dashes mean your lane is running out.
sec10-card-sec10-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Standard allows changes, short warns merge

visual_sync.text_span: Standard allows changes, short warns merge

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: What three forms can a roadway median take, and is driving on or across one ever legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Painted eighteen-inch yellow median islands prohibit U-turns and shortcut crossings just as strictly as raised concrete barriers.
sec10-card-sec10-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Open, concrete, or painted; never cross

visual_sync.text_span: Open, concrete, or painted; never cross

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: When are you allowed to cross a dashed white line separating two lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Dashed paint permits changing lanes, though you still owe mirrors, signals, and a blind-spot head check first.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What does a single solid white line between same-direction lanes instruct you to do?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Solid white lines discourage weaving near intersections, tunnels, and ramps unless an unusual hazard forces you out.
sec10-card-sec10-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Single solid white means stay put

visual_sync.text_span: Single solid white means stay put

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What rule applies wherever double solid white lines separate two lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Treat parallel solid white stripes like an invisible concrete wall separating express lanes or hazardous merge zones.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How does lane-changing permission step down across dashed, single solid, and double solid white lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Test makers contrast single solid against double solid constantly, so separate discouraged lane changes from flat-out illegal crossings.
sec10-card-sec10-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Dashed change, single stay, double illegal

visual_sync.text_span: Dashed change, single stay, double illegal

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: What passing maneuver does a single dashed yellow centerline permit on a two-lane road?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Sight distance must stay completely clear of approaching traffic, hills, and curves before borrowing the opposing lane.
sec10-card-sec10-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Pass in oncoming lane when safe

visual_sync.text_span: Pass in oncoming lane when safe

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What two things can a single solid yellow line mark, and may you cross it to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: On divided highways solid yellow marks the left edge, and on two-way roads it locks out passing.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What passing rule applies when double solid yellow lines run down the middle of a roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Both directions face restricted sightlines or heavy turn conflict where crossing center risks a head-on crash.
sec10-card-sec10-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Neither direction may cross to pass

visual_sync.text_span: Neither direction may cross to pass

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: When a solid yellow stripe and a dashed yellow stripe sit side by side, how do you know who can pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Cresting a hill opens sight distance for one direction while the opposing climb stays blind, so check your closest stripe.
sec10-card-sec10-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Dashed your side passes, solid waits

visual_sync.text_span: Dashed your side passes, solid waits

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: How does a dashed yellow centerline contrast with single or double solid yellow lines for passing?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Whenever unbroken yellow paint borders your lane, overtaking slower traffic in the opposing lane is off-limits.
sec10-card-sec10-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Dashed yellow allows, solid yellow bans

visual_sync.text_span: Dashed yellow allows, solid yellow bans

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Along a mixed solid-and-dashed yellow centerline, which stripe governs your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Ignoring your own solid stripe just because the far side has dashes puts you into a blind oncoming zone.
sec10-card-sec10-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Obey the stripe touching your lane

visual_sync.text_span: Obey the stripe touching your lane

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Once you pull into a marked intersection turn lane, what are you legally required to do?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Darting straight back into through traffic from a turn bay sideswipes drivers who expect you to turn.
sec10-card-sec10-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Enter turn lane, complete the turn

visual_sync.text_span: Enter turn lane, complete the turn

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Are you allowed to cross the solid exterior yellow stripe to enter a center lane painted with left-turn arrows?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Shared two-way left-turn lanes wrap solid yellow outside and dashed yellow inside specifically for turning entries.
sec10-card-sec10-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Yes, cross into center turn lane

visual_sync.text_span: Yes, cross into center turn lane

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: How does the rule against crossing solid yellow to pass interact with entering an arrow-marked center turn lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Know the difference on exam day: overtaking cars across solid yellow is illegal, whereas pulling into a turn lane is legal.
sec10-card-sec10-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Bans passing, allows center turn entry

visual_sync.text_span: Bans passing, allows center turn entry

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Which maneuvers are legal inside a shared two-way center lane, and what oncoming hazard exists there?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Drivers traveling the opposite direction share that exact same middle lane, so watch head-on before pulling in.
sec10-card-sec10-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Left turns and legal U-turns only

visual_sync.text_span: Left turns and legal U-turns only

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What passing rule and maximum travel distance apply inside a shared center turn lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Cruising down a center turn lane like a bonus travel lane invites head-on crashes with opposing left-turners.
sec10-card-sec10-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Never pass; three hundred feet max

visual_sync.text_span: Never pass; three hundred feet max

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Why must you keep your stay inside a shared center lane brief and never use it to overtake traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Keeping every entry short and strictly for turning prevents two oncoming cars from meeting bumper-to-bumper in the middle.
sec10-card-sec10-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Turn only, stay under three-hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: Turn only, stay under three-hundred feet

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Which vehicles are HOV lanes built for, and what symbol and stripe set them apart?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Spotting the painted white diamond early keeps solo drivers from wandering across the solid white divider into a steep fine.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: What rider count is needed to enter an HOV lane, and which two-wheeled vehicle qualifies automatically?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Occupancy minimums change between two-plus and three-plus depending on corridor signs, while motorcycles always qualify.
sec10-card-sec10-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Meet posted rider count, or motorcycle

visual_sync.text_span: Meet posted rider count, or motorcycle

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What makes a roadway lane a reserved lane, and what is a common transit example?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Driving or stopping in a bus-only transit lane delays whole coachloads of commuters and earns an immediate citation.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which four vehicle types ride free in express toll and HOT lanes, and how can a solo car driver use them?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: High-occupancy toll lanes blend carpool perks with paid solo access to keep freeway traffic flowing.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What account does the Washington driver guide recommend for paying state tolls automatically at the lowest rate?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Pay-by-mail bills charge higher rates than an active Good To Go account across Washington's toll bridges and express lanes.
sec10-card-sec10-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Good To Go saves money automatically

visual_sync.text_span: Good To Go saves money automatically

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Inside an express toll or high-occupancy toll lane, which drivers actually pay the toll?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Qualifying carpools, vanpools, buses, and motorcycles ride toll-free while solo motorists buy into the spare capacity.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Why do reversible lanes flip traffic direction, and when do they typically open?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Borrowing center capacity inbound each morning and outbound each evening moves rush-hour peaks without widening highways.
sec10-card-sec10-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Flips direction for commutes or events

visual_sync.text_span: Flips direction for commutes or events

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What pavement stripes typically border a reversible lane, and what must you check before entering?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Entering a double-dashed lane without reading overhead lane-control displays can put you nose-to-nose with rush-hour traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Above a reversible lane, what do a green arrow, a red X, and a steady yellow X each command?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: A steady yellow X warns that opposing traffic is about to get the lane, so merge out promptly and safely.
sec10-card-sec10-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Green go, red blocked, yellow vacate

visual_sync.text_span: Green go, red blocked, yellow vacate

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Between double-dashed pavement paint and overhead lane signals, which one tells you whether a reversible lane is open right now?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Paint only shows which lane can reverse; overhead gantries control which direction owns that asphalt right now.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: How does a red X above a reversible lane differ in urgency from a steady yellow X?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Never enter under a red X because oncoming traffic already owns the lane, and vacate quickly under steady yellow.
sec10-card-sec10-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Red bars entry, yellow clears lane

visual_sync.text_span: Red bars entry, yellow clears lane

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: At a crosswalk, when does your legal duty to yield to a pedestrian begin?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Waiting until someone is already in front of your bumper is too late—yield as soon as they prepare to step off.
sec10-card-sec10-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Yield inside or stepping into crosswalk

visual_sync.text_span: Yield inside or stepping into crosswalk

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: What must you do when pedestrian-activated lights embedded in a crosswalk start flashing?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: In-pavement strobes alert drivers across multi-lane arterials where a stopped car in the next lane might hide a walker.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: Does an intersection still count legally as a crosswalk when no white crosswalk lines are painted?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Missing paint never erases pedestrian right-of-way at street corners, a classic trap on Washington knowledge exams.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: How are standard bike lanes and buffered bike lanes marked on the pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Recognizing two solid white lines filled with diagonal crosshatching helps you keep tires clear of extra cyclist buffer space.
sec10-card-sec10-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Solid white, bike symbol, crosshatched buffer

visual_sync.text_span: Solid white, bike symbol, crosshatched buffer

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: What part of the road does a crosshatched bike buffer belong to, and when is a car allowed to cross it?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Never drift or park in diagonal bike crosshatching—check mirrors and blind spots first, then cross only for a legal turn.
sec10-card-sec10-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Part of bike lane; turns only

visual_sync.text_span: Part of bike lane; turns only

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop when approaching a stop sign or red light with a painted stop line or crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Rolling past the thick white bar blocks wheelchair ramps and forces pedestrians out toward moving cross-traffic.
sec10-card-sec10-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Stop before stop line or crosswalk

visual_sync.text_span: Stop before stop line or crosswalk

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: How are fire lanes marked, where might cities paint them, and what two actions are banned there?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Even idling briefly with hazards flashing inside a red fire zone can block ladder trucks answering an alarm.
sec10-card-sec10-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Red markings; zero parking or stopping

visual_sync.text_span: Red markings; zero parking or stopping

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: What do diagonal yellow stripes painted across a patch of pavement tell drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Painted yellow gore zones channel traffic away from bridge piers, turn-pocket noses, and oncoming conflict points.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: Why is sitting at the wheel inside a fire lane still illegal, and where besides red curbs do fire lanes appear?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Drivers assume staying inside the cab excuses a quick pause, yet fire lanes ban both stopping and parking outright.
sec10-card-sec10-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Bans stopping too, including station fronts

visual_sync.text_span: Bans stopping too, including station fronts

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: What does a painted bicycle sharrow mean, and how much space must you leave when passing a cyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Without a separate bike lane, cyclists legally share the travel lane and need at least three feet of side clearance.
sec10-card-sec10-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Shared lane; pass with three feet

visual_sync.text_span: Shared lane; pass with three feet

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: What turn restriction and stopping rule apply when you approach an intersection painted with a bicycle box?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Waiting behind the white bar lets queued cyclists clear the intersection visibly on green without right-hook collisions.
sec10-card-sec10-F35.must_match_memory_hook: No right on red; cyclists first

visual_sync.text_span: No right on red; cyclists first

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: What is Washington's school-zone speed limit around schools and playgrounds, and how are these zones marked?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Dropping to twenty around schoolhouses and playgrounds cuts stopping distance dramatically where children dart into streets.
sec10-card-sec10-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty miles per hour near schools

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty miles per hour near schools

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Where does the twenty-mile-per-hour school limit apply, and how do you know which hours enforce it?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Read the supplemental plaques or beacons carefully because enforcement windows vary between arrival bells, beacons, and playground zones.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: Why must you still slow down through a highway work zone even when no road crew is visible?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Shifted concrete barriers, narrowed lanes, and milled pavement edges remain hazardous long after workers clock out.
sec10-card-sec10-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Always slow; narrow lanes, rough road

visual_sync.text_span: Always slow; narrow lanes, rough road

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: What hazards should you scan for entering a work zone, and how should your focus and following gap adjust?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes top work-zone wrecks when distracted tailgaters miss flaggers or slow dump trucks.
sec10-card-sec10-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Drop distractions, add gap, expect stops

visual_sync.text_span: Drop distractions, add gap, expect stops

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: Until which sign must you obey work-zone restrictions, and when do work zones demand extra caution?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: Speeding up as soon as cones thin out earns tickets before the End Road Work sign, and darkness hides lane shifts.
sec10-card-sec10-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Obey until End Road Work sign

visual_sync.text_span: Obey until End Road Work sign

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: What kind of roadside situation creates an emergency zone in Washington?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: Unlike scheduled construction, emergency zones appear without advance roadwork warnings wherever crashes or breakdowns strand people.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What personal identifier appears on every Washington license, permit, and ID card—and what letters often start it?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Every permit, ID, and driver credential ties back to your single lifetime Washington identifier.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: What is Washington's secure online DOL portal called, and why must every new driver open their own profile?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Trying to apply or renew under a parent's login fails because DOL ties services strictly to your individual account.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How many listed residency conditions—such as keeping a home, voting, filing taxes, or state aid—trigger Washington resident status?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Meeting just one trigger—not every item on the list—makes you a Washington resident subject to state licensing deadlines.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How many days does a licensed newcomer aged eighteen or older have to obtain a Washington driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Driving past thirty days of residency on your old state plastic risks an unlicensed-resident citation.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What must a new Washington resident pass if their out-of-state driver license has already expired?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Letting your former state's card lapse before transferring wipes out the exam waiver and requires written plus road testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Which Washington license does a licensed newcomer under eighteen apply for, and what two items must DOL verify?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Out-of-state teens cannot jump straight to unrestricted privileges without DOL-approved driver ed and six permit months.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: How does Washington's transfer path for a licensed adult newcomer differ from a licensed newcomer under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Adults swap into standard licenses within thirty days, whereas teens enter Washington's graduated intermediate phase.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Is REAL ID a single card or a federal law, what Washington credential satisfies it, and where do standard cards fail?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Standard state licenses cannot clear TSA airport checkpoints, international border gates, or secure federal facilities.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What personal DOL identifier must you obtain before submitting an instruction permit application?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Driver training schools and permit systems cannot link your enrollment or exam records until your WDL number exists.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: How young can you apply for an instruction permit when enrolled in driver training, and what is the pre-class window?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Enrolling in an approved school unlocks permit eligibility at fifteen within ten days of opening class.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: At what age may you test for a permit without taking driver training, and when can you take the skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Skipping driver ed saves tuition upfront yet locks you out of the road exam and license until your eighteenth birthday.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: How long does a Washington instruction permit stay valid compared with a passing knowledge exam score?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Renewing an expired one-year permit costs a fee, yet your passed written score still holds for a second year.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: By how much time does enrolling in a driver training course beat the non-course path for getting a permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Starting class opens the permit at fifteen flat instead of waiting half a year to test at fifteen and a half.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Between your instruction permit and your passing knowledge exam score, which expires in one year and which in two?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Mixing up those two clocks is a classic question trap—your written score outlives a single permit term.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which four core age, residency, permit-time, and schooling milestones unlock a first license at sixteen or seventeen?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Even turning sixteen on the calendar cannot skip holding the permit a full six months and finishing approved driver ed.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: What minimum classroom and behind-the-wheel hours must an out-of-state safety course meet to count in Washington?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Shorter online-only courses from other states get rejected if they fall below thirty class and six wheel hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: How many day and night practice hours must a teen log, beside whom, and who attests to them?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Every logged drive requires a supervisor licensed at least three years before a parent, guardian, or adult attests.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: What ticket, conviction, and substance record must a teen hold before applying for an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Catching a ticket on your permit resets your six-month countdown, and any alcohol or drug offense blocks licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which two facts does a parent or guardian certify when signing a teen's in-person authorization form?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Parental signature legally vouches for both the full fifty-hour log and half a year without infractions.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How many years of licensed driving experience must a teen's practice supervisor hold?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Watch the teen-versus-adult contrast—teen practice requires a three-year veteran whereas adult permit practice requires five.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How do Washington's daytime and nighttime teen practice minimums connect to the parent authorization total?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Forty daylight hours combined with ten after-dark hours produce the exact fifty-hour figure parents sign off.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Within what timeframe must a driver training school upload a teen's passing exam results into DOL's system?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Waiting up to twenty-four hours lets the school post your passing score before you finish licensing online.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: How long does the temporary license issued at a licensing office stay valid while your plastic card mails out?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Keep that forty-five-day temporary document with you on every drive until your permanent card reaches your mailbox.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: When a teen completes licensing online, what acts as the temporary license—and why does it fail as ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Your printed receipt proves driving privileges at a traffic stop, yet having no photo disqualifies it as identity proof.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does an in-person forty-five-day temporary license compare with an online license receipt?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Both let you drive legally right away, yet the photo-free online printout cannot verify your identity.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: What four licensing pathways exist for an adult first-time Washington applicant?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Adults eighteen-plus can transfer valid plastic, pass both exams directly, practice on a permit, or take driver training.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: When an adult eighteen or older practices on an instruction permit, how much experience must their supervising driver have?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Do not confuse teen and adult supervisors—adult permit holders need a five-year licensed rider beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: What happens if your DOL vision screening shows you need glasses or contact lenses to see clearly?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Driving without corrective lenses listed on your restriction code counts as driving outside your license terms.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: What extra credential must be added to your personal license before operating a motorcycle or commercial motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: A standard passenger license alone never covers two-wheel motorcycles or heavy commercial trucks.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Through which two restricted stages do sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds progress before earning an unrestricted license?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Graduated licensing builds supervised skill on a permit first and solo experience under intermediate limits second.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: During the first six months of an intermediate license, which passengers under age twenty are allowed in your car?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Peer distraction spikes teen crash risk sharpest right after solo driving begins, barring non-family friends under twenty.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: After your first six intermediate months—until age eighteen or one year—how many non-family passengers under twenty may ride?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Capping non-family teen riders at three bridges the second half of your first solo year safely.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: Between which early-morning hours is solo intermediate driving barred, who can accompany you, and when does curfew lift?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Fatigue and severe crashes peak between one and five a.m. unless a parent or twenty-five-plus driver rides along.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: May an intermediate license holder talk or text using hands-free dashboard Bluetooth—and what lone exception exists?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Even voice-dialed hands-free calls are illegal on an intermediate license unless you are reporting an emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How does the non-family under-twenty passenger cap change after the first six months on an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: First-half solo driving bans non-family peers under twenty completely before opening to three in phase two.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: In Washington's intermediate rules, how does the age-twenty cutoff differ in purpose from the age-twenty-five cutoff?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Keep both birthdays straight—twenty caps young passengers while twenty-five qualifies a late-night supervising rider.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: What happens after a first, second, and third violation or at-fault crash on an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Strike one freezes limits to eighteen, strike two suspends six months or to eighteen, and strike three suspends to eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does the suspension length on a second intermediate violation differ from a third violation?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Strike two ends after six months if eighteen is farther off, whereas strike three locks suspension straight to eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Under which two circumstances may an intermediate holder drive at any hour carrying passengers?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Farm-work trips allow unrestricted hours immediately, and completing one crash-free, ticket-free year lifts those limits too.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: Do you need to visit DOL for a brand-new card to drop intermediate restrictions when you turn eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Your existing card converts automatically on your eighteenth birthday, saving an extra trip until normal renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: To which age group does DOL mail an early warning letter after a first moving ticket—and why?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Statistical crash odds double right after a young adult's first moving violation between eighteen and twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: What driving does a Washington agricultural permit authorize under eighteen, and what is its minimum age?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Juvenile agricultural permits carry zero minimum age floor yet confine driving strictly to mapped farm-work zones.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Does holding an agricultural permit replace an instruction permit or waive practice hours for your first license?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Farm driving inside a local ag zone leaves every regular instruction-permit and fifty-hour license requirement intact.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: What is the key trade-off between a juvenile agricultural permit and a standard instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: You can drive farm routes earlier with no age minimum, yet none of it counts toward earning a standard license.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What single habit is the most effective way to protect yourself and cut fatal-injury risk in a crash?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Skipping or miswearing a belt forfeits your biggest defense against deadly crash ejection and cabin impact.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: Where must the shoulder strap and lap belt sit — and which three shoulder-belt placements are off-limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Tucking straps behind your back, under an arm, or over soft belly tissue causes severe internal crash injuries.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: Under Washington's occupant-restraint statutes, who inside a moving vehicle must be belted or in an approved child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Unbelted back-seat passengers become deadly human projectiles in a crash and trigger primary citations.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: Which six strap, knee, foot, and headrest checks confirm proper seating and seat-belt fit?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Aligning your headrest with your ears stops whiplash while flat straps on strong hip and shoulder bones absorb force.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Match the headrest, lap belt, and cross strap to the exact body landmark each must align with?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Test questions swap neck for mid-shoulder or stomach for upper thighs to catch careless readers.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Which safety standards and dual instructions govern child restraints — and who can inspect your setup?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Following both car and seat manuals plus visiting a certified technician eliminates loose harness and anchor mistakes.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: How long should a child remain in each restraint stage, and how must children under age two ride?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Rushing toddlers forward early exposes fragile infant necks when rear-facing shells cradle the whole spine.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What restraint requirement and facing options apply to children aged two through four?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Five-point harnesses spread crash forces across a toddler's frame whether kept rear-facing or turned forward.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: From age four onward, what height and age window typically require a car or booster seat until adult belts fit?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Adult belts ride dangerously across a child's neck and belly until height reaches four feet nine inches, usually ages eight to twelve.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: What must riders taller than four feet nine inches wear once old enough for an adult seat belt?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Graduating out of a booster never makes riding unrestrained legal — proper lap-and-shoulder fit takes over.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Why is riding unbelted dangerous around airbags, and which age group belongs strictly out of the front seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Explosive front airbags strike unbelted riders or children under thirteen with fatal force during deployment.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How does age four serve as the handoff between Washington's harnessed-seat stage and booster-seat stage?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Ages two to four stay harnessed, while age four opens the car-or-booster window until adult belts fit.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: Contrast what lets a child graduate from a booster seat against Washington's front-seat age rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Passing four feet nine inches ends booster duty, yet sitting up front still waits until age thirteen.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Where on the steering-wheel rim — and at which clock numbers — should your hands rest for maximum control?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Gripping the outer rim around nine and three maximizes leverage while keeping thumbs and wrists clear of airbags.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Which five driving situations call for hand-over-hand steering, and how do your arms execute and finish the turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Low-speed corners, blind junctions, parking stalls, and skid corrections need rapid wheel travel before straightening smoothly.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: When is one-hand steering appropriate, and for what single maneuver is twelve o'clock hand placement recommended?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Twisting your torso to look out the rear glass while backing makes top-dead-center twelve o'clock practical.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: What two safety advantages come from hand-to-hand push-pull steering never crossing arms or releasing the rim?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Keeping forearms off the center hub prevents broken bones if an airbag fires mid-turn.
