sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: Contrast the twelve o'clock one-hand grip with the hand positions used for normal forward driving?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Cruising forward with one hand perched at twelve puts your arm directly over the steering-wheel airbag.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Which four braking-pressure levels does the Washington guide name, and how do you master picking the right one?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Learning how your specific pedal responds across all four pressures prevents panicked lockups in traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Which two braking levels should handle everyday driving, what mental picture guides smooth stops, and why skip sudden stops?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Picturing an open cup of water on your lap keeps deceleration progressive so trailing drivers never slam into you.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: During an emergency stop, what control benefit does ABS give, what does it NOT shorten, and how does the car feel?

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: Where should a new driver practice firm or emergency braking to experience how ABS feels?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Feeling antilock pulsing first in an empty paved lot prevents startling your foot off the brake in real danger.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: Summarize the three test facts about Antilock Brake Systems during hard emergency stops?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Exam distractors claim ABS cuts braking feet in half, when its real job is preventing wheel lock so you can steer.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: How does the cup-of-water image guide acceleration across creeping traffic versus dodging a hazard?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Rolling smoothly off the brake tames stop-and-go traffic while decisive throttle stays ready when escaping danger.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: Why does even weight across all four tires matter, and which three upkeep habits preserve it?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Uneven tire inflation or bad wheel alignment overloads individual corners and ruins emergency handling.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: What is vehicle pitch, and which end takes the weight under acceleration versus hard braking?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Slamming brakes pitches nose weight onto front tires while unweighting rear tires enough to slide.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: What is vehicle roll — and during a left turn, onto which side does centrifugal force push the weight?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Fast cornering leans weight onto the outside tires rather than the inside direction you turned.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What is vehicle yaw, and what steering mistake triggers that rear-end zig-zag?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Whipping the wheel left and right swings the rear tires out of line behind the front axle into a fishtail.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Contrast the direction of weight transfer in vehicle pitch versus vehicle roll?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Gas and brake pedals rock weight nose-to-tail in pitch, while steering inputs lean weight sideways in roll.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Why is picking 'left side' wrong when asked where vehicle weight rolls during a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Momentum pushes car mass outward toward the right-side suspension whenever you bend left.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Which four parts of your car serve as visual reference points, and which four maneuvers do they guide?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Pairing fixed body parts with pavement lines lets you place invisible bumpers accurately when parking or stopping.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: How close is your front bumper to an intersection stop line when that painted line appears right under your side mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Using the underside of your side mirror stops you crisply behind crosswalks without creeping over paint.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: How far is your car from the lane edge when the center of your hood lines up visually with the lane stripe?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Matching hood center to the curb or fog line parks and positions your right tires cleanly within half a foot.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: Does the side-mirror stop-line reference measure side clearance or forward bumper distance — and what is the gap?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Even though it uses a side mirror, spotting the cross-line underneath gauges your front bumper's forward stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: What vehicles can vanish completely inside your blind zones, and who bears legal responsibility for checking them?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Saying you never saw a motorcycle or sedan in your mirror never excuses merging into an occupied blind zone.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: How do mirror adjustments pair with head checks — and what must your hands do while glancing over your shoulder?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Drivers unconsciously tug the steering wheel toward the shoulder they look over unless they brace hands straight.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: Which six forward, mirror, and shoulder directions belong in a complete regular scan?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Cycling smoothly across windshield, center mirror, both side mirrors, and shoulder checks prevents tunnel vision.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: How do you avoid riding in other drivers' blind zones, and what are the huge blind zones around buses, RVs, and trucks called?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Buses, motor homes, and commercial rigs carry massive blind areas where lingering cars vanish completely.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: What does it mean whenever you cannot see a large truck, bus, or RV's side mirrors?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Without a clear line of sight to the big rig's mirror glass, the commercial driver has zero view of your car.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: What two speed tweaks clear another vehicle's blind zone, and which three large vehicle types carry bigger no zones?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Either easing back or accelerating past puts your car back in sight, especially beside long buses, RVs, and semis.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: How often must you recheck and adjust your mirrors before driving — and use them once moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Seat posture or shared-car drivers shift mirror angles overnight, requiring a fresh check every single trip.
